item.title: Anthony Davis Trade Rumors: Raptors Among Three Teams To Look Out For If Extension Talks Fail
item.description: November 18, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Washington Wizards Anthony Davis (23) reacts after a call at a NBA game against the Toronto Raptors during the second half at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Sousa-Kevin Sousa-Imagn Images The Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis is in the final guaranteed season of his NBA contract and earns $58.5 million this season (with a $62.78 million player option for 2027-28). Amid uncertainty about his future after this season, rumors have emerged about three potential teams expected to lead the race to land his services if the contract extension talks fail or Anthony Davis’ representation grows impatient or frustrated . According to NBA insider Jake L. Fischer, the Toronto Raptors , the Golden State Warriors , and the Atlanta Hawks are the three teams expected to be interested in landing Anthony Davis , with a potential promise of a contract extension. “Sources say that the struggling Raptors are still poking around on the center market,” Fischer wrote in his recent Substack . “Last season, Toronto, at various points, expressed interest in the likes of Sacramento’s Domantas Sabonis and then-Maverick Anthony Davis.” “The Raptors, as a result, continue to be mentioned as a team to watch, along with Golden State and Atlanta after both the Warriors and Hawks were also previously linked with Davis, if Washington ever reaches the point of making the 33-year-old available.” “The Wizards, though, have not yet done so. Davis, in fact, just earned Eastern Conference Player of the Week honors for leading Washington to a much-needed run of three consecutive wins after a 4-11 start.” “My sense is that the Wizards have no imminent designs on moving Davis,” Fischer reported Tuesday. “Could that change between now and the Feb. 11 trade buzzer? Conceivably.” “But I’m also told that Davis, unlike New Orleans’ Dejounte Murray, is not pushing for relocation. Both players are represented by Klutch Sports, but it’s been conveyed to me that there are no current plans for Davis to request a trade.” Considering that the Warriors are expected to have significant salary cap space in the next free agency, their ability to offer Davis the contract extension he wants naturally puts them in the discussion of potential landing spots. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Sousa-Kevin Sousa-Imagn Images The Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis is in the final guaranteed season of his NBA contract and earns $58.5 million this season (with a $62.78 million player option for 2027-28). Amid uncertainty about his future after this season, rumors have emerged about three potential teams expected to lead the race to land his services if the contract extension talks fail or Anthony Davis’ representation grows impatient or frustrated . According to NBA insider Jake L. Fischer, the Toronto Raptors , the Golden State Warriors , and the Atlanta Hawks are the three teams expected to be interested in landing Anthony Davis , with a potential promise of a contract extension. “Sources say that the struggling Raptors are still poking around on the center market,” Fischer wrote in his recent Substack . “Last season, Toronto, at various points, expressed interest in the likes of Sacramento’s Domantas Sabonis and then-Maverick Anthony Davis.” “The Raptors, as a result, continue to be mentioned as a team to watch, along with Golden State and Atlanta after both the Warriors and Hawks were also previously linked with Davis, if Washington ever reaches the point of making the 33-year-old available.” “The Wizards, though, have not yet done so. Davis, in fact, just earned Eastern Conference Player of the Week honors for leading Washington to a much-needed run of three consecutive wins after a 4-11 start.” “My sense is that the Wizards have no imminent designs on moving Davis,” Fischer reported Tuesday. “Could that change between now and the Feb. 11 trade buzzer? Conceivably.” “But I’m also told that Davis, unlike New Orleans’ Dejounte Murray, is not pushing for relocation. Both players are represented by Klutch Sports, but it’s been conveyed to me that there are no current plans for Davis to request a trade.” Considering that the Warriors are expected to have significant salary cap space in the next free agency, their ability to offer Davis the contract extension he wants naturally puts them in the discussion of potential landing spots. Moreover, if the Wizards convey their trade Davis instead of waiting for the threat of him potentially becoming a free agent next summer, the Warriors could offer a lucrative trade package as well. If Davis becomes a free agent next summer, it could come down to which team is willing to offer the closest figure to the four-year, $275 million max contract he is eligible for. The 33-year-old star is currently averaging 25.6 points, 10.1 rebounds, and 2.0 assists while shooting 53.5% from the field and 35.0% from behind the three-point line. The issue with Davis staying with the Wizards in the short term to prove his value is that they may not have room to offer the extension he wants. But the Wizards have three key young players who will soon also be eligible for contract extensions over the next few years: Kyshawn George, Alex Sarr , and even AJ Dybantsa . So, after extending Trae Young to a $212 million max contract this summer, they have to keep their long-term future in mind. Hence, Davis and the Wizards may not agree on the terms of their extension. You could say Anthony Davis’ future is up in the air. Ultimately, the Warriors, Raptors, and Hawks could emerge as serious contenders for Davis if he and the Wizards fail to reach an extension agreement. Anthony Davis may still have an opportunity to establish his value in Washington, but the franchise’s long-term financial commitments could complicate negotiations. The coming months should clarify whether the 33-year-old remains part of the Wizards’ plans or begins preparing for another chapter elsewhere.

item.title: Valley Regional-Old Lyme clinches CIAC football berth with 3rd straight Principal's Cup win over H-K
item.description: Charlie Zelek hoists The Principal's Cup after Valley Regional/Lyme-Old Lyme defeated Haddam-Killingworth 47-28 in Higganum on Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026. (Bryant Carpenter/Hearst Connecticut Media) HIGGANUM - The postseason is coming to The Hill. Valley Regional/Lyme-Old Lyme clinched an unofficial CIAC Class S football playoff berth, and a home quarterfinal to boot, with a 47-28 victory Tuesday night over Haddam-Killingworth in the 47th edition of The Principal's Cup. The win marked Valley's third straight Cup win over its rival and sent the 7-3 Warriors back to the postseason for the first time since 2024. Haddam-Killingworth, which had to win to have any chance of qualifying, finished 6-4 and on the cusp of the playoffs for the fourth time in five years. Valley's quarterfinal opponent won't be known until the final regular season games are played on Thanksgiving. Of particular interest will be the Naugatuck Valley League game between Woodland and Seymour, both 6-3. On Tuesday night, the Warriors struck for touchdowns on each of their first two plays from scrimmage, both receivers screens from sophomore quarterback Max White to junior wide-out Charlie Zapatka. They scored on five consecutive possessions (save for taking a knee just before halftime) and built a 34-7 lead through three quarters. H-K, led by senior QB Tim Hickman, senior running back Kyle House and junior receiver Jonathan Slane, battled back to close to within two scores in a wild fourth quarter that saw the teams combine for five touchdowns and 34 points. H-K recovered an onside kick and cashed in with a touchdown. Within 34-21, the Cougars recovered a Valley fumble at their own 31 with 6:20 still on the clock, but their inability to capitalize on that turnover took crucial steam and time from the rally. Valley senior running back Patrick Lynch punched in his second 4-yard TD run of the night, and while Hickman answered with his third rushing score less than a minute remained by then and White drove a final dagger with a 44-yard post-onside burst. Valley now leads The Principal's Cup series 36-11. Valley won the last two editions on the last play of the game. There was Sam Zelek's 43-yard field goal for a 9-7 final in 2025 and Tommy Troy's 1-yard touchdown and for a 22-18 final in 2024. H-K's last win was 20-7 in 2023. This story will be updated. Player of the Game Max White. VRLOL's sophomore quarterback ran for two touchdowns and three threw to junior wide receiver Charlie Zapatka. 47TH PRINCIPAL'S CUP VRLOL 47, Haddam-Killingworth 28 VRLOL 19 7 8 13 - 47 H-K 7 0 0 21 - 28 H-Tim Hickman 8 run (Isaac Edwards kick) V-Charlie Zapatka 71 pass from Max White (run failed) V-Zapatka 53 pass from White (pass failed) V-Patrick Lynch 4 run (Sam Zelek kick) V-White 15 run (Zelek kick)his V-Zapatka 9 pass from White (Zelek kick) H-Hickman 16 run (Edwards kick) H-Kyle House 14 run (Edwards kick) A-Lynch 4 run (pass failed) H-Hickman 2 run (Edwards kick) V-White 44 run (Zelek kick) Records: VR

item.title: Celtics’ Paul George hits rare career milestone during blowout of Wizards
item.description: Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Celtics’ Paul George hits rare career milestone during blowout of Wizards appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coming off three consecutive disappointing defeats , the Boston Celtics showed some desperation in their return to action on Tuesday night against the Washington Wizards. Paul George , in particular, came to life after a few disappointing shooting performances in recent games. On Tuesday, George put up 28 points on the night on 11-of-19 shooting as the Celtics staved off a late charge from the Wizards to hold on for a 131-116 victory. He made six of his nine attempts from beyond the arc, and in so doing, he joined an uber-exclusive three-point shooting club. Having entered the night with 2,495 made three-pointers to his name, the Celtics veteran has now become the latest member of the 2,500 made threes club — becoming just the eighth player in NBA history to accomplish this feat, as per the official ClutchPoints account on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) With this three, Paul George has eclipsed 2,500 career three-pointers 🎯 He is just the 8th player in NBA History to achieve this milestone! pic.twitter.com/H5oCvuFcUk — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 25, 2026 George has been an elite marksman in the NBA for so long that it should not come as a surprise whatsoever that he’s rubbing elbows with some of the best shooters the league has ever seen. Included in the exclusive 2,500 made threes club are Stephen Curry, the all-time leader, James Harden, Ray Allen, Klay Thompson, Damian Lillard, LeBron James, and Reggie Miller. Now 36 years of age, George’s touch from beyond the arc remains as clean as ever. He entered play against the Wizards averaging 3.3 made triples through 14 games thus far this season while shooting the ball at a 40.7% clip from downtown. In a perfect marriage between system and skillset, George has found a new lease in life with the Celtics . His perimeter-oriented play style is perfect for a Boston team that loves hoisting up threes, and as long as George is in Beantown, he’ll be able to attempt and make threes to his heart’s content — improving his standing on the all-time threes leaderboard even further the deeper he gets into his career. item.title: Charley Hull, Atlanta Drive's WTGL debut included a lot of 'laughs'
item.description: PALM BEACH GARDENS — Atlanta Drive's Charley Hull stood in a bunker at SoFi Center holding a conversation with team owner Arthur Blank. Hull, whose team was making its WTGL debut about 30 minutes later, then grabbed her wedge, and as Blank was walking away, holed a 30-footer. Looking on and nodding with approval was Billy Horschel, a star on Atlanta's TGL team. For Hull — and Atlanta — that proved to be the highlight of the night. Even with Horschel and Justin Thomas, both part of Atlanta's championship winning team in TGL's inaugural season, lending support from the team owner's box, Boston Common Golf held on for an 8-3 victory Tuesday at SoFi Center. Boston Common had the advantage of playing its second WTGL match. "Obviously it wasn't the result that we wanted, but we had a great laugh," Hull said in perhaps the most upbeat post-game press conference ever held by a losing team. "It is a lot of fun. It's nice actually to be ... I know we're not on the golf course, but you're in the golf environment, and having a laugh." Hull, one of the marquee names playing in WTGL's first season, is considered the most popular active woman's golfer in Europe. The Englishwoman is No. 7 in the world, a three-time winner on the LPGA Tour and although she still is chasing her first major championship, she has five runner-ups in the tour's marquee events. She has played in eight Solheim Cups. Hull, 30, also this year checked off what she called a childhood dream, appearing in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit edition. All of which makes her a natural for a league that encourages the golfers to let loose and show their personality. Her 869,000 Instagram followers are more than any other golfer on WTGL's 25-woman roster. "I think it's cool that here in WTGL we can also show a little bit of fashion, just expose people that it's actually fun to play golf and dress pretty cool," said Hull's teammate, Nataliya Guseva. "I think that's kind of our goal as well with Charley out here with the Malbon (golf fashion) stuff." Every woman who has played in the league's first four matches agree that the league is part entertainment and fashion along with the competition. Guseva, the 23-year-old from Russia, had a rough night, drawing three penalties. She admitted to having nerves and said ... well, here is what she said. "It was super cool, but it was just kind of weird ... to show how nervous I am," she said. "But at the same time, every golfer kind of has nerves, and I think it's kind of cool to show that even professional golfers kind of s*** themselves during a tournament." item.content:encoded: PALM BEACH GARDENS — Atlanta Drive's Charley Hull stood in a bunker at SoFi Center holding a conversation with team owner Arthur Blank. Hull, whose team was making its WTGL debut about 30 minutes later, then grabbed her wedge, and as Blank was walking away, holed a 30-footer. Looking on and nodding with approval was Billy Horschel, a star on Atlanta's TGL team. For Hull — and Atlanta — that proved to be the highlight of the night. Even with Horschel and Justin Thomas, both part of Atlanta's championship winning team in TGL's inaugural season, lending support from the team owner's box, Boston Common Golf held on for an 8-3 victory Tuesday at SoFi Center. Boston Common had the advantage of playing its second WTGL match. "Obviously it wasn't the result that we wanted, but we had a great laugh," Hull said in perhaps the most upbeat post-game press conference ever held by a losing team. "It is a lot of fun. It's nice actually to be ... I know we're not on the golf course, but you're in the golf environment, and having a laugh." Hull, one of the marquee names playing in WTGL's first season, is considered the most popular active woman's golfer in Europe. The Englishwoman is No. 7 in the world, a three-time winner on the LPGA Tour and although she still is chasing her first major championship, she has five runner-ups in the tour's marquee events. All of which makes her a natural for a league that encourages the golfers to let loose and show their personality. Her 869,000 Instagram followers are more than any other golfer on WTGL's 25-woman roster. "I think it's cool that here in WTGL we can also show a little bit of fashion, just expose people that it's actually fun to play golf and dress pretty cool," said Hull's teammate, Nataliya Guseva. "I think that's kind of our goal as well with Charley out here with the Malbon (golf fashion) stuff." Every woman who has played in the league's first four matches agree that the league is part entertainment and fashion along with the competition. Guseva, the 23-year-old from Russia, had a rough night, drawing three penalties. She admitted to having nerves and said ... well, here is what she said. "It was super cool, but it was just kind of weird ... to show how nervous I am," she said. "But at the same time, every golfer kind of has nerves, and I think it's kind of cool to show that even professional golfers kind of s*** themselves during a tournament." "Yeah, I think it was great." Charley Hull's WTGL debut: A lot of laughs in Atlanta's loss From the entertainment side, Hull's debut was as expected. From the golf side she, too did not expect the nerves she felt, and was tripped up by the Hammer strategy. "If it was left up to me, I would have thrown it out straight away," she said. Hull helped Atlanta climb back to within a point (4-3) after winning her first singles match against Solheim Cup teammate Celine Boutier, but not without some drama. After hitting her second shot on the par 5 to within 19 feet, Hull knocked her putt 15 feet beyond the hole just to the edge of the green. "I was a bit embarrassing," she said. "I de-greened it nearly." That feeling was fleeting. Hull holed the 15-foot comebacker to defeat Boutier. Soon after the camera panned to Hull. She turned and winked and then told her teammates, "I winked at the camera." Hull could have been excused if she hit her tee shot off a decaying bridge on The Last Toll (which she did), or busted her driver into the rocks on Stinger (she did not). After a T23 in the CME Group Championship last weekend, the LPGA's season-ending event, Hull had a 10-hour shoot for TaylorMade on Monday and was up at 7 a.m. on match day to finish the shoot. "I am massively flagging," she said. "I was kind of golfed out by the time I came here." And there's more. Following the match, Hull was headed to Disney World with her family. "No, I'm not driving," Hull said. "I've got a driver, so I can snooze." Tom D'Angelo is a senior sports columnist and reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at tdangelo@pbpost.com . item.title: Raiders Urged to Add $120 Million WR as New Target for Fernando Mendoza
item.description: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk. Getty The Las Vegas Raiders could have a chance to give rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza a new target. The Raiders dived head-first into the Mendoza era after shipping quarterback Kirk Cousins back to the Minnesota Vikings. While Mendoza has shown promise through his first two games, the Raiders could have a chance to give even more help after the release of a proven NFL receiver who is looking for a fresh start. Raiders Named Landing Spot for Brandon Aiyuk The San Francisco 49ers just parted ways with Brandon Aiyuk, ending a long and drawn-out breakup that included a long injury absence and deteriorating relationship between the two sides. Aiyuk cleared waivers and hit free agency, where he could be a target for the Raiders. Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox named the Raiders among a handful of teams that could be interested in Aiyuk, noting that he could give some short-term help for the rookie Mendoza. “The Las Vegas Raiders probably won’t be pushing for the postseason over the final month of the season. They’ve lost seven of their last eight, and they’re rapidly falling behind in the AFC’s wild-card race,” Knox noted. “However, the rest of the season is all about developing quarterback and first overall pick Fernando Mendoza . Adding Aiyuk could help with that process and could potentially help Mendoza well beyond the current season.” Knox added that the Raiders have some weapons already, including tight end Brock Bowers and running back Ashton Jeanty, but could always use more help for the No. 1 overall pick. They could find it in Aiyuk, who once signed a $120 million contract with the 49ers, but could now come to them cheap. “Still, the Raiders could use help on the perimeter, and Aiyuk would be a terrific fit for their offense. Head coach Klint Kubiak was San Francisco’s passing game coordinator during Aiyuk’s career campaign in 2023,” Knox wrote. Raiders Might Face Tough Competition Knox suggested that several teams could be interested in Aiyuk, including a reunion with the Washington Commanders. Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, suggested that Aiyuk could lean on his existing relationships — which could help Kubiak and the Raiders. “That’s just my guess,” Rosenhaus said. “There’s a lot of that in the NFL; you see people connect the dots where they have history where there’s relationships. I don’t know where yet, but that’s just my assumption that something like that could happen — a former coach maybe a former player that he played with, somebody that knows him.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Raiders Urged to Add $120 Million WR as New Target for Fernando Mendoza appeared first on HEAVY .

I don’t know where yet, but that’s just my assumption that something like that could happen — a former coach maybe a former player that he played with, somebody that knows him.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Raiders Urged to Add $120 Million WR as New Target for Fernando Mendoza appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Wild Would Be ‘Interested in a Nanosecond’ in Sidney Crosby
item.description: Sidney Crosby Wild Getty The Minnesota Wild would be “interested in a nanosecond” if Pittsburgh Penguins captain Sidney Crosby were made available in a trade. The Wild just missed out on their top free-agent center target, Dylan Larkin, so the team may turn their attention elsewhere ahead of the NHL trade deadline as they look to acquire a No. 1 or No. 2 center That could potentially be Crosby, who may be traded by the Penguins if he asks Pittsburgh GM Kyle Dubas for a trade in the final season of his contract with the Penguins, which is unlikely to make the playoffs. If that’s the case, then look for Minnesota to be interested in acquiring the superstar’s services. Wild Could Make Pitch for Sidney Crosby In a mailbag for The Athletic , Wild beat reporter Michael Russo said that if Crosby were made available by the Penguins, then Minnesota would be interested, and Crosby’s relationship with Wild GM Bill Guerin — who he won the Stanley Cup with in Pittsburgh in 2009 — could be a benefit to the Wild. “And Crosby? His future will depend solely on what he wants to do. Obviously, he has the relationship with Guerin and the Wild would be interested in a nanosecond,” Russo wrote. Crosby being traded will be entirely up to him, as he has a full no-movement clause. But if he tells Dubas that he wants a chance to win a fourth Stanley Cup, then the Wild would be a great fit for him. Wild Would Also Be Interested in Evgeni Malkin In addition to Crosby, the Wild would also be interested in Evgeni Malkin, the other aging superstar from Pittsburgh who can send the Penguins a list in January of three teams that he would accept a trade to. Based on his relationship with Guerin and Wild star Kirill Kaprizov, Russo theorized Malkin may be interested in joining the Wild. “As for Malkin, if he ever leaves Pittsburgh, he’d likely include Minnesota on his list of teams he’d accept a trade to because of his relationships with former teammate Bill Guerin and offseason workout partner Kirill Kaprizov,” Russo wrote. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Wild Would Be ‘Interested in a Nanosecond’ in Sidney Crosby appeared first on HEAVY .

(Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) Getty The Miami Heat are set to visit the Philadelphia 76ers on Wednesday as part of the 2026 NBA Cup group stages, and they could be without their best player, Giannis Antetokounmpo. According to the Heat’s official injury report, Antetokounmpo is questionable due to right groin tendinitis. He missed Miami’s previous game last Sunday against the Oklahoma City Thunder. Despite the two-time MVP’s absence, the Heat prevailed over the short-handed Thunder 123-113. Bam Adebayo had 24 points, 15 rebounds, 12 assists, two steals and two blocks, while six more players scored in double figures. Who Starts if Giannis Sits? Getty Giannis Antetokounmpo #7 of the Miami Heat controls the ball against the Milwaukee Bucks at Kaseya Center on November 18, 2026 in Miami, Florida. If Giannis is downgraded to out before the scheduled 5:00 p.m. EST tip-off, Bobby Portis is expected to step into his place in the starting lineup. Portis started on Sunday’s game at power forward, finishing with 10 points and eight rebounds in 21 minutes. Bam Adebayo will be carrying the offensive load as a scorer and playmaker, just like he did against the Thunder. In 15 games this season, Giannis is averaging 28.

It will create a three-way tie with the Heat and Cleveland Cavaliers , heading into the final day of the group stage. As for their final group stage opponents, the Heat face the defending NBA Cup holders, the New York Knicks . The Sixers have an easier matchup against the Tyrese Haliburton -less Indiana Pacers . item.title: Who was Martha Firestone Ford? Her life, family and Lions legacy
item.description: Martha Firestone Ford's life bridged two of the American Midwest's most prominent industrial families and left a lasting mark on Detroit's sports landscape. Ford, the owner and chair emeritus of the Detroit Lions , died Nov. 24 at age 101, leading to an outpouring of support from local leaders, Lions fans and NFL officials. From her Akron roots to her years leading the Detroit Lions, here's a look at the woman behind the name. From the Rubber City to the Motor City Born in Akron, Ohio, in 1925, Ford was the granddaughter of Harvey Firestone, founder of the Firestone Tire and Rubber Co. She studied at Our Lady of the Elms High School in Akron before graduating from Vassar College in New York in 1946. She married William Clay Ford Sr. the following year. The couple initially settled in New Haven, Connecticut, before relocating to the Detroit area in 1952. More: Tributes pour in for Martha Firestone Ford Lions ownership In 1963, William Clay purchased the Lions for $4.5 million from a consortium of more than 100 shareholders. For decades, Ford stood alongside her husband, often with their children, greeting players after games, according to her obituary by the NFL. Martha assumed control of the franchise following William Clay's death in March 2014. She was 88 at the time and became the fifth principal owner or ownership group to lead the franchise since its move to Detroit in 1934. She served as the team's principal owner through 2019 before transitioning to an emeritus role in 2020. Her impact on the franchise Firestone Ford brought a more hands-on approach to the organization, making clear her expectations for a more competitive team. During her tenure, the Lions earned playoff berths in 2014 and 2016. After the Lions started 1-5 in the 2015 season, Firestone Ford fired longtime team president Tom Lewand and general manager Martin Mayhew, signaling a willingness to make significant organizational changes. More: Dan Campbell gave Martha Firestone Ford a game ball for 100th birthday She also oversaw the $100 million renovation of Ford Field in 2017 and helped launch Detroit Lions Inspire Change, a social justice initiative supported by an initial $600,000 commitment from Ford and players in 2019, according to her biography on the team's website. Her legacy in Detroit and the Ford family Ford's marriage connected two prominent American industrial families. Her grandparents founded the Firestone Tire and Rubber Company, while her husband was a grandson of auto innovator Henry Ford. Together, the couple raised four children, all of whom went on to assume leadership positions in the Lions organization. Her family includes 14 grandchildren and 17 great-grandchildren. Over the years, Ford numerous leadership positions outside of her work with the football franchise. She was on the board for the Detroit Lions Foundation and was an honorary member of the Henry Ford Health System Board of Trustees. She also helped lead other organizations geared toward educ

item.title: Why Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers in stunning decision
item.description: Why Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers in stunning decision originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Aaron Rodgers announced over the summer that the 2026 season would be his last, and it's possible he's already played his final NFL snap. The Steelers announced late Tuesday night that Rodgers will be inactive for Friday's game against the Broncos , naming Mason Rudolph their starter. The decision is not injury-related. Coach Mike McCarthy is benching Rodgers, despite the four-time MVP's pedigree and the Steelers' possession of the AFC's final playoff spot through 10 games. https://t.co/F2qo4OawcY — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 25, 2026 Here's what you need to know about the stunning move by the Steelers. MORE: Updated NFL playoff picture Why Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers McCarthy is making a "coach's decision," according to Netflix's Tom Pelissero. Stunner: The Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday's game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach's decision. But Rodgers has struggled and now Mike McCarthy is making a change. https://t.co/wPSeMX3lmq — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 25, 2026 The Steelers have struggled mightily on the offensive end in recent weeks, dropping from 6-2 to 6-4 after they were able to skate by behind a strong defense earlier in the season. Joe Burrow surpassed 220 yards before Rodgers even completed a pass against the Bengals on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 10, and Pittsburgh's offense was sluggish all day long as the Eagles snapped their seven-game losing streak with a win over the Steelers this past weekend. Given the short week, Rodgers' pedigree and his familiarity with McCarthy, however, a benching wasn't expected at this point. The Steelers are undoubtedly looking for a spark from Rudolph as they try to make one more push to win the AFC North, but Rodgers won't even serve as the backup on Friday, indicating he could be out of the team's plans entirely going forward.

item.title: Nollywood legend Pete Edochie dies at 79
item.description: Pete Edochie, Nollywood legend, has died at the age of 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Chief Edochie died at 12:30a.m. on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, the family announced. His family made the announcement in a statement on Instagram by Leo Pete Edochie, his son, describing the late veteran actor as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman”. He captioned the post “An Iroko Has Fallen.” “With profound sadness and hearts bowed in total submission to the will of Almighty God, we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman, Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE, MON (Ononenyi), a retired broadcaster and veteran Actor,” the statement read. Edochie “departed this life on Wednesday, 25th November 2026 at 12.30a.m. after a protracted battle with prostate cancer in Enugu, Nigeria. He was aged 79 years. “Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE hailed from Akamnato Ifite Nteje and is survived by his beloved wife, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, his children, siblings and numerous other relations. “Funeral arrangements will be announced in due course. “As we mourn this painful loss, we pray that Almighty God grants his gentle soul eternal rest and gives the entire family the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. “May God be with us all at this trying time,” added. Below is the post: View this post on Instagram A post shared by Leo Edochie (@edochieleo) Biography Vanguard News The post Nollywood legend Pete Edochie dies at 79 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Virginia Tech football: Benji Gosnell represents all the right things
item.description: BLACKSBURG, VA - OCTOBER 26: Virginia Tech Hokies tight end Benji Gosnell (82) catches a pass during a college football game between the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets and the Virginia Tech Hokies on October 26, 2024, at Lane Stadium in Blacksburg, VA.(Photo by Brian Bishop/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Virginia Tech tight end Benji Gosnell was once a four-star tight end prospect out of East Surry High School in Pilot Mountain, North Carolina. He had scholarship offers from everywhere, including Ohio State. He committed to the Buckeyes as a sophomore in high school. Gosnell’s family later moved to Southwestern Virginia, where he played his senior season at Carroll County High School. He also had a change of heart about college, backing off his pledge to Ohio State and later committing to Virginia Tech. He was essentially Brent Pry’s first recruiting win as head coach back in December 2021. Gosnell signed with the Hokies and enrolled in 2022. Unfortunately, he missed his freshman season while recovering from knee surgery — his second. In 2023, Gosnell quickly established himself, playing in all 13 games and making eight starts. In 2024, he started all 13 games for the Hokies at tight end and was beginning to look like a future NFL player. In 2025, Gosnell was named captain and was expected to be a primary piece in new offensive coordinator Philip Montgomery’s offense. Things didn’t go as planned. Pry was fired after three games and Montgomery was named interim coach. And his offense forgot tight ends existed. Last offseason, the Hokies hired James Franklin as head coach. His new offensive coordinator, Ty Howle, is arguably the best tight-end developer in college football. They were also bringing a couple of former Penn State tight ends, Luke Reynolds and Matt Henderson, with them. Instead of leaving for another opportunity, Gosnell did what is rare these days: he stuck it out in Blacksburg, knowing his role may change. Gosnell has played in every game this season, but has a career low of six receptions for 33 yards. He still plays a vital role as a blocker and he delivers when his number is called. But Gosnell’s role is even more important than what he does on the field. He remains a captain under Franklin. Even if his role changed for his final season, Gosnell remains the ultimate representative of Virginia Tech. A true culture-changing player. While his numbers may not be remembered years from now, his impact will. After last week’s loss at Miami, which dropped the Hokies to 6-5, the usually reserved Gosnell addressed his team. He told them that while losing to Miami hurt, losing to Virginia in the regular-season finale would hurt even more. It was a message his coaches and teammates appreciated. Gosnell also spoke to the media this week and said that while he’s dealt with adversity, he wouldn’t change a thing. Great stuff here from Benji Gosnell looking back on his time at Virginia Tech with nothing but love

Epitome of a Hokie pic.twitter.com/j9RhyK2blU — Sons of Saturday Virginia Tech (@SonsofSatVT) November 19, 2026 Saturday’s game against UVA will be Gosnell’s last at Lane Stadium. Saturday may be the last home game of Gosnell’s college career, but he will leave behind a lasting legacy he should be proud of.

item.title: Ex-Mets hurler signs with Yankees’ division rival
item.description: Ex- Mets pitcher Freddy Peralta has found a new home. And it’s with a division rival of the Yankees. Peralta and the Baltimore Orioles are in agreement on a five-year, $125 million contract, per ESPN’s Jeff Passan and Ken Rosenthal of Fox. Peralta, whom the Mets traded at the deadline, went 2-1 with a 2.95 ERA in five postseason appearances with the Tampa Bay Rays during their run to the World Series. He was named MVP of the ALCS against the Cleveland Guardians. An unrestricted free agent, he had been linked to teams like the Giants, Twins, White Sox and Padres, as well as potential returns to Tampa Bay and the Mets. item.title: Doc Rivers speaks on his relationship with Giannis Antetokounmpo after recent comments
item.description: Doc Rivers speaks on his relationship with Giannis Antetokounmpo after recent comments originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Doc Rivers recently made headlines on Bill Simmons' podcast, where he spoke extensively about his tenure with the Milwaukee Bucks . Considering that he had Giannis Antetokounmpo as the superstar player, the conversation naturally led to discussions about what it was like to coach the Greek Freak. While he addressed Giannis' strengths, he did have a tidbit there where he downplayed the two-time MVP's basketball IQ. Of course, that led to a news frenzy because Rivers was already an unpopular figure amongst fans, but that further fueled the flames. However, Rivers admits that it was blown way out of proportion. Doc Rivers reveals he and Giannis Antetokounmpo don't have any beef Now that Antetokounmpo is playing for the Miami Heat , he looks infinitely better than the last couple of seasons with the Bucks . The two-time MVP still has immense love for the Bucks and the city of Milwaukee, but he has moved on, so it seems he does not pay too much attention to what happened in the past. Of course, Antetokounmpo made sure to dismiss that issue a couple of days after the podcast was released. Giannis did not give it any more attention, and the news about it died down naturally. However, it seems that Rivers has wanted to clarify those comments a couple of weeks later. MORE: Giannis Antetokounmpo finally responds to Doc Rivers' intriguing comments about him Rivers was once again talking about the controversial comments on another appearance on The Bill Simmons Podcast. However, it was to clear up any ill will between him and his former star player after Simmons asked him about the relationship after the viral clip. "That got outta control, and where that went was hilarious. I talked to Giannis; it’s no issue. I have opinions no one can have from being a coach, and you want to be honest, and that’s what I’m trying to do," Rivers said on another appearance on The Bill Simmons Podcast . It seems that this controversy is now back in the news, but considering that it is dismissive of what happened, this might not cause the same uproar as the previous comment. However, it will still get some people a bit angry because they don't want to deal with the discourse anymore. item.title: Colts OC sees silver lining in riding Anthony Richardson roller coaster for rest of 2026
item.description: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Colts OC sees silver lining in riding Anthony Richardson roller coaster for rest of 2026 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts may be struggling, but quarterback Anthony Richardson has a huge opportunity to show his mettle and finally silence the doubters, who have been tugging at him since his rookie year in 2023. The criticisms, however, have weight, as Richardson has not lived up to his potential as the No. 4 pick. Inconsistent performances and major injuries have derailed him, possibly affecting his mentality and confidence. But all is not lost. Richardson has been handed the keys again after the Colts surprisingly released Daniel Jones . Offensive coordinator Bob Cooter mentioned the silver lining in leaning on the 24-year-old signal-caller, as reported by The Athletic’s James Boyd. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We’ve obviously had an interesting four years at (quarterback). But Anthony’s got to watch a lot of different guys go through their weekly process. Of preparing for an opponent,” said Cooter. “It can be nice to have that 10,000-foot view.” Fans on X, however, did not appreciate Cooter’s tone. “Why do the coaches shade AR every chance they get? It’s WHACK!” said @CharonVonberg. “I’m sick and tired of their excuses as to why Richardson did or didn’t do,” added @KirbyHa20330142. “Every coach’s response is basically a shoulder shrug, LMFAO. I hope AR balls out,” wrote @dfaustt. “I get annoyed with this coaching staff talking about preparation when we have won two games in the last year,” stated @r_burton19. “Ant, bro, please cook these next six weeks. All these coaches will be fired, and you will have the last laugh! Tired of seeing the disrespect for real!” commented @MartellEverett. Richardson will have his hands full trying to steer the Colts back on track, as they are 1-6 in their last seven games. All eyes will be on him when Indianapolis hosts the New York Giants on Sunday. As they say, adversity can lead to a defining moment. item.title: ‘People Have Lost Their Minds,’ ‘Lotta People Willing to Die on That Joe Buck Hill’ — Ex-ESPN Star Defends Troy Aikman Amid Backlash Over MNF Drama
item.description: ‘That Microphone Is a Drug,’ ‘This Is All About Ego’ -- Vikings Legend Breaks Down Troy Aikman vs. Joe Buck Fallout at ESPN Tim Cowlishaw thinks the Troy Aikman criticism has gone well past the point of fair game. With seemingly every remark from ESPN’s Monday Night Football booth getting picked apart, the former “Around the Horn” panelist stepped in to defend him. Cowlishaw’s complaint was about the reaction to Aikman’s humor. He believes viewers are treating jokes as fresh evidence in the drama involving Aikman and longtime broadcast partner Joe Buck. Tim Cowlishaw Pushes Back Against Troy Aikman’s Critics Cowlishaw delivered his defense in a short post that left little doubt about where he stood. “People have lost their minds with their criticism of Aikman for everything he says. He makes a joke on anything and they go nuts. lotta people willing to die on that Joe Buck Hill i suppose…” Cowlishaw wrote . The post did not announce a development in either broadcaster’s contract situation. It challenged the way Aikman’s comments were being received, with Cowlishaw suggesting that allegiance to Buck had become part of the response. That distinction matters in a story increasingly driven by how people interpret a sentence, a facial expression or a pause between two broadcasters. Cowlishaw sees an audience primed to take offense, even when he believes Aikman is kidding. He also has experience with the demands of sports television. Cowlishaw was a regular panelist on ESPN’s Around the Horn, which ended its run in May 2025. His defense comes from someone who spent years making arguments and trading remarks in front of a camera. Cowlishaw didn’t spell out which joke prompted his post. His wording addressed the broader criticism of Aikman, making it clear that he thought the scrutiny had become excessive. Troy Aikman-Russell Yurk MNF Exchange Adds to Broadcast Debate Notably, the latest Monday night broadcast supplied another moment for viewers to debate. After Washington’s 22–20 win over Cincinnati, ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk explained the clock issue surrounding the finish. Aikman’s reaction to Yurk drew criticism , particularly his remark, “That was your moment, Russ.” The exchange became another talking point about the atmosphere in ESPN’s booth. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor It was a busy night for the broadcast crew even before the postgame discussion. The game ended with a dispute over whether two seconds should have remained following Washington’s winning field goal. Yurk explained that replay couldn’t restore the time because the next play would have been a kickoff. The quarterback matchup featured Joe Burrow and Jayden Daniels. Washington won a game that kept the broadcast focused on a close finish before attention shifted upstairs. Cowlishaw’s post pushed back on that habit of reading everything through the same dispute. His defense leaves viewers to judge the broadcast themselves. What he clearly rejects is the assumption that every Aikman joke deserves another round of outrage. Cowlishaw has watched enough sports television to know people will disagree. This time, he thinks the audience is trying too hard to find a fight. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Joe Rogan and Anthony Kim Have Big News Coming: Report
item.description: BEDMINSTER, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 06: Anthony Kim of United States of America looks on from the third green during day one of LIV Golf New York at Trump National Golf Club on August 06, 2026 in Bedminster, New Jersey. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) Getty BEDMINSTER, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 08: Anthony Kim of United States of America looks on from the 16th green during day three of LIV Golf New York at Trump National Golf Club on August 08, 2026 in Bedminster, New Jersey. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) Getty Joe Rogan is now part of the conversation surrounding Anthony Kim’s comeback. Kim has spent much of his return to professional golf answering questions about his game. There’s a longer story fans have wanted to hear since he came back, and a new report suggests it could soon reach well beyond the people who have followed his career. Kim was one of the most exciting young players in golf before he stepped away for more than a decade. His return with LIV Golf gave fans a chance to see him compete again. It also brought back questions about what happened during all those years away and what made him ready to return. Kim has shared pieces of his story since then. The latest report points to two opportunities for fans to hear more, including one that could make a little history in golf. Anthony Kim Reportedly Set to Join Joe Rogan’s Podcast Flushing It Golf reported that Kim is in line for an appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience . The outlet described it as a first for the show. “Sources indicate that Anthony Kim is set to be the first professional golfer ever to appear on The Joe Rogan Experience, the most popular podcast in the world,” Flushing It Golf reported. The outlet also pointed to an upcoming documentary about Kim. That gives fans another reason to follow what he has planned away from the course. “He has a huge army of fans following his story and looking forward to what comes next. The appearance on Joe Rogan and the upcoming documentary will both be must watch.” Most tournament interviews start with the round a player just finished. Rogan’s format could give Kim time to get into the years between his PGA Tour career and his return. It could also give him the chance to talk about what it took to start competing again after so long away. item.title: Stephen A. Smith Says NBA Stars Thanked Him For Lakers ‘Too White’ Comments
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - NOVEMBER 12: Stephen A. Smith, sports commentator and TV personality, speaks to reporters after meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House on November 12, 2026 in Washington, DC. Smith spoke about his interview with President Trump and told reporters he would not be the next White House Press Secretary. (Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images) Getty Controversial NBA pundit Stephen A. Smith revealed that current players have supported his racial comment about the Los Angeles Lakers. Smith claimed that the Lakers have no chance at winning the NBA Championship due to their three top stars being white. A new layer to the story emerged today when Smith shared that current NBA players have privately backed him up. Smith believes that the Lakers won’t win it all due to Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler all being white. View this post on Instagram The following comment showed that Smith feels empowered by his comments: “You know how many brothers reached out to me in the NBA and thanked me for saying it? Because they can’t say it. You’re gonna have to mix some chocolate up into that mix right now, because the brothers is waiting down the pike for them.” The Lakers have a tough path to the title with teams like the San Antonio Spurs , New York Knicks , and Minnesota Timberwolves all considered realistic contenders. Despite the early season success, the Lakers are often viewed as an overachieving team more than a top contender for the NBA Championship. Smith has been under fire for constantly bringing up race, but there are plenty of other reasons why they’ll likely fall short. Stephen A Smith Controversial Lakers Comments Various talk show appearances witnessed Smith going out of his way to bring up the Lakers being “too white” when discussing their early success. Smith cited historic teams like the Boston Celtics and Chicago Bulls when stating no team has won it all past the 1960s with the top three players all being white. Recent rumors leaked that Smith was going to be suspended from ESPN due to the negative backlash. Fans of all races felt the comment was a bit out of line for a sports show, but Smith confirmed those rumors were inaccurate. No punishment was issued, and he remains on ESPN First Take. Lakers Not Responding To Stephen A Smith The Lakers have not said anything about Smith’s comments, despite NBA athletes often speaking out against media pundits who disrespect them. Smith had a relationship with head coach JJ Redick back when the latter appeared on ESPN First Take. Despite Redick often having volatile debates with Smith, the two remained friends. Stephen A often praises JJ more than the Lakers players when he is forced to give them credit for their success. However, Smith has had multiple issues with the Lakers in recent years. Stephen A made headlines when LeBron James confronted him at a live Lakers game about comments he made on air. LeBron reportedly felt disrespected when Smith criticized

item.title: ‘He Didn’t Wanna Miss (Patrick) Mahomes’ — NFL World Takes Notice As NBC Switches Cris Collinsworth’s SNF Assignment for Chiefs-Bills on Thanksgiving
item.description: ‘You Just Know He’s Punching Air,’ ‘Can’t Make It Up’ — NFL World Reacts to Cris Collinsworth ‘Going Dead Silent’ After Patrick Mahomes’ Mistakes The Thanksgiving slate of football has always been one of the biggest days on the NFL calendar. This season is no different, with three blockbuster matchups set for the day. The marquee matchup, of course, features one of the best modern rivalries in sports, writing its latest chapter as the Buffalo Bills take on the Kansas City Chiefs. With the magnitude of the game and major ramifications on the line, NBC decided to change Cris Collinsworth’s assignment and bring him on board for this game. Cris Collinsworth Draws Chiefs vs. Bills Assignment for NBC A former wide receiver with three Pro Bowl appearances to his credit, Collinsworth became one of the biggest names in the broadcasting business, with 17 Sports Emmy Awards to his name. As a result, it was understandable that the network wanted one of its best announcers working the Chiefs vs. Bills game. At 8-2 (Chiefs) and 9-1 (Bills), the two teams are near the top of the AFC pyramid, and this game could end up deciding the playoff seeding come January. Add in the history and the rivalry component between Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, and it is shaping up to be a matchup for the ages. Fans, too, were quick to notice the change in assignments. “Boooo. Disrespectful to the Browns,” Big Cat of Barstool Sports remarked , as Collinsworth switched places with Jason Garrett for Sunday’s game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Cleveland Browns. Podcaster Farzin Vousoughian noted , “Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth will announce the Chiefs-Bills game on Thanksgiving night on NBC. Collinsworth usually takes off for Thanksgiving, but he will be on the call this year and will take this Sunday night off instead. In other words, he didn’t wanna miss Mahomes vs. Allen.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor But for all of the great work that Collinsworth has done on the booth, fans have also accused him of playing favourites at times and going above and beyond for the players he likes. The biggest example of that has been Mahomes. “Makes sense,” Dallas Cowboys beat writer Tom Downey pointed out , before adding, “He’s gonna need time to recover from glazing Mahomes like he’s a honey-baked ham.” Sam Chimenti came to a similar conclusion , claiming, “You can never pull Collinsworth away from Mahomes lmao.” Wayne Pruski added , “Great. A love fest on Mahomes. Well, we can watch the game with the sound off, sorry sponsors!” It remains to be seen how the exact game plays out and which way Collinsworth leans. But with both teams coming in on dominant winning streaks, Week 12 promises to be worth the price of admission. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: College Football Playoff rankings: Big Ten CFP chances take a major hit
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - JANUARY 10: The National Championship trophy is displayed after the Georgia Bulldogs defeated the Alabama Crimson Tide 33-18 in the 2022 CFP National Championship Game at Lucas Oil Stadium on January 10, 2022 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday night, the College Football Playoff Bowl Selection Committee released its fourth Top 25 rankings. Eight Big Ten teams made the top 25. November 2️⃣4️⃣ #CFP Top 25 🏆 pic.twitter.com/Ax7mJPObI4 — CFP (@CFBPlayoff) November 25, 2026 Big Ten teams ranked in the CFP Top 25 No. 9 UCLA No. 12 Oregon No. 13 Iowa No. 14 Indiana No. 15 USC No. 21 Ohio State No. 24 Washington No. 25 Nebraska While this is the most teams the Big Ten has had in the top 25, it’s the fewest they’ve had in the top 10. If the season ended today, only one Big Ten team would make the playoffs — UCLA. UCLA would have a road matchup against No. 8 Wake Forest. UCLA dropped from No. 4 to No. 9 after losing to Michigan last Saturday, while Indiana dropped from No. 8 to No. 14 after losing to Washington. Iowa rose from No. 15 to No. 13, Oregon from No. 13 to No. 12, and USC from No. 18 to No. 15. Oregon has the best Big Ten betting odds of winning the national championship at +2000, per FanDuel Sportsbook . Despite being ranked No. 9 currently, UCLA has +15000 odds of winning it all. The pessimism surrounding UCLA has everything to do with quarterback Ty Dieffenbach’s injury status and whether he’ll be able to play on Saturday versus USC. Dieffenbach injured his hip against Michigan but practiced on Tuesday and hasn’t been ruled out for the USC game. Per ESPN’s College Football Power Index , only two Big Ten teams have over a 50% chance of making the playoffs. ESPN’s FPI gives Oregon a 66.4% chance of making the playoffs and UCLA a 57.6% chance. What do you think of the top 25 rankings this week? How many Big Ten teams will make the playoffs? Let us know in the comments.

item.title: Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers benched for Week 12 vs Broncos, new starter named
item.description: There is some major NFL quarterback news ahead of a drawn-out Week 12 of the regular season. With games beginning on Wednesday night, the Pittsburgh Steelers dropped a late-night bomb announcing a quarterback change. Veteran signal-caller Aaron Rodgers has been benched by the Steelers after a string of brutal offensive performances from the team. With Rodgers sidelined, the team will be turning to backup quarterback Mason Rudolph for Friday afternoon’s showdown against the Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium. NFL insider Jordan Schultz was the first to report the news . MORE: NFL power rankings entering Week 12: All 32 teams ranked worst to first According to another league insider, Tom Pelissero, “Aaron Rodgers will be inactive Friday, and now has potentially played the final snap of his legendary 22-year career .” With Rodgers inactive, it will be interesting to see whether Will Howard or rookie Drew Allar suits up as the primary backup. Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) after the game at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The news comes after the Steelers suffered back-to-back losses to the divisional foe Cincinnati Bengals and struggling cross-state rival Philadelphia Eagles. The Steelers were dominated in Week 10 against the Bengals, with Rodgers throwing for just 143 yards. He was sacked three times and recorded a miserable QBR of 26.3. Against the Eagles, Rodgers again struggled to get rid of the ball. He was sacked five times, while throwing for 227 yards and one interception for a QBR of 40.7 as the Eagles snapped a seven-game losing streak. It was clearly time for a change in Pittsburgh, and now they’ll have to see what Mason Rudolph brings to the table on Black Friday. item.title: Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers, name Mason Rudolph starting QB vs. Broncos
item.description: (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback vs. the Denver Broncos in their Week 12 game on Black Friday, the team announced in a statement Tuesday night . The Steelers’ passing game took a massive step backward over the last two weeks, with Aaron Rodgers’ play actively hurting the offense. In that span, Rodgers ranks 26th in success rate and the Steelers have failed to score 20 points. On the season, Rodgers ranks 35th in EPA per play (min. 25 dropbacks). He has thrown 16 touchdowns to six interceptions. Rudolph’s last start came in 2025 against the Chicago Bears in relief of an injured Rodgers. Rudolph went 24-of-31 for 171 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in a 31-28 loss. He finished the game the previous week when Rodgers broke his wrist, throwing a touchdown in a 34-12 win over the Bengals. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! item.title: BREAKING: Mason Rudolph to Replace Aaron Rodgers as Steelers Quarterback
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterbacks Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph at practice on Sept. 11, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Pittsburgh Steelers have declared that Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the team’s Week 12 home game against the Denver Broncos on Friday, and announced that Mason Rudolph will be the team’s starting quarterback. The announcement came via a statement from Steelers spokesman Burt Lauten after 11 p.m. on Tuesday, and did not include any context or reasoning for the change. Team sources indicated that it was a coach’s decision. Head coach Mike McCarthy had said definitively during his press conference on Monday that Rodgers would remain his starting quarterback. “Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback,” McCarthy said. Rodgers had his normal media availability after practice on Tuesday, and did not give any inclination that anything was amiss. “It’s November into December football,” he said. “You’ve got to be playing your best ball this time of year, so we’ve got to bounce back accordingly this week.” Rodgers and the rest of the Pittsburgh passing offense have been struggling. He has thrown for only 370 yards over the last two games combined. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph during a preseason game on Aug. 21, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Rudolph, 31, has dressed as the Steelers backup all season. He last appeared as a starter in 2025, when he made one appearance in place of an injured Rodgers. In 2024, he started five games for the Tennessee Titans. In five games with the Titans in 2024, Rudolph threw for 1,530 yards, nine touchdowns and nine interceptions, while maintaining an 80.1 passer rating. He lost his lone start with the Steelers in 2025. item.title: Watch Oilers’ Connor McDavid knife through Golden Knights defense for wicked goal
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Watch Oilers’ Connor McDavid knife through Golden Knights defense for wicked goal appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . They don’t call Edmonton Oilers superstar forward Connor McDavid “McJesus” for nothing. He showed why people call him that once again during Tuesday’s showdown against the Vegas Golden Knights at Rogers Place in Edmonton. With under 20 seconds left in the second period, McDavid sliced through the gut of the Golden Knights defense in the offensive zone and dished the puck to Kasperi Kapanen before getting it back to finish the give-and-go in spectacular fashion. Vegas goalie Carter Hart just couldn’t do much about it. Here is a look at that huge score from the three-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner McDavid: Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) WHAT A GOAL CONNOR MCDAVID 🚨 Simply spectacular! pic.twitter.com/1MzwvrJ2Iu — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 25, 2026 That goal tied the score at 2-2 and brought the house down inside the Oilers’ home arena. People on social media were just as hyped after seeing that incredible goal from McDavid. “When does he play against the hard teams 😂? Good grief he’s different.,” a fan said . “That was beauty,” a social media user on X shared . “MCDAVID… WE ARE NOT WORTHY 🥹,” another one commented . “It’s ridiculous how easy Connor McDavid makes hockey seem,” a different fan said . “Yeah he’s the best we’ve ever seen. Hope Levi is the goalie to eventually lead them to the promised land,” another comment read. McDavid is always going to do what he does best for the Oilers , and that’s using his elite skills to get the better of even great teams. The 29-year-old McDavid entered the Golden Knights game with 13 goals and 45 assists for an absurd total of 58 points through just 26 games played in the 2026-27 NHL season. item.title: IPL 2027 auction: List of overseas players registered in Indian Premier League mini-auction
item.description: IPL 2027 auction: List of overseas players registered in Indian Premier League mini-auction originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Ben Stokes and David Warner headline a large overseas contingent in the IPL 2027 mini-auction register. Several Bangladesh players have entered, despite the Mistafizur Rahman saga in early 2026. Franchises now face two deadlines before the board prepares the final shortlist for Goa. IPL 2027 mini-auction: Full list of overseas players registered in Indian Premier League mini-auction with base prices and countries A long list of overseas players has put their names forward for the IPL 2027 mini-auction, and the full register offers an early look at who could be available when the bidding begins in Goa. The event is scheduled for Wednesday, December 16, 2026, with the action starting at 11:00 AM IST. The most prominent name on the register is Ben Stokes, the 35-year-old England all-rounder who retired from international cricket earlier this year. He has signed up at the top base price of ₹2 crore, and his presence is a boost for an auction that does not carry many marquee names. Some franchises may also see him as a possible captaincy option, particularly those that are searching for a new leader. In total, 1,220 players have registered, made up of 939 Indians and 281 overseas players, and they will compete for a maximum of 66 places across the ten teams. Only 25 of those places are open to overseas players, so the competition among the foreign names will be fierce. The initial list will be pruned further before the final auction pool is released. The register also includes 12 players from Bangladesh, which has come as a surprise in light of last year's controversy. However, Shakib Al Hasan and Mustafizur Rahman do not appear on the list, and their absence has drawn almost as much attention as the names that are present. IPL 2027 mini-auction register: How many overseas players have signed up? The overseas group of 281 consists of 170 capped internationals, 69 uncapped overseas players and 42 players from Associate nations. One of the Associate names is Japan's Benjamin Ito-Davis, who has a base price of ₹30 lakh. Category Players Total registered 1,220 Indians 939 Overseas players 281 Capped internationals 170 Uncapped overseas players 69 Associate nation players 42 Capped Indians 14 Uncapped Indians from previous IPL seasons 127 Other uncapped Indians 798 Available slots (overseas) 66 (25) IPL 2027 mini-auction list: Overseas players in the ₹2 crore base price bracket Reports suggest that 30 players are in the highest bracket, two of them Indians and 28 overseas. He has signed up at the top base price of ₹2 crore, and his presence is a boost for an auction that does not carry many marquee names. Some franchises may also see him as a possible captaincy option, particularly those that are searching for a new leader. In total, 1,220 players have registered, made up of 939 Indians and 281 overseas players, and they will compete for a maximum of 66 places across the ten teams. Only 25 of those places are open to overseas players, so the competition among the foreign names will be fierce. The initial list will be pruned further before the final auction pool is released. The register also includes 12 players from Bangladesh, which has come as a surprise in light of last year's controversy. However, Shakib Al Hasan and Mustafizur Rahman do not appear on the list, and their absence has drawn almost as much attention as the names that are present. IPL 2027 mini-auction register: How many overseas players have signed up? The overseas group of 281 consists of 170 capped internationals, 69 uncapped overseas players and 42 players from Associate nations. One of the Associate names is Japan's Benjamin Ito-Davis, who has a base price of ₹30 lakh. Category Players Total registered 1,220 Indians 939 Overseas players 281 Capped internationals 170 Uncapped overseas players 69 Associate nation players 42 Capped Indians 14 Uncapped Indians from previous IPL seasons 127 Other uncapped Indians 798 Available slots (overseas) 66 (25) IPL 2027 mini-auction list: Overseas players in the ₹2 crore base price bracket Reports suggest that 30 players are in the highest bracket, two of them Indians and 28 overseas. Country Players at ₹2 crore Australia (5) David Warner, Jake Fraser-McGurk, Jhye Richardson, Mahli Beardman, Spencer Johnson England (5) Ben Stokes, Jonny Bairstow, Sam Billings, Sonny Baker, Tom Curran New Zealand (8) Adam Milne, Ben Sears, Bevon Jacobs, Daryl Mitchell, Devon Conway, Rachin Ravindra, Trent Boult, Will O'Rourke Afghanistan (3) Fazalhaq Farooqi, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Rahmanullah Gurbaz South Africa (2) Anrich Nortje, Gerald Coetzee Sri Lanka (2) Matheesha Pathirana, Wanindu Hasaranga West Indies (2) Shai Hope, Shimron Hetmyer IPL 2027 mini-auction list: Overseas players at ₹1.5 crore, ₹1.25 crore and ₹1 crore base prices The next two brackets hold a mix of experienced white-ball names and bowlers who have impressed in recent seasons. Scott Boland is listed in the ₹1 crore group, but he has since withdrawn. Base price Players (country) ₹1.5 crore Allah Mohammad Ghazanfar (Afghanistan), Daniel Sams and Riley Meredith (Australia), David Wiese (Namibia), Rassie van der Dussen (South Africa), Jayden Seales and Keemo Paul (West Indies) ₹1.25 crore Ashton Agar and Billy Stanlake (Australia), Kyle Mayers and Matthew Forde (West Indies) ₹1 crore: Afghanistan Gulbadin Naib, Ibrahim Zadran, Mohammad Nabi ₹1 crore: Australia Chris Lynn, Matthew Kuhnemann, Nikhil Chaudhary, Scott Boland (withdrawn) ₹1 crore: England Tymal Mills ₹1 crore: New Zealand Blair Tickner, Matthew Fisher, Nathan Smith, Zak Foulkes ₹1 crore: South Africa Duan Jansen, Marques Ackerman, Matthew Breetzke, Ottneil Baartman ₹1 crore: Sri Lanka Charith Asalanka, Dushmantha Chameera, Kusal Mendis, Maheesh Theekshana, Sonal Dinusha ₹1 crore: West Indies Andre Fletcher, John Campbell ₹1 crore: Zimbabwe Newman Nyamhuri Who are the Bangladesh players registered for IPL 2027 mini-auction? The 12 Bangladesh players on the register are Hasan Mahmud, Mahedi Hasan, Mohammad Rubel, Parvez Hossain Emon, Ripon Mondol, Rishad Hossain, Saif Hassan, Shamim Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, Taskin Ahmed and Towhid Hridoy. Their entry is unexpected because Kolkata Knight Riders were forced to release Mustafizur Rahman last year on a BCCI instruction, amid political tension between India and Bangladesh. KKR had bought the left-arm pacer for ₹9.2 crore at the previous mini-auction. It is not clear whether the BCCI have been given a green light from the Union Government, and that may explain why Shakib Al-Hasan and Mustafizur Rahman have stayed out. IPL 2027 auction deadlines: November 27 and December 1 The BCCI has told the franchises to submit any extra player requests by 5:00 PM IST on Friday, November 27, for names that are not on the initial register, and those players will be added to the final set. The teams must then send in their preferred shortlist by Tuesday, December 1, after which the board will release the truncated auction list. For all the latest cricket news, opinion, and commentary, and to share your voice, head to our Facebook , Instagram , and X (Twitter) pages.

item.title: FSU easily dispatches UNC Asheville but saw a key player injured in the process
item.description: Shon Abaev brings the ball up the court for FSU against UNC Asheville. | Peyton Baker Florida State (6-1, 0-0) led by double-digits for the final 29 minutes of the game, cruising to a blowout over UNC Asheville (2-6, 0-0), 97-61. The Seminoles received contributions from up and down the bench, with 11 players in the scoring column and 10 players recording at least 2 assists or rebounds. However, it wasn’t all good news as 6’8 sophomore Shon Abaev left the game late in the first half after a hard fall and never returned. First Half The Bulldogs came into the game as a top 60 three point shooting team in the country, so naturally they opened up the scoring with back-to-back buckets at the rim (scoring over Marcis Ponder on both) to take a 4-0 lead. The Asheville lead grew to 7-2 one possession later, but from there the Seminoles went on a 9-0 run to go up 11-7 less than five minutes in. A rim-rocking ally-oop from Kameron Taylor to Ponder highlighted the spurt. The squads played back and forth basketball over the next four minutes, much to the delight of anyone who bet the over. Leading 18-15 coming out of the under-12 media timeout, the Seminoles began to turn up the pressure. Long rebounds and steals allowed the ‘Noles to get out in transition which is when they are often at their best. Ponder ran the court to follow a missed layup with a thunderous put-back, Anthony Robinson converted an and-one layup the next possession, and FSU then made five free throws to make it a “kill shot” and take a 28-15 with 8:20 left. The active hands on defense continued the following possession as Shon Abaev grabbed a steal, led the break, and then dished to a trailing Alex Steen for a crowd pleasing, one-handed jam. UNC Asheville finally stopped the bleeding with a made three, but FSU continued to add to the lead thanks to defense leading to offense. More concerning than the score was a hard fall and apparent leg injury suffered by Abaev. The do-it-all forward was helped off the court before hopping on one leg to the locker room with a little more than 6 minutes left in the half. He did not return. To their credit, FSU kept their foot on the gas following the injury timeout. The Seminoles used three different 4-0 spurts, all of which came on free throws or dunks/layups, to slow extend their lead, reaching 50-32 when the first half horn sounded. For the half, FSU scored 1.43 points per possession and really it could have been even better if it weren’t for turnovers on three or four fast break opportunities. A clock malfunction stopped play less than a minute in, followed by two different challenges over the next two minutes (one by each team, both successful). item.content:encoded: Shon Abaev brings the ball up the court for FSU against UNC Asheville. | Peyton Baker Florida State (6-1, 0-0) led by double-digits for the final 29 minutes of the game, cruising to a blowout over UNC Asheville (2-6, 0-0), 97-61. The Seminoles received contributions from up and down the bench, with 11 players in the scoring column and 10 players recording at least 2 assists or rebounds. However, it wasn’t all good news as 6’8 sophomore Shon Abaev left the game late in the first half after a hard fall and never returned. First Half The Bulldogs came into the game as a top 60 three point shooting team in the country, so naturally they opened up the scoring with back-to-back buckets at the rim (scoring over Marcis Ponder on both) to take a 4-0 lead. The Asheville lead grew to 7-2 one possession later, but from there the Seminoles went on a 9-0 run to go up 11-7 less than five minutes in. A rim-rocking ally-oop from Kameron Taylor to Ponder highlighted the spurt. The squads played back and forth basketball over the next four minutes, much to the delight of anyone who bet the over. Leading 18-15 coming out of the under-12 media timeout, the Seminoles began to turn up the pressure. Long rebounds and steals allowed the ‘Noles to get out in transition which is when they are often at their best. Ponder ran the court to follow a missed layup with a thunderous put-back, Anthony Robinson converted an and-one layup the next possession, and FSU then made five free throws to make it a “kill shot” and take a 28-15 with 8:20 left. The active hands on defense continued the following possession as Shon Abaev grabbed a steal, led the break, and then dished to a trailing Alex Steen for a crowd pleasing, one-handed jam. UNC Asheville finally stopped the bleeding with a made three, but FSU continued to add to the lead thanks to defense leading to offense. More concerning than the score was a hard fall and apparent leg injury suffered by Abaev. The do-it-all forward was helped off the court before hopping on one leg to the locker room with a little more than 6 minutes left in the half. He did not return. To their credit, FSU kept their foot on the gas following the injury timeout. The Seminoles used three different 4-0 spurts, all of which came on free throws or dunks/layups, to slow extend their lead, reaching 50-32 when the first half horn sounded. For the half, FSU scored 1.43 points per possession and really it could have been even better if it weren’t for turnovers on three or four fast break opportunities. At the other end, FSU’s defense forced turnovers on over 28% of possessions and held UNCA to just 37.9% shooting from the field. Second Half Calling the start to the second half disjointed would be putting it nicely. A clock malfunction stopped play less than a minute in, followed by two different challenges over the next two minutes (one by each team, both successful). In the middle of all that was a concerning development of Anthony Robinson II picking up his 4th foul, which when combined with Abaev being unavailable meant freshman Martay Barnes would need to carry a significantly expanded role off the bench. Barnes acquitted himself fairly well and FSU stretched the lead out to 27 over the next four minutes. By the 10 minute mark the scoreboard read 75-46 and from there the ‘Noles could have essentially named their score. During the closing stretch, in what must have been a welcome site for Coach Loucks, the outside shots finally started to fall. Elisee Assui, Robinson II, Taylor, Brandon Bass, Jr., and Sebastion Rancik, and Barnes all made second half threes, helping push Florida State’s lead out to 93-56 by the under-4 media timeout, before the deep end of the bench closed out the game. Box Score and Takeaways Chief of the Court – Sebastian Rancik scored over 20 points once again, shooting 7-10 from the field and 7-8 from the stripe. He added 5 rebounds, 2 assists, a block, and a steal and even helped bring the ball up the court when Robinson was out with foul trouble. The Abaev injury has massive implications. His athleticism and positional size has been a huge part of FSU’s success early in the year, and he fills up a stat sheet with his ability to score, rebound, and stir the drink for others. While his shot selection can get a bit out of control at times, he’s really one of the few true creators off the bounce for this FSU team. We will see what the official diagnosis is, but I can’t imagine he’s able to play in a week up in Knoxville. If he misses extended time, FSU will need several young guys to step up in a big way. Speaking of young guys, it was three freshmen who finally got FSU’s perimeter shooting going. Barnes, Bass, Jr., and Assui combined to shoot 4-8 from deep. Continuing that trend would be especially helpful in a world where Abaev has a lengthy stay on the shelf. Up Next The Seminoles break for a Thanksgiving feast before taking a drive down I-10 to face off against the West Florida Argonauts in Pensacola on Sunday. A member of the Atlantic Sun conference, this is UWF’s first year playing Division 1 basketball. They’ve only notched one win against a D1 opponent so far (an 18 point win over the same Green Bay team FSU beat last week), but they have a pair of two point losses to Alabama A&M and Cleveland State respectively. They are one of the smallest teams in all of D1 basketball, but they do shoot it pretty well, hitting 77% from the free throw line and 37.1% from deep. The game tips at 3:00pm eastern from the Pensacola Bay Center.
