item.title: Travis Kelce receives ultimate GOAT recognition from Bills head coach before Thanksgiving clash
item.description: Photo by Amy Kontras/Getty Images Travis Kelce has received a major endorsement from Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady, who has named the Kansas City Chiefs star the greatest tight end in NFL history ahead of their Thanksgiving showdown. The 37-year-old is enjoying another productive season with the Chiefs, having spent his entire 14-year NFL career in Kansas City. Kelce is coming off an impressive performance against the Arizona Cardinals, recording six receptions for 72 yards and two touchdowns in a dominant 34-7 victory. Joe Brady explains why Travis Kelce is the greatest tight end ever Brady was asked about the challenge of preparing for Kelce ahead of the Bills’ meeting with Kansas City and made his feelings clear. According to reporter Jon Scott, Brady called Kelce the greatest tight end of all time and praised the impact he has had on the position. “Joe Brady calls Travis Kelce the greatest tight end of all time, adding he revolutionized the position,” Scott reported. It is a significant compliment coming from a coach preparing to face Kelce in one of the biggest games of the Chiefs’ regular season. The veteran tight end has continued to produce despite being 37, adding another impressive display against Arizona to his already remarkable career. Kelce has also climbed the NFL’s all-time touchdown rankings. He now has 110 career touchdowns, including the playoffs, placing him third among all players in the position. Kansas City will need another strong performance from him against Buffalo, particularly with the Bills currently holding the best record in the AFC. The Chiefs enter the contest at 8-2 and sit second in the AFC West behind the Denver Broncos. A victory would give them a major opportunity to strengthen their position in the conference standings. However, Brady’s Bills will be determined to protect their place at the top of the AFC. With Kelce continuing to play an important role in Andy Reid’s offence, Buffalo will have to find a way to limit one of the greatest tight ends the league has seen. item.title: FSU men's basketball wins fourth straight, beats UNC Asheville, 97-61
item.description: Behind Sebastian Rancik's 22 points, Florida State men's basketball beat UNC Asheville 97-61 for the Seminoles' fourth consecutive win on Tuesday, Nov. 11, at the Donald L. Tucker Civic Center. It's Rancik's fourth game this season with 20 or more points, and his second in a row. Entering the game, Rancik was the ACC's leading scorer with 20.8 points per game, and his 22 will keep him on top of the league standings. He did his work primarily at the free-throw line in the first half, nailing all six of his attempts in the opening 20 minutes while going four-of-six from the field. Rancik added eight points in the second half, and he hit his lone three. He finished the game with 22 points, five rebounds, two assists and a block and steal, while shooting 70% from the field and seven-of-eight from the free-throw line. The Seminoles shot 55.4% from the field and scored 46 points in the paint, utilizing a significant size advantage over UNC Asheville. After a cold stretch shooting from deep, FSU shot 42.1% from three, its best mark since shooting 42.9% from behind the arc against Ball State, and the eight makes are tied for the most this season, joining the season-opening win over FAMU. Marcis Ponder scored eight first-half points and grabbed six rebounds. He was a consistent lob threat, scoring twice on alley-oops, and he added a putback dunk. He finished the game with those eight points and tallied 11 total rebounds. FSU led 50-32 at halftime thanks to 11 points off turnovers and 14 points at the free-throw line to pair with 30 points in the paint. Building off its 18-point lead, FSU put the game out of the reach of the Bulldogs quickly in the second half, jumping in front by 27 points after outscoring UNC Asheville 23-14 in the first 10 minutes of the half. In the final 10 minutes, FSU outscored the Bulldogs 23-15 to extend its margin of victory to 36 points. Late in the game, Amaree Robinson checked in and scored his first collegiate points, a layup in the paint. The Tallahassee native scored in the same game as his older brother, Anthony Robinson II, who finished the night with 14 points, four rebounds and an assist. Ant joins the 3-point party! 🎉 📺 ACCN | #ALLIN 🍢 pic.twitter.com/O0rGSXgnnT — Florida State Men’s Basketball (@FSUHoops) November 25, 2026 Brandon Bass Jr. scored nine points off the bench and added four rebounds, two steals and a block. Elisee Assui scored nine points off the bench, contributing 35 points off the bench. FSU's Shon Abaev exits game with injury One of the biggest moments of the game came in the final minutes of the first half when Abaev jumped to block a fastbreak dunk attempt and landed awkwardly on his ankle. He was helped off the court without putting any pressure on his right leg and jumped one-footed to the locker room for further evaluation. item.title: Delta Killings: Police summon Omo-Agege, Egbo, others for questioning
item.description: *Thugs disrupted preparations, attacked Omo-Agege’s supporters, eyewitness insists By Clifford Ndujihe, Politics Editor The police yesterday summoned former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Area Chairman, Jaro Egbo and others for questioning over the political violence that erupted during a campaign rally of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Uduere community, Ughelli North LGA of Delta State on Monday. The violence has triggered fresh accusations of political intimidation, police bias and inflammatory rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. While the NDC yesterday boycotted a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, IGP, Olatunji Disu, accusing the police of failing to protect its members, the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, called on President Bola Tinubu to renounce what it described as dangerous political rhetoric. On a day that supporters of the camps staged protest and counter protest over the killings in Ughelli, Delta State governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, who visited the troubled community, condemned the killings and directed security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible. The state government also imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area. The attack occurred on Monday during a political campaign event involving former deputy president of the Senate and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Four persons were confirmed dead, while the NDC said no fewer than 15 others were receiving treatment in intensive care. The Inspector-General of Police subsequently ordered an immediate, impartial and evidence-based investigation, including an examination of the circumstances surrounding the shooting and the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue. However, Vanguard gathered that one of the four supporters of Omo-Agege, killed in the attack, identified as Efemena Umukoro, had his first child barely six months ago. Yesterday, conflicting casualty figures trailed the killings. with rival political camps claiming seven deaths, against six acknowledged by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the police. Ughelli North Chairman, Chief Jaro Egbo, who hails from Uduere, named three persons he said were killed on his side, including the community’s President-General, PG, Cosmos Ejovwoke. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, on the other hand, listed four members of his campaign organisation died. The competing accounts bring the number of claimed fatalities to seven, although the governor and police put the toll at six, pending investigations. This was as former Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Olukayode Ariwoola, retd., warned against a repeat of the deadly violence that followed the 2011 general elections, which claimed over 800 lives, urging political parties, security agencies and other stakeholders to take urgent steps to protect the 2027 electoral process. item.content:encoded: *Thugs disrupted preparations, attacked Omo-Agege’s supporters, eyewitness insists By Clifford Ndujihe, Politics Editor The police yesterday summoned former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Area Chairman, Jaro Egbo and others for questioning over the political violence that erupted during a campaign rally of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Uduere community, Ughelli North LGA of Delta State on Monday. The violence has triggered fresh accusations of political intimidation, police bias and inflammatory rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. While the NDC yesterday boycotted a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, IGP, Olatunji Disu, accusing the police of failing to protect its members, the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, called on President Bola Tinubu to renounce what it described as dangerous political rhetoric. On a day that supporters of the camps staged protest and counter protest over the killings in Ughelli, Delta State governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, who visited the troubled community, condemned the killings and directed security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible. The state government also imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area. The attack occurred on Monday during a political campaign event involving former deputy president of the Senate and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Four persons were confirmed dead, while the NDC said no fewer than 15 others were receiving treatment in intensive care. The Inspector-General of Police subsequently ordered an immediate, impartial and evidence-based investigation, including an examination of the circumstances surrounding the shooting and the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue. However, Vanguard gathered that one of the four supporters of Omo-Agege, killed in the attack, identified as Efemena Umukoro, had his first child barely six months ago. Yesterday, conflicting casualty figures trailed the killings. with rival political camps claiming seven deaths, against six acknowledged by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the police. Ughelli North Chairman, Chief Jaro Egbo, who hails from Uduere, named three persons he said were killed on his side, including the community’s President-General, PG, Cosmos Ejovwoke. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, on the other hand, listed four members of his campaign organisation died. The competing accounts bring the number of claimed fatalities to seven, although the governor and police put the toll at six, pending investigations. This was as former Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Olukayode Ariwoola, retd., warned against a repeat of the deadly violence that followed the 2011 general elections, which claimed over 800 lives, urging political parties, security agencies and other stakeholders to take urgent steps to protect the 2027 electoral process. Also, 53 days to the presidential and National Assembly elections of January 16, 2027, the Kimpact Development Initiative, KDI, warned that the country was sliding towards violence, disclosing that its monitoring recorded 124 incidents of electoral violence, and 22 deaths across 35 states and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Abuja between July 1 and November 23, 2026. NDC boycotts IGP’s meeting The NDC, in a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, said it would not attend the meeting summoned by the IGP for chairmen and secretaries of registered political parties to address attacks on campaign rallies, destruction of campaign materials and threats to public peace. The party said it no longer felt protected by the police, accusing the force of watching helplessly while its members were attacked and killed. It called on the international community to compel President Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress, APC-led government to adhere to internationally accepted democratic standards. The statement read: “The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, condemns in the strongest terms the spate of violence orchestrated against its members across the country. “Therefore, the NDC has decided to boycott the security meeting called by the Inspector General of Police. We no longer feel safe and protected by a Police Force that watches helplessly the slaughter of our members across the country by hired thugs of the ruling APC. We will not lend legitimacy to a process that has failed to protect us. “The violence against NDC members has become an intolerable pattern across the length and breadth of Nigeria. “From Benue State, where our Presidential Candidate, Mr. Peter Obi, was prevented from entering the state by thugs loyal to the APC government, to Edo, Calabar, Enugu and the incessant attacks on our members in Delta State, the political temperature is on the rise, with campaigns turned into a battlefield. “Politics and campaigns are not supposed to be war. However, the APC government has turned the campaign into a battlefield, where lives have become nasty, brutish and uncertain. “The situation is compounded by the complicity of the police and security forces. The killing of four members of the NDC in Delta State was done in the full glare of the Police and security forces who were supposed to protect all Nigerians. Currently, the Nigeria Police has become an APC police sustained by taxpayers’ money. “The NDC and its members no longer feel safe and protected by the Police and security agencies, due to the manifest bias shown by their inability to carry out a proper investigation and make those responsible for the violence face the full wrath of the law.” Oborevwori orders arrest Governor Oborevwori, who visited Uduere, yesterday, to assess the situation and reassure residents, directed security agencies to identify and arrest all those involved in the killings. He had earlier held a security meeting with heads of security agencies at the Area Command Office in Ughelli. Those who accompanied him to the community included Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Etaifo Erale; Commander, 63 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Brigadier-General Ibrahim Buhari; the State Director of the Department of State Services, DSS, and other security officials. The governor described the killings as unfortunate and unacceptable, insisting that no political disagreement or ambition justified the loss of human lives. Warning that political activities must not become a source of insecurity, he said: “This must stop. It must stop. We cannot continue like this.” Oborevwori appealed to political leaders, supporters and other stakeholders to exercise restraint and shun political thuggery, stressing that peace and security were essential for economic growth and investment. He also directed the police and other security agencies to conduct a comprehensive investigation and ensure that all perpetrators were brought to justice. IGP orders impartial investigation In response, IGP Disu directed Delta State commissioner of police to immediately commence a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation into the attack. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, said in a statement that the investigation would establish the sequence of events, identify those responsible and examine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of police personnel at the venue. The police statement read: “The Nigeria Police Force strongly condemns the deadly violence that occurred on Monday, 23 November 2026, at Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, during a political campaign event. “The Force deeply regrets the loss of lives and injuries recorded and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families, while wishing the injured a speedy recovery. “The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. From the manufacturing clusters in Aba, Abia State, to the industrial workshops in Nnewi, Anambra State, the commercial centres of Onitsha, the business communities of Enugu and the productive enterprises of Imo and Ebonyi states, they all face the high cost and unreliability of electricity, forcing them to spend millions of naira to power their generators just to ensure that they remain in business. It has not been easy for a region whose economic strength is deeply rooted in entrepreneurship, manufacturing, commerce, and small-scale industries. Indeed, the energy challenge remains a major obstacle to industrial expansion as they spend huge resources powering their factories. All of them, including small businesses, struggle with rising operational costs. Will the proposed 400-kilometer South-East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project, with an initial investment budget of approximately $100 million, be a game changer for them? This initiative by the South-East Development Commission, SEDC, is planned to connect natural gas resources around the region to industrial and commercial centres across the five states in the region. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Chinedu Adonu For decades, businesses and industries across Nigeria’s South-East region have depended on generators for their daily operations at a high cost. From the manufacturing clusters in Aba, Abia State, to the industrial workshops in Nnewi, Anambra State, the commercial centres of Onitsha, the business communities of Enugu and the productive enterprises of Imo and Ebonyi states, they all face the high cost and unreliability of electricity, forcing them to spend millions of naira to power their generators just to ensure that they remain in business. It has not been easy for a region whose economic strength is deeply rooted in entrepreneurship, manufacturing, commerce, and small-scale industries. Indeed, the energy challenge remains a major obstacle to industrial expansion as they spend huge resources powering their factories. All of them, including small businesses, struggle with rising operational costs. Will the proposed 400-kilometer South-East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project, with an initial investment budget of approximately $100 million, be a game changer for them? This initiative by the South-East Development Commission, SEDC, is planned to connect natural gas resources around the region to industrial and commercial centres across the five states in the region. It was unveiled at the South- East Gas Infrastructure Investment and Project Development Ceremony in Enugu on October 27, 2026. The initiative is a partnership between SEDC and GasSync Limited, NNPC Gas Marketing Limited and other stakeholders. President Bola Tinubu, represented at the ceremony by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt., Hon. Benjamin Kalu, described the project as an important step towards addressing the infrastructure deficit which has constrained the productive capacity of the South-East region. “There is a sound familiar to every manufacturer in Aba, Nnewi, Onitsha, Enugu and across the South-East. It is the sound of a generator,” Tinubu noted, adding that the resilience of South-East entrepreneurs should no longer be an excuse for inadequate infrastructure. “Our manufacturers should not have to spend more on generating electricity than on expanding production. Our young entrepreneurs should not find that the greatest obstacle to their ambition is the cost of keeping their machines running,” he pointed out. According to the President, Nigeria’s natural gas resources should be measured not merely by what lies beneath the soil but by the factories they power, the jobs they create and the prosperity they bring. A 400-km economic corridor At the heart of the initiative is a proposed regional gas distribution network designed to connect the Assa North-Ohaji gas processing project in Imo State to major industrial and commercial centres across the South-East. Presenting the project details, GasSync representative, Callistus Mba explained that the pipeline would begin from the gas source around Assa North-Ohaji, extending to Owerri, Aba, Onitsha, Enugu and eventually, Ebonyi State. The proposed network, he explained, will cover approximately 400 kilometers, with construction expected to commence simultaneously from two major points to accelerate delivery. According to Mba, the construction strategy followed consultations with the Enugu State Government, which expressed concern that beginning from Imo and extending sequentially to the other states could prolong delivery. “We are going to start at Assa North and at Onitsha at the same time. We will construct from Onitsha to Enugu and Ebonyi while simultaneously working from Assa North to Owerri and Anambra,” he explained. The arrangement, he explained, is intended to fast-track construction and ensure that the northern sections of the network are developed alongside the southern corridors. The proposed infrastructure will comprise different pipeline sizes to accommodate the varying pressure requirements and distribution needs of the regional market. He explained that a 24-inch high-pressure pipeline would transport gas from the source to Owerri, while 18-inch pipelines would serve the regional distribution corridors. Smaller 12-inch pipelines would connect major industrial customers. The network, he further explained, will also incorporate city-gate facilities, pressure reduction and metering stations to ensure that gas is delivered at appropriate pressure levels and under safe operating conditions. Demand for gas already exists One of the major considerations behind the project is the growing demand for affordable and reliable energy among manufacturers and commercial establishments across the region. Mba disclosed that GasSync had identified more than 150 prospective customers across the five states, while surveys indicated potential demand of approximately 254 million standard cubic feet of gas per day. He noted that some businesses already depend on expensive virtual gas transportation arrangements, including compressed natural gas and liquefied natural gas delivered by road from other parts of the country. The proposed pipeline, he said, would provide a more direct and potentially cost-effective transportation option. “What GasSync is intended to do is ensure that there is a pipeline coming through so that these virtual pipelines, which are expensive and require delays in delivery, will be taken off,” Mba stated, saying that the company has identified prospective industrial customers in different states and is already engaging some of them on supply arrangements. According to him, in Abia, discussions are ongoing with Geometric Power, while other industrial customers have been identified in Imo and Anambra. In Enugu, the state government’s interest in reviving former industrial establishments, including ANAMMCO and the Niger Gas Company, presents additional opportunities for gas utilisation. Mba also disclosed that the company was making provisions to accommodate gas resources that could be developed within Enugu State, including the possibility of utilising coal-bed methane. In Ebonyi, the focus includes agro-processing and other gas-dependent enterprises. The company, he disclosed, has also identified additional potential gas supply connections around the region, including the Kwale Gas Processing Plant, activities around Obeaku/OB3 and other existing gas infrastructure. The initial phase requires approximately $100m Tinubu, in the course of his speech, noted that government could not finance every development ambition from the public treasury, stressing the need to deploy public resources strategically to attract larger pools of private capital. “This is the model I expect from our development institutions: identify strategic economic opportunities, prepare credible projects, commit public resources responsibly and mobilise private capital at a scale government budgets alone cannot achieve,” he stated. For the SEDC, the project is also consistent with the broader South-East Vision 2050 framework, which seeks to promote coordinated regional development and economic integration. A new future for South-East youths For Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah, the gas project represents an important opportunity to reposition the region as a competitive industrial and investment destination. He commended Tinubu for establishing the SEDC, describing it as a long-awaited institutional framework for the industrialisation of the South-East. Mbah said the investment agreement signed at the ceremony represented the commencement of the investment process and demonstrated the importance of bringing the private sector into regional infrastructure development. “What we have just signed here today is an investment agreement, meaning that investment has commenced,” the governor said. He described the financial arrangement as an innovative model that could bring together government institutions, private investors and other development partners to finance critical infrastructure.

item.title: Political Violence: Dying for nothing as a Nigerian politician?
item.description: By Jide Ajani From the First Republic to the Fourth, politicians have been murdered, opposition figures silenced and political supporters killed. Yet, beyond the initial outrage, Nigeria has perfected the art of forgetting its dead. What, then, is the value of dying for a political cause in a country that cannot even preserve the memory of its political martyrs? The alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State, brings this odd reality into focus once again. Worse, many innocent, ordinary Nigerians have lost their lives while supporting or opposing politicians, only becoming part of an unidentified statistical figure. There is something inescapably tragic about dying while politicking in Nigeria. You could spend a lifetime building a political movement, challenging an unjust system, defending an electoral mandate, or fighting for an idea about your country’s future – or just being loud for nothing like a former, two-time state governor from the South West, or a former Rep and Senator from the North Central. You could become a household name, command enormous political influence and acquire a place in the nation’s history. Then, one morning, gunmen arrive, bullets are fired, and your life is terminated. There will be outrage. Condemnations will pour in. Politicians will issue statements, newspapers will publish editorials (like this), civil society organisations will demand justice, and the police will announce investigations. And then, Nigeria happens, and the people move on. The murder will become another entry in the country’s expanding archive of unresolved political crimes. The victim’s name will gradually disappear from public conversations, except when anniversary commemorations provide an opportunity for political speeches. Even the circumstances of the death may eventually become blurred by competing narratives, political expediency and the convenient amnesia of a nation. Is it, therefore, worth dying for Nigeria’s politics? The question intends to interrogate a society that celebrates political martyrs without demonstrating a corresponding commitment to preserving their legacies or establishing the truth about their deaths. On Monday, November 23, 2026, four persons were killed during an alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere Community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State. Yet, beyond the initial outrage, Nigeria has perfected the art of forgetting its dead. What, then, is the value of dying for a political cause in a country that cannot even preserve the memory of its political martyrs? The alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State, brings this odd reality into focus once again. Worse, many innocent, ordinary Nigerians have lost their lives while supporting or opposing politicians, only becoming part of an unidentified statistical figure. There is something inescapably tragic about dying while politicking in Nigeria. You could spend a lifetime building a political movement, challenging an unjust system, defending an electoral mandate, or fighting for an idea about your country’s future – or just being loud for nothing like a former, two-time state governor from the South West, or a former Rep and Senator from the North Central. You could become a household name, command enormous political influence and acquire a place in the nation’s history. Then, one morning, gunmen arrive, bullets are fired, and your life is terminated. There will be outrage. Condemnations will pour in. Politicians will issue statements, newspapers will publish editorials (like this), civil society organisations will demand justice, and the police will announce investigations. And then, Nigeria happens, and the people move on. The murder will become another entry in the country’s expanding archive of unresolved political crimes. The victim’s name will gradually disappear from public conversations, except when anniversary commemorations provide an opportunity for political speeches. Even the circumstances of the death may eventually become blurred by competing narratives, political expediency and the convenient amnesia of a nation. Is it, therefore, worth dying for Nigeria’s politics? The question intends to interrogate a society that celebrates political martyrs without demonstrating a corresponding commitment to preserving their legacies or establishing the truth about their deaths. On Monday, November 23, 2026, four persons were killed during an alleged assassination attempt on the former Deputy Senate President, Ovie Omo-Agege, two days ago, in Uduere Community of Ughelli North LGA of Delta State. Over a dozen were said to have been injured. Mind you, in an outburst of emotive frustration about happenings inthe political sphere, the self-same Omo-Agege had used the phrase ‘ ig and die’. He was to later clarify that he was merely drawing attention to the need for credible elections. A bloody inheritance Political violence has accompanied Nigeria’s political evolution almost from independence. The January 15, 1966 military coup was a defining bloodbath. Among the prominent political victims were Prime Minister Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, Northern Premier Sir Ahmadu Bello, Western Premier Chief Samuel Ladoke Akintola and Federal Finance Minister Chief Festus Okotie-Eboh. They were not anonymous casualties. They occupied the commanding heights of the First Republic and represented competing political interests and constituencies. Their assassination, alongside the killing of senior military officers, fundamentally altered Nigeria’s political trajectory. The July 1966 counter-coup brought another round of killings, including Head of State Major-General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi and Western Region Governor Colonel Adekunle Fajuyi. Although these were killings arising from military coups and counter-coups rather than conventional electoral assassinations, they established a dangerous precedent: political disagreements and struggles for power could be settled through the elimination of human beings. On February 13, 1976, another military coup attempt claimed the life of Head of State General Murtala Mohammed. He was assassinated in Lagos by officers involved in the unsuccessful coup led by Lieutenant-Colonel Buka Suka Dimka. The military era also saw attacks on prominent government opponents. In October 1995, Chief Alfred Rewane, businessman, political financier and prominent supporter of the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO), was murdered in his Ikeja residence. The killing occurred during General Sani Abacha’s military dictatorship. The circumstances generated widespread suspicions of political motivation, but no satisfactory public resolution followed. The following year, on June 4, 1996, Kudirat Abiola was assassinated by unknown gunmen while travelling along the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway. She had become a prominent campaigner for the validation of her husband Moshood Abiola’s June 12, 1993 presidential mandate. Her murder was widely perceived as an attempt to silence the pro-democracy movement. Subsequent proceedings produced a conviction of Major Hamza al-Mustapha and another accused person, but the Court of Appeal overturned the convictions. The circumstances and ultimate accountability for her killing have remained contested. There were other disturbing incidents. Alex Ibru, publisher of The Guardian and a former minister, survived an assassination attempt in February 1996 after being shot in Lagos. Gani Fawehinmi, the human rights lawyer, was also the subject of a reported attack on the prison facility where he was detained, although he was not there at the time. The Fourth Republic: democracy and its dead The return to civilian government in 1999 raised expectations that constitutional politics would make political violence less attractive. Those expectations were soon tested. On December 19, 2001, Osun State legislator Odunayo Olagbaju was stabbed to death in Ile-Ife. Four days later, on December 23, Chief Bola Ige, the serving Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, was shot dead in his Bodija residence in Ibadan. Ige was a formidable politician, former governor of Oyo State, intellectual and prominent member of the Alliance for Democracy. His murder, against the background of the political crisis involving the governor and deputy governor of Osun State, sent shockwaves through the country. Several suspects were arrested and prosecuted, but the accused were discharged and acquitted in June 2004. The actual perpetrators have not been established through a successful prosecution. What happened to the national outrage that followed the murder of a sitting Attorney-General? On March 5, 2003, Harry Marshall, a senior opposition politician and national vice-chairman of the All Nigeria Peoples Party (ANPP), was murdered in his Abuja residence. Armed men reportedly forced their way into his home at about 3 a.m., tied up his security guard, and shot him in his bedroom. His killing occurred days before the commencement of the party’s presidential campaign. The police initially investigated extensively, but the motive was never conclusively established. Some suspected political connections; the authorities also considered armed robbery. In February 2004, Chief Aminasoari Dikibo, a prominent PDP national vice-chairman, was murdered while travelling in Delta State. His death generated allegations of political conspiracy, but no definitive public resolution emerged. Then came July 27, 2006. Engineer Funsho Williams, a prominent Lagos politician and governorship aspirant, was found murdered in his Ikoyi residence. His hands were reportedly tied, and the post-mortem evidence presented during the subsequent proceedings indicated death by strangulation. Several people were prosecuted. In 2014, however, a Lagos High Court discharged and acquitted the defendants after finding that the prosecution had failed to establish a sufficient connection between them and the murder. Another aspirant, Dr Ayo Daramola, was murdered at his home in Ekiti State in August

item.title: NRS seeks simpler tax rules for creative sector
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS) has called for simpler, clearer and business-friendly tax rules to unlock investment opportunities in Nigeria’s creative economy, stressing the need for a tax system that supports innovation, enterprise growth and wealth creation. The Service noted that the emergence of digital business models, intellectual property-driven enterprises and cross-border transactions required regulations that creators, entrepreneurs and investors could easily understand and navigate. Speaking at the just concluded high-level dialogue on taxation and investment in the creative economy during the Creative Africa Nexus (CANEX) event in Lagos, Executive Chairman of the NRS, Dr. Zacch Adedeji, described the creative economy as one of Nigeria’s most promising economic assets, noting that it had evolved beyond entertainment into a major source of employment, foreign exchange earnings, investment and economic opportunities. Adedeji who was represented by the Executive Director, People, Stakeholders and Communication, Mr. Obinna Ihedioha, also said that digital platforms had transformed how creative value was produced and commercialised, with entrepreneurs building businesses around copyrights, designs, brands and digital products. He reiterated that tax administration must evolve to accommodate these developments without discouraging innovation or business expansion. “The government needs sustainable revenue to invest in education, security, technology and infrastructure. But how we tax matters as much as what we collect. It shapes whether businesses start, whether investors come, and whether enterprises grow or stay small,” he said. Adedeji added that the new tax laws offered an opportunity to establish a more efficient system through clearer regulations, reduced compliance burdens for small businesses and improved taxpayer support. He identified clarity, understanding and value as essential to effective taxation, stressing that formalisation should provide creative businesses with tangible benefits, including access to finance, contracts, investment, wider markets and legal protection. The NRS, he said, participated in CANEX through a high-level dialogue, an Investment and Tax Advisory Hub for creators and investors, and the Creative Economy Tax and Investment Initiative (CETII), designed to sustain engagement beyond the event. The post NRS seeks simpler tax rules for creative sector appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Edo Police parades security operative for allegedly leaking information to cultists
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — THE Edo State Police Command said four members of the Edo State Security Corps, ESSC, have been arrested for allegedly leaking information to suspected cultists to enable them evade arrests. The Command’s spokesperson, Eno Ikoedem, disclosed this while parading 16 suspects arrested across the state in connection with various criminal activities. The suspects, Isaac Irú we, Ashem Gideon, Tony Okhiale and Venture Uzu were arrested at Evbhomore community, in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of the state. They were accused of leaking information on police movements to cultists, enabling them to escape arrest. According to the Command, operatives of the Anti-Cultism Unit acted on intelligence on cult initiation activities in Benin City and immediately swung into action. “Upon getting there, we discovered that someone was giving out information on our movement to these cultists who escaped arrest. “Further investigation revealed that these men are members of the Edo State Security Corps, and four of them have been arrested and they are in our custody.” The command said investigation was still ongoing to ascertain their roles in the secret cult organisation. Vanguard News The post Edo Police parades security operative for allegedly leaking information to cultists appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Petrol imports crash 52% as crude, wheat top Lagos ports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Imports of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), also known as petrol, through Lagos ports plunged by 52.23 per cent in November, while crude oil and bulk wheat ranked among the leading commodities imported through the ports in October and November. According to the Shipping Position document obtained from the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), PMS imports fell to 73,895 metric tonnes in November from 328,231 metric tonnes recorded in October. Crude oil imports through Lagos ports also dropped sharply, with 702,254 metric tonnes recorded in October, while no crude oil import was recorded in November. Bulk wheat ranked among the major commodities imported through Lagos ports during the period, with a combined 461,190 metric tonnes recorded in September, October and November. The breakdown showed that wheat imports rose to 252,348 metric tonnes in October and declined by 17.24 per cent to 208,842 metric tonnes in November. item.title: Osun man tortures 21-yr-old son to death over N75,000, phone
item.description: By Shina Abubakar Osogbo —The Osun State Police Command has said it arrested a 48-year-old man, Ogunniran Kayode over alleged murder of his son, Raphael, at Faaji, Odo-Otin Local Government Area of the state. A statement by the command’s Public Relations Officer, Abiodun Ojelabi, yesterday, stated that the police received intelligence on October 19, 2026, that the suspect tortured his 21-year-old son to death. Then he buried his body in a shallow grave. Following the intel, the statement disclosed that the operatives of the command swung into action and arrested the suspect as he confessed to the killing of his son. “During the interrogation, he stated that his son stole a sum of N75,000 and absconded with one android phone he bought for him on easy buy to an unknown place. “And being a member of Iru-Ekun Security Network, he was able to get the son arrested through the help of his colleague.” “The case was then transferred to Homicide Section for further investigation”, the statement added. Meanwhile, operatives of the homicide unit visisted the crime scene and the shallow grave, where details and pictorial evidence of the torture were retrieved. The state Police Commissioner, Ibrahim Zungura, therefore, warned individuals with criminal intent to desist from the act or face full wrath of the law. Vanguard News The post Osun man tortures 21-yr-old son to death over N75,000, phone appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Access Bank, Deloitte train SMEs on business sustainability
item.description: By Efe Onodjae & Jacintha Ezugwu Access Bank has urged small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to embrace sustainable business practices to ensure their survival and growth beyond their first five years. The Head of SME Banking Group at Access Bank Plc, Mrs Abiodun Olubitan, gave the advice at the three-day Access Bank SME Academy 2.0, organised in partnership with Deloitte to equip business owners with skills to improve their operations and sustainability. The programme, which ended on Friday in Lagos, attracted about 100 SME owners physically, with others participating virtually. It targeted businesses that had operated for between two and five years. Olubitan said SMEs were critical to economic development, noting that their survival and expansion were necessary for job creation and national growth. She urged participants to apply the knowledge acquired, particularly in separating personal finances from business accounts and understanding the difference between turnover and profit. According to her, the bank introduced the academy to support businesses at different stages of growth and help them overcome challenges that often threaten their survival. In her part, Team Lead, SME Banking Products at Access Bank and coordinator of the academy, Adesola Oyedipe, said the initiative was designed to address gaps in access to finance and capacity building among SMEs. Oyedipe said the three-day programme provided participants with more extensive training than the bank’s usual short workshops and business clinics. She explained that the partnership with Deloitte was aimed at giving business owners access to professional advisory services they might otherwise be unable to afford. The post Access Bank, Deloitte train SMEs on business sustainability appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: No missing funds in $2.04bn Duke Oil crude cargoes — NNPC
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) has dismissed reports alleging that $2.04 billion realised from crude oil cargoes lifted by Duke Oil Company Incorporated, now NNPC Trading S.A., was unaccounted for, insisting that all transactions were fully reconciled. The company said the $2.04 billion represented the gross value of 29 cargoes whose proceeds were set off against the cost of refined petroleum products supplied to Nigeria under the Direct Sale Direct Purchase (DSDP) programme. In a statement by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, NNPC said the absence of separate dollar receipts for some cargoes did not indicate missing funds. “No separate receipt appears because the crude sale proceeds were set off against the product purchase price, as the contracts provide,” it stated. Under the DSDP programme, participating traders lifted crude oil in exchange for refined petroleum products, including petrol, for the Nigerian market. NNPC explained that while crude was priced in dollars, products supplied were sold in naira, with transactions reconciled and captured in the audited financial statements of the relevant entities. The company said all 59 cargoes referenced in the reports were accounted for, adding that 30 were paid for in dollars, while proceeds from 28 cargoes, valued at approximately $1.96 billion, were remitted in naira to the NNPC Group Treasury or NNPC Upstream Investment Management Services accounts. The remaining cargo, a February 2023 Bonga tax-oil lifting valued at about $75.9 million, was paid into the then designated Federal Inland Revenue Service dollar account. On Duke Oil’s ownership, NNPC said it was incorporated in 1989 as its wholly owned trading subsidiary, adding that the relationship was documented in its corporate history, audited financial statements and NEITI’s 2023 industry report. It maintained that transactions between the company and its subsidiaries were disclosed as related-party transactions under International Financial Reporting Standards. NNPC reaffirmed its commitment to transparency and accountability, but warned that it reserved the right to take legal action against publications it considered false or misleading. The post No missing funds in $2.04bn Duke Oil crude cargoes — NNPC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: CBN holds MPR at 23%, says external reserves drop temporary
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, dismissing concerns over a decline of over $300 million in external reserves as a temporary, seasonal movement. Governor of the CBN, Mr. Olayemi Cardoso, disclosed this yesterday at a press conference announcing the outcome of the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) in Abuja. The bank also retained the standing facilities corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR, Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and Non-TSA public sector deposits at 75 per cent. Explaining the decision to retain the policy rate, Cardoso said: “In reaching its decision, the committee acknowledged the continued decline in headline inflation, but remained mindful of lingering upside risks, particularly those arising from the ongoing Middle East conflict, which could sustain pressure on energy prices. “In addition, the MPC observed that the anticipated increase in spending from the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities could impact aggregate demand with likely upward pressure on prices. “Nevertheless, the committee judged that maintaining the current policy stance is appropriate to safeguard the gains of disinflation so far achieved, while remaining data-dependent and vigilant in taking further appropriate measures.” He added that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply associated with the harvest season would further strengthen the disinflation process. Cardoso said headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, reflecting sustained exchange rate stability and improved monetary policy transmission. “However, given the prevailing headwinds, which have slowed the pace of moderation in price pressures, members were of the view that maintaining the current policy stance would further anchor inflation expectations and support the disinflation process,” he said. On concerns over the decline in external reserves by over $300 million, Cardoso said the movement was not a source of worry, describing it as seasonal. “Our reserves is in a very strong position. So, that, I want to say, has not changed. And in actual fact, I believe it will continue to improve. What you mention is something that is transient,” he said. He explained that portfolio investors tend to recalibrate their positions towards year-end, while domestic users also increase demand for foreign exchange to hedge against future uncertainties. “These are all seasonal issues. And of course, with the elections coming, there’s more spending that is going on. These are all seasonal. And we believe very strongly that as we go into the next year, we will find a major moderation in the volatility that you have seen,” he said. item.content:encoded: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, dismissing concerns over a decline of over $300 million in external reserves as a temporary, seasonal movement. The bank also retained the standing facilities corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR, Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and Non-TSA public sector deposits at 75 per cent. Explaining the decision to retain the policy rate, Cardoso said: “In reaching its decision, the committee acknowledged the continued decline in headline inflation, but remained mindful of lingering upside risks, particularly those arising from the ongoing Middle East conflict, which could sustain pressure on energy prices. “In addition, the MPC observed that the anticipated increase in spending from the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities could impact aggregate demand with likely upward pressure on prices. “Nevertheless, the committee judged that maintaining the current policy stance is appropriate to safeguard the gains of disinflation so far achieved, while remaining data-dependent and vigilant in taking further appropriate measures.” He added that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply associated with the harvest season would further strengthen the disinflation process. Cardoso said headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, reflecting sustained exchange rate stability and improved monetary policy transmission. “However, given the prevailing headwinds, which have slowed the pace of moderation in price pressures, members were of the view that maintaining the current policy stance would further anchor inflation expectations and support the disinflation process,” he said. On concerns over the decline in external reserves by over $300 million, Cardoso said the movement was not a source of worry, describing it as seasonal. “Our reserves is in a very strong position. So, that, I want to say, has not changed. And in actual fact, I believe it will continue to improve. What you mention is something that is transient,” he said. And of course, with the elections coming, there’s more spending that is going on. These are all seasonal. And we believe very strongly that as we go into the next year, we will find a major moderation in the volatility that you have seen,” he said. Cardoso disclosed that gross external reserves stood at $54.02 billion as of November 17, 2026, sufficient to cover 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. He also cited a current account surplus and diaspora remittances of over $900 million in the latest month as supporting external buffers. “I want to assure all Nigerians that the Central Bank of Nigeria will do everything that is possible to ensure that that stability, that hard-earned stability, will continue,” he said. item.title: Tears as victims of Bayelsa boat mishap get mass burial
item.description: By Emem Idio YENAGOA — It was tears and wailing at the Azikoro Cemetery in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, yesterday, as victims of Friday’s boat mishap in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of the state, were laid to rest in a mass burial. The burial, which commenced at about 11am, ended at 4pm, when the last batch of bodies, wrapped in black plastic bags, were brought to the cemetery in ambulances. The exercise was supervised by the Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Nimibofa Ayawei, and the Commissioner for Environment, Mr. Ebi Ololo, alongside other government officials. The cemetery was enveloped by a foul stench from the bodies, some of which had begun to decompose, as grieving relatives, friends and sympathisers gathered to witness the burial. Many mourners broke down in tears, while others stood in groups, speaking in hushed tones as the remains of their loved ones were lowered into shallow graves. One of the bereaved relatives, Timipreye Diepreye, who said she lost seven family members in the tragedy, faulted the manner in which relatives were informed about the mass burial. She said the family would have made arrangements for coffins for their deceased relatives, particularly those whose bodies were recovered on Friday, if they had been adequately informed ahead of the exercise. Also speaking, the Chairman of the Community Development Committee, CDC, of Ukubie community, Mr. Ruben Kemelate, said the tragedy had plunged the entire community into mourning, with hardly any family left untouched by the loss. Kemelate, who disclosed that his elder sister also died at the Federal Medical Centre, said the scale of the tragedy had left the community devastated. He said: “We are in a very sad mood. Every family is affected. There is no family that is not affected. Like me particularly, my elder sister died in the FMC. So, every family is in a sad mood. We are in a very sad mood as a community. “So far so good, we have recovered 35 bodies and we have buried 29. We buried one on the first day, one seven-year-old boy. And today (yesterday) we have buried 28 corpses. Vanguard News The post Tears as victims of Bayelsa boat mishap get mass burial appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Campaign Violence: INEC awaits police case files to prosecute offenders
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has asked the Nigeria Police Force to speed up the arrest, investigation and transmission of case files against perpetrators of campaign violence, so the Commission can prosecute them directly. The INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, SAN, said swift action was necessary so that “impunity is decisively checked before January.” He spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the Inspector General of Police’s Interactive Session with Chairmen and Secretaries of Political Parties on a peaceful electoral process before, during and after the 2027 General Elections. The session held at the Goodluck Ebele Jonathan Peace Conference Hall, Force Headquarters. According to a statement by the commission, last night, Amupitan said INEC was “deeply concerned by isolated incidents of campaign violence, intimidation, and attacks on political rivals, journalists, and electoral facilities.” No election, office, or partisan interest is worth the loss of a single Nigerian life. Achieving a peaceful political environment is a collective national responsibility, not the duty of a single institution”, he added. He said the Electoral Act 2026 had “significantly strengthened legal deterrence,” adding that Sections 96 and 97 prohibit inciting campaign rhetoric and ban the use of thugs, private armed guards or masquerades at political rallies. According to him, the Act prescribes penalties of up to ₦5 million or twelve months’ imprisonment for individuals, and up to ₦10 million for political parties, on initial breaches. “Under Section 148, INEC is empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receipt of completed case files,” he said, explaining the Commission’s request for prompt transmission of the files by the Police. The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission remained distinct from security agencies. “INEC is not a security agency; it lacks both the constitutional mandate and operational capacity to maintain public order, arrest offenders, or provide armed security,” he said. He said Section 95 of the Electoral Act assigns the duty of securing political rallies to the Police. The Section also mandates the Commissioner of Police in each state and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to provide adequate security for rallies and processions, with support from the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, and other federal security agencies. Amupitan reminded political parties that INEC guidelines required them to notify the commissioner of police in writing of rally venues and times, and to submit the details to the Commission at least ten days in advance. He appealed to political leaders “to refrain from seeking political support by creating fear,” urging them instead to “earn public confidence through integrity and transparency.” In his remarks, the Inspector General of Police IGP, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, said recent violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues

Achieving a peaceful political environment is a collective national responsibility, not the duty of a single institution”, he added. He said the Electoral Act 2026 had “significantly strengthened legal deterrence,” adding that Sections 96 and 97 prohibit inciting campaign rhetoric and ban the use of thugs, private armed guards or masquerades at political rallies. According to him, the Act prescribes penalties of up to ₦5 million or twelve months’ imprisonment for individuals, and up to ₦10 million for political parties, on initial breaches. “Under Section 148, INEC is empowered to prosecute electoral offenders directly upon receipt of completed case files,” he said, explaining the Commission’s request for prompt transmission of the files by the Police. The INEC chairman stressed that the Commission remained distinct from security agencies. “INEC is not a security agency; it lacks both the constitutional mandate and operational capacity to maintain public order, arrest offenders, or provide armed security,” he said. He said Section 95 of the Electoral Act assigns the duty of securing political rallies to the Police. The Section also mandates the Commissioner of Police in each state and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) to provide adequate security for rallies and processions, with support from the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, and other federal security agencies. Amupitan reminded political parties that INEC guidelines required them to notify the commissioner of police in writing of rally venues and times, and to submit the details to the Commission at least ten days in advance. He appealed to political leaders “to refrain from seeking political support by creating fear,” urging them instead to “earn public confidence through integrity and transparency.” In his remarks, the Inspector General of Police IGP, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, said recent violent clashes among political supporters, attacks on campaign venues and convoys, and the use of dangerous weapons had become matters of serious concern. He described these developments as “warning signs that must be addressed decisively before they escalate into a broader threat to national security.” The IGP declared that the Police have “zero tolerance for political violence, irrespective of the political party, candidate, personality or interest involved,” adding that the Force’s neutrality in the political process “is non-negotiable.” Disu said those who sponsor, finance or direct political violence “will be treated with the same seriousness as those who carry them out.” He assured participants that the Police would “protect the rights of all lawful political actors to organise rallies, hold meetings and participate in the democratic process.” The IGP, however, that the Force would “not hesitate to take lawful and decisive action against anyone who engages in thuggery, intimidation, assault, the use of offensive weapons or any conduct capable of disrupting public peace.” Vanguard News The post Campaign Violence: INEC awaits police case files to prosecute offenders appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: South-East governors working for my re-election — Tinubu
item.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — AHEAD of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu, on Monday, told the Igbo community and their leaders, in Lagos, that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election. The President said he was excited and that he would go home happy and eat because of their endorsement of his second term. He thanked the Igbo communities and business leaders in Lagos for their resolve to support his re-election on January 16, 2027. He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians. President Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing youths, elders, and Ndigbo leaders during a town hall meeting organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos State. He called on Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics, and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous and united Nigeria. To reaffirm his commitment to national unity, President Tinubu joined the gathering to sing the national anthem a second time. “I didn’t believe you would turn out this many; I am very, very happy. May God bless you, and may God continue to guide and bless our country. “It is a great honour for me to be here before you as your president. I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria. “Though tribes and tongues may differ, we stand in brotherhood. None of us told God where we would be born or what language we would speak when we were born. “Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no control over yourself. God created you and created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians. “Let’s see ourselves as individuals living in the same house geographically called Nigeria,” the President told the gathering. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — AHEAD of the January 16 presidential election, President Bola Tinubu, on Monday, told the Igbo community and their leaders, in Lagos, that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election. The President said he was excited and that he would go home happy and eat because of their endorsement of his second term. He thanked the Igbo communities and business leaders in Lagos for their resolve to support his re-election on January 16, 2027. He assured them of his administration’s commitment to inclusive governance, national unity and equity for all Nigerians. President Tinubu gave the assurance while addressing youths, elders, and Ndigbo leaders during a town hall meeting organised by the Ndigbo National Dialogue and Development Initiatives at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts, Iganmu, Lagos State. He called on Ndigbo to strengthen their unity, deepen their participation in national politics, and work with other ethnic groups to build a peaceful, prosperous and united Nigeria. To reaffirm his commitment to national unity, President Tinubu joined the gathering to sing the national anthem a second time. “I didn’t believe you would turn out this many; I am very, very happy. May God bless you, and may God continue to guide and bless our country. “It is a great honour for me to be here before you as your president. I can commit to one thing: the unity of Nigeria. “Though tribes and tongues may differ, we stand in brotherhood. None of us told God where we would be born or what language we would speak when we were born. “Whether you are Igbo or Hausa, you have no control over yourself. God created you and created that opportunity. We are all Nigerians. “Let’s see ourselves as individuals living in the same house geographically called Nigeria,” the President told the gathering. A statement by the presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, said: “President Tinubu told the gathering that all the South-East governors are with him on the journey to make Nigeria a better place and are working for his re-election.” He mentioned Chief Chidi Anyaegbu, owner of Chisco Motors; Dave Umahi; Doris Uzoka-Anite; and Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, who were at the gathering, as people with whom he has close connections. On his part, the host Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, appealed to Ndigbo to support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, assuring the President of massive votes from the state in the January 16, 2027, presidential election. Sanwo-Olu described the turnout of Igbo leaders, traders and business owners as proof that Lagos residents were united behind the President, despite the meeting being held on a Monday, when many participants had to leave their businesses to attend. In her remarks, the convener of the meeting and Minister of State for Budget and Economic Planning, Dr. Doris Uzoka-Anite, declared the Igbo community’s commitment in Lagos State to supporting President Tinubu’s re-election bid, saying the community had resolved to unite behind his leadership. She said that Ndigbo had commenced grassroots mobilisation across Lagos State, with structures established at the polling-unit level ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Also speaking, the former Minister of State for Labour and Employment, Nkeiruka Onyejeocha, assured President Bola Tinubu of Ndigbo’s support for his 2027 re-election bid, saying the gathering of Igbo leaders and stakeholders in Lagos demonstrated their unity and commitment to the President. She said the community had recognised the importance of building political alliances with other geo-political zones to achieve its future presidential ambition. The leader of the Ndigbo Traders Association in Lagos, Prince Tony Nwakeze, pledged the members’ support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, while appealing for access to loans at a 5 per cent interest rate to help traders transition from importation to local manufacturing. Nwakeze said traders from Alaba, Trade Fair and Ladipo markets were seeking financial support to empower young people and expand their businesses. He also assured the President that traders were prepared to organise themselves and adopt a cross-guarantee arrangement to ensure repayment of any loans granted to their members. “We, the market people, will stand with you, support you and honour every agreement we enter into today,” he said. item.title: Greenwich Bank opens Warri, Uyo branches, targets five more cities
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Greenwich Bank Limited has opened branches in Warri, Delta State, and Uyo, Akwa Ibom State, as it targets five additional cities in its nationwide expansion drive. The new outlets bring its physical network to seven, following the opening of five branches in Lagos, Ondo and Ekiti states in October. The Bank plans to extend its operations to Asaba, Port Harcourt, Abuja, Benin and Ibadan in the coming months. Speaking at the commissioning of the Warri branch, Group Chairman of Greenwich Holdings, Kayode Falowo, described the Niger Delta as a strategic market, citing its economic importance and entrepreneurial potential, particularly in oil and gas, maritime services and logistics. He said: “Warri’s economic prospects extend beyond its natural resources to the entrepreneurs, traders, contractors, service providers and other businesses driving commercial activities in the region.” At the Uyo branch commissioning, Chairman of Greenwich Bank, Segun Oloketuyi, said the commercial banking licence would enable the institution to extend its 32 years of financial services experience to farmers, traders, civil servants, students and entrepreneurs. He identified credit facilities, agricultural and SME financing, trade and treasury services, salary solutions and digital banking as key offerings. Delta State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Fidelis Telije, urged residents, particularly small businesses, young entrepreneurs and women-owned enterprises, to take advantage of the Bank’s services. Similarly, Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, represented by Commissioner for Finance, Emem Almond Bob, said the Uyo branch would improve access to banking services and credit, support business growth and potentially boost the state’s internally generated revenue. Managing Director of Greenwich Bank, Benson Ogundeji, said the branches would deepen customer engagement and bring financial solutions closer to businesses and individuals. He identified oil and gas, maritime services, agriculture, manufacturing, trade, logistics and SMEs as priority sectors, adding that the Bank would combine physical branches with technology-driven solutions to promote enterprise growth and financial inclusion. Greenwich Holdings has over three decades of financial services experience, with interests in commercial banking, capital markets, asset management and securities. item.title: Bellingham beauty in Real Madrid win; Arsenal, Man City held in Champions League
item.description: Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season’s Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home. Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued their excellent form since the start of the league phase, but Aston Villa slumped to another defeat on their travels. Record 15-time European champions Real had to come from behind to beat PSV at the Bernabeu as they made it five wins from five in this season’s league phase to go clear at the top of the standings with 15 points. Dutch champions PSV led at half-time courtesy of an Ivan Perisic penalty, but Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the restart. Bellingham then put Real ahead on the hour with a remarkable strike, as he controlled a Kylian Mbappe lay-off outside the box and then teed himself up for a sweet volley on the outside of his right boot which flew into the corner of the net. Mbappe then scored twice to move to 19 goals in all competitions this season and 76 career Champions League goals. The France captain now has 105 Real Madrid goals, one more than the Brazilian Ronaldo managed for the club. Vinicius Junior sealed the win for Jose Mourinho’s side, who have now claimed 10 consecutive victories in all competitions. “That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and then I just hit it. I thought I would go with the outside of the boot a little bit, stab it a little bit, I am not one for smashing the ball too hard. It was a nice moment,” England star Bellingham told British broadcaster TNT Sports about his goal. Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain can join Real at the top of the standings if they beat Roma on Wednesday, but Como and Betis are currently level with the French side on 12 points after they beat AEK Athens and Slovan Bratislava respectively. Como and Betis flying Luis Milla scored as Como beat AEK 1-0 in Italy after Lucas Da Cunha earlier squandered a penalty, while Cucho Hernandez grabbed both goals for Betis in their 2-0 victory in Slovakia. Arsenal had to settle for a point after drawing 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres put the Gunners ahead but later missed a golden chance to win the game. Gyokeres opened the scoring with a thunderous strike, but Maximilian Beier equalised for Dortmund and the Arsenal striker headed woefully wide from Martin Odegaard’s cross late on. It is the second time Arsenal, last season’s beaten finalists, have dropped points to German opposition this season following a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich. Manchester City are in the midst of a poor run of form in the Premier League and Enzo Maresca’s side had to come from behind twice in the second half to draw 2-2 against Napoli. It is the second time Arsenal, last season’s beaten finalists, have dropped points to German opposition this season following a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich. Manchester City are in the midst of a poor run of form in the Premier League and Enzo Maresca’s side had to come from behind twice in the second half to draw 2-2 against Napoli. Rasmus Hojlund, formerly of Manchester United, gave the Italians the lead early in the second half only for Ayyoub Bouaddi to equalise. Kevin De Bruyne was returning to face his former side and he saw his Napoli team retake the lead through Noa Lang in the 76th minute, but Rayan Cherki’s fine late goal earned City a point. City won 10 of their first 11 games this season under Maresca. But the wheels have come off in the wake of the club being found guilty of widespread breaches of Premier League financial rules. Aston Villa lose “We don’t like these moments – we want to win games – but unfortunately this moment is like this,” said Maresca, ahead of a trip to Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday. None of the Premier League’s representatives in the competition won on Tuesday, with Villa losing 1-0 to Galatasaray in Istanbul as Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game late on. The two clubs are now level on nine points in the standings. Portuguese champions Porto won 1-0 at Feyenoord thanks to Oussama Targhalline’s early own-goal, while Antonio Nusa netted twice as RB Leipzig beat Lens 3-1 — that was a fourth straight Champions League loss for the French team. A stoppage-time own-goal gave Bodo/Glimt a 1-0 victory against Austria’s LASK in Norway. item.title: Bakassi Port, border reforms to unlock Cross River’s economic potential – Customs boss
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, has said the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port and planned modernisation of strategic border corridors will unlock Cross River State’s economic potential, boost regional commerce and reposition the state as a major gateway for international trade. Adeniyi, who spoke at the 6th AfSNET Investment Conference 2026 in Calabar, Cross River State, said the state was on the path to reclaiming its historic position as one of Nigeria’s foremost commercial hubs. He described the groundbreaking ceremony for the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port as a significant milestone that could transform the economic fortunes of Cross River State and strengthen its participation in international trade. Reflecting on Calabar’s commercial heritage, the Customs boss recalled that the city once hosted Nigeria’s busiest Customs port, noting that its trading history dated back approximately a century. He also highlighted that Nigeria’s first indigenous and longest-serving Comptroller-General of Customs hailed from Calabar, underscoring the state’s historic contribution to the Service and the country’s commercial development. Adeniyi expressed optimism that the proposed port, alongside the modernisation of strategic border corridors, would create opportunities for investment, expand exports, generate employment and stimulate economic activities across the region. However, he stressed that infrastructure development must be accompanied by operational reforms, noting that the construction of ports and border facilities alone would not eliminate existing trade bottlenecks. He disclosed that the Nigeria Customs Service had conducted a Time Release Study to determine how long it takes to process consignments at the ports and identify areas requiring improvement in cargo clearance. The Customs CG also identified the establishment of effective One-Stop Border Posts at the Mfum-Ekok and Seme borders as critical to improving cross-border trade, eliminating duplicate examinations and reducing cargo clearance delays. According to him, effective implementation of the initiative could increase trade volumes by as much as 70 per cent.
