item.dc:creator: Urowayino Jeremiah
item.content:encoded: By Godwin Oritse The Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, has said the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port and planned modernisation of strategic border corridors will unlock Cross River State’s economic potential, boost regional commerce and reposition the state as a major gateway for international trade. Adeniyi, who spoke at the 6th AfSNET Investment Conference 2026 in Calabar, Cross River State, said the state was on the path to reclaiming its historic position as one of Nigeria’s foremost commercial hubs. He described the groundbreaking ceremony for the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port as a significant milestone that could transform the economic fortunes of Cross River State and strengthen its participation in international trade. Reflecting on Calabar’s commercial heritage, the Customs boss recalled that the city once hosted Nigeria’s busiest Customs port, noting that its trading history dated back approximately a century. He also highlighted that Nigeria’s first indigenous and longest-serving Comptroller-General of Customs hailed from Calabar, underscoring the state’s historic contribution to the Service and the country’s commercial development. Adeniyi expressed optimism that the proposed port, alongside the modernisation of strategic border corridors, would create opportunities for investment, expand exports, generate employment and stimulate economic activities across the region. However, he stressed that infrastructure development must be accompanied by operational reforms, noting that the construction of ports and border facilities alone would not eliminate existing trade bottlenecks. He disclosed that the Nigeria Customs Service had conducted a Time Release Study to determine how long it takes to process consignments at the ports and identify areas requiring improvement in cargo clearance. The Customs CG also identified the establishment of effective One-Stop Border Posts at the Mfum-Ekok and Seme borders as critical to improving cross-border trade, eliminating duplicate examinations and reducing cargo clearance delays. According to him, effective implementation of the initiative could increase trade volumes by as much as 70 per cent. He explained that modernising the border corridors would require supporting infrastructure, including warehouses, storage facilities, weighbridges and scanners, to improve cargo handling, operational efficiency and border management. Adeniyi said the Service had studied successful models of modern border operations in other countries, expressing confidence that proven practices could be adapted to Nigeria’s operating environment. He also emphasised the need to maximise the deployment of non-intrusive inspection technology, particularly scanners, to facilitate legitimate trade, minimise unnecessary physical examinations and strengthen enforcement against smuggling and other illicit activities. On trade compliance, the Customs boss disclosed that the Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) programme had facilitated the recovery of approximately N200 billion through improved compliance. He acknowledged the support of the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank) in advancing trade development and modernisation initiatives, while stressing the importance of stronger partnerships among government institutions, financial organisations and private-sector operators. He maintained that government alone could not provide all the resources required to create sustainable wealth, calling for greater private-sector participation in developing trade infrastructure and unlocking investment opportunities. The Customs CG further noted that Customs administrations must strike a balance between facilitating legitimate trade and enforcing regulations to prevent smuggling and other illegal activities. He expressed confidence that with the right partnerships, investments and institutional commitment, Nigeria could build a more efficient, transparent and competitive trade environment. For Cross River State, the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port and the planned modernisation of the Mfum-Ekok border corridor are expected to strengthen its position as a strategic trade gateway, with opportunities to expand regional commerce, attract investment, boost exports and create jobs. Meanwhile, the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS), Cross River/CFTZ/Akwa Ibom Area Command, has pledged collaboration with government agencies and other stakeholders to support the development of the proposed Bakassi Deep Sea Port and facilitate legitimate trade in the region. The Acting Customs Area Controller of the Command, Deputy Comptroller Nkiruka Nwala, gave the assurance when he joined service chiefs and heads of government agencies to receive Vice President Kashim Shettima at the Margaret Ekpo International Airport, Calabar, ahead of the port’s groundbreaking ceremony. Shettima was in Cross River State on Friday, November 13, 2026, for the groundbreaking ceremony of the proposed deep sea port, an infrastructure project expected to expand the state’s maritime capacity, attract private investment and create employment opportunities. The Vice President also participated in the 6th AfSNET Investment Conference 2026 in Calabar, where stakeholders deliberated on investment, trade and economic development. The airport reception brought together service chiefs, heads of security agencies and other government officials ahead of the Vice President’s scheduled engagements in the state. Nwala’s participation, according to the Command, underscored its commitment to inter-agency cooperation and readiness to work with relevant government institutions and stakeholders to advance the port project and maximise its economic benefits. The Command reaffirmed its commitment to discharging its statutory responsibilities in revenue generation, border security, trade facilitation and the protection of Nigeria’s economic interests, while supporting initiatives capable of promoting legitimate trade, investment and regional economic growth. It added that effective collaboration among government agencies and other stakeholders would be critical to ensuring that the proposed port and associated trade infrastructure deliver their expected economic benefits. item.title: We have a workable blueprint to take Zamfara to greater heights – Governor Lawal
item.description: Governor Dauda Lawal said the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) has the blueprint to address all pending socio-economic and infrastructural issues in Zamfara State. The governor disclosed this on Monday during the launch of the APC Presidential and Gubernatorial Campaign for the 2027 general elections in Talata Mafara, Zamfara State. “We have a workable blueprint, as you all can testify to, and I will continue to do more if re-elected as the governor of Zamfara State,” the governor said to a rousing applause of thousands of supporters at the rally. In his remarks at the rally, Governor Lawal expressed satisfaction with the turnout and gratitude to the people of Talata Mafara for the grand reception. He highlighted key projects implemented by his administration in the Talata Mafara Local Government Area. He said, “I am here today to flag off the Presidential and Gubernatorial campaign of the APC, seeking your votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and for myself as your governor. “I am also here to seek your support to vote for the APC from top to bottom. And from what we have seen today, I am sure that Mafara is for the APC. “I have executed more than 40 projects in Talata Mafara LGA, which include the total rebuilding and equipping of the General Hospital, and many other projects in the State University.” Governor Lawal assured supporters of his administration’s resolve to build infrastructure and address all other basic human and socio-economic challenges facing the state. He also appealed to the youths, women and all other supporters to vote for the APC candidates from the president to the state house of assembly in the state The Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, said he was overwhelmed by the unprecedented crowd of supporters who graced the event. Senator Yari appealed to the APC supporters to vote for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Lawal and all other candidates of the party in the 2027 general elections. The city of Mafara was agog during the campaign rally held at the main Eid Ground in the Talata Mafara Local Government Area. The rally brought together major APC stakeholders in the state, including Mr Yari, and former governors Ahmad Sani Yarima and Mahmud Aliyu Shinkafi, among others. The party’s stakeholders were welcomed by thousands of APC members and supporters, attesting to Governor Lawal’s popularity in the state. The post We have a workable blueprint to take Zamfara to greater heights – Governor Lawal appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Dell and HPE both say they’ve become ‘different companies’
item.description: Dell and HPE this week both told investors they’ve become “different companies.” The two hardware giants made that assertion on their respective earnings calls this week. HPE went first, on Monday, when CEO Antonio Neri declared “We are now a fundamentally different company” after acquiring Juniper Networks and creating products “built to capitalize on the next phase of AI.” On Tuesday, Dell’s chief operating officer and vice chairman Jeff Clarke declared “We are now a different company” because the Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) has become the source of “the vast majority of our profit and growth.” HPE’s claim to having changed is perhaps more credible on the face of it, given that its acquisition of Juniper means it has become more of a networking player. Dell hasn’t made significant additions to its hardware portfolio, but there’s a big difference in its sources of revenue, which three years ago was just about evenly split between its infrastructure and client devices. In its Tuesday announcement, Dell revealed ISG revenue grew 198 percent year over year to $42 billion, while CSG racked up three percent growth to $12.9 billion – meaning Dell is now predominantly an infrastructure company. Clarke said he’s seen some companies deferring their PC purchases to buy AI hardware instead, and said Dell is re-assigning parts it ordered to build PCs and using them for servers instead. Dell exited its Q3 with a backlog of $32 billion worth of AI servers and is clearly aware that investors might worry that’s not a useful metric because some buyers’ dreams of operating neoclouds have struck financial or regulatory barriers. Clarke assured investors that Dell is “highly selective about the partners we work with” “Every AI order is vetted for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance, and access to land and power.” HPE also has wrinkles in its AI business, because buyers won’t stand for fat margins and that’s dented the company’s profits a little. Neri was able to point to AI-related revenue also rising sharply, up 68.6 percent year over year to $11.3 billion, while overall revenue climbed 50 percent to reach $14.5 billion. Networking grew at a more relaxed 12 percent. The CEO said HPE expects better growth ahead, because new server purchases create demand for networks and storage. He also pointed to HPE having the opportunity to sell its networking kit to other OEMs who build AMD’s Helios rack-scale systems. HPE predicted its next quarter will see revenue reach $14.0 billion to $14.6 billion, up 51 to 57 percent year over year. Dell is also optimistic that AI buyers will spend on kit beyond servers and GPUs and updated its full-year revenue outlook to $202 billion, $10 billion above its previous forecasts and up 78 percent year over year. ®

item.title: Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa
item.description: A sign identifying the facility sits inside a fence surrounding the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, on November 19th. | Photo: Getty Images The US Army is moving ahead with plans to detonate the nation's stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday . The Verge reached out to experts on what to expect, and will keep this post updated. What material is the Army planning to detonate? There are 68 drums holding about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound created to detonate munitions like grenades. item.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
item.description: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks. The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history. Losing its voice The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate. Read full article Comments

item.title: SpaceX launches secretive spy satellites from California for US Space Force (video)
item.description: null SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. While details about the mission's payload weren't disclosed, it's the fifth space launch in support of U.S. national security in the last two weeks, and comes amid efforts by the Space Force to expand its communications and tracking capabilities. (Image credit: SpaceX) About two and a half minutes after liftoff, Falcon 9's first-stage booster separated from the rocket's upper stage, which continued toward low Earth orbit with the classified payload. The booster, meanwhile, began a descent toward SpaceX's Of Course I Still Love You droneship in the Pacific Ocean, where it touched down approximately eight and a half minutes after launch. Tuesday's launch marked the 29th flight for this Falcon 9 booster, B1081, which previously launched NASA 's Crew-7 astronaut mission to the International Space Station , the PACE and EarthCARE science satellites , two other classified Space Force launches (USSF-153 and USSF-481), and 16 Starlink missions. Previous classified Space Force launches have fueled speculation about the possible deployment of SpaceX's Starshield satellites, which are designed for national security applications. Starshield is an adapted spacecraft design developed from SpaceX's Starlink internet constellation that supports military operations with capabilities like Earth observation and secure communications. SpaceX has not confirmed whether USSF-266 is carrying Starshield spacecraft. USSF-266 follows three other classified Space Force missions launched by SpaceX from Vandenberg earlier this month: USSF-432 on Nov. 6, USSF-627 on Nov. 11 and USSF-317 on Nov. 20, as well as a National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) launch, NROL-136, on Nov. 22. Those missions were also launched aboard Falcon 9 rockets, also with undisclosed payloads.

item.title: Microsoft's historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”
item.description: According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters , Microsoft has declared a "Code Red" overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide. Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft's target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. "Needless to say, we aren't here yet," Henderson wrote. The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company's post-incident report , dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident. Read full article Comments

item.title: How to flip your car in GTA 6
item.description: Flipping your car in Grand Theft Auto 6 works a bit differently than it did in previous games. In Rockstar's bid for realism, the team made it so you can't flip your car while you're still in it. Instead, whichever character you're controlling will have to get out of the car and turn it over. Note that flipping only works on certain vehicles, though. You can flip cars, boats, even larger construction vehicles, but not planes.

item.title: Rayan Cherki magic denies Napoli but Manchester City’s struggles continue
item.description: For reasons best known to those eyeing the pound signs, Manchester City gave a debut to a special rust-coloured kit in front of a nonplussed crowd. It was of a piece with their performance for most of a familiarly frustrating night that at least concluded with a shot of energy, the home side belatedly shaking off their torpor and ending the prospect of a triumphant return to the Etihad for Kevin De Bruyne. Despite the relief sparked by a fine equaliser by Rayan Cherki, who was rewarded for an insistent but hitherto fruitless evening’s endeavours when his angled shot flashed past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic, it was hard to see this as anything but a perfect snapshot of their autumn difficulties. Nobody could pretend City were up against crack opposition in a one-paced Napoli, who are eighth in Serie A and lack the brio of old, but they simply cannot keep the door shut and could not have quibbled about departing with a defeat. Continue reading...

item.title: Dortmund’s Beier halts Arsenal charge after thunderbolt from Gyökeres
item.description: Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently coasting toward victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday , this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition. It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe ­Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres. But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s goal, racking up 30 shots by the final whistle. The German side had to hang on for a result that gave their travelling fans a night to remember, although Arteta admitted his players must be more clinical when Real Madrid and Jude Bellingham visit north London in a fortnight. Continue reading...

item.title: Political Signals: The Price Of Participation
item.description: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. item.dc:creator: Nosakhale Akhimien
item.content:encoded: Deadly violence in Delta sharpens the question of campaign safety, while economic policy and electoral preparations face tests. An election campaign should ask citizens for their votes. In Uduere, Delta State, families are now mourning people who went to a political gathering. Police said on Tuesday that six people died in Monday’s violence at a campaign event in Ughelli North. That preliminary figure is higher than the four deaths initially reported by Ovie Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation. The circumstances and responsibility remain under investigation. This is the most consequential political development since Friday. Its significance extends beyond one party’s campaign. Every attack raises a question for the next person considering attending a meeting, volunteering or accompanying a candidate: is participation worth the risk? When citizens begin making that calculation, electoral competition has already suffered. Delta Needs Evidence And Accountability Delta Governor Sheriff Oborevwori The NDC has alleged official complicity. The Delta State Government has rejected attempts to link Governor Sheriff Oborevwori to the violence, condemned the killings and promised that those responsible will face justice. Those competing positions must remain distinct from investigative findings. The state has imposed a daily 6 p.m. to 6 a.m. curfew across Ughelli North. Restoring calm is an immediate necessity. Establishing responsibility is the next obligation. The investigation should establish the sequence of events, identify those who used weapons and examine allegations about the conduct of officials and security personnel. Witnesses need protection, and the public needs credible updates. Political leaders also have an immediate responsibility to restrain inflammatory claims and prevent retaliation. The standard is straightforward: lawful political activity must receive protection regardless of the party organising it. A Separate Court Decision Changes The Delta Contest On Tuesday, the Federal High Court in Warri nullified Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC’s Delta Central senatorial candidate and directed INEC to remove his name. Reporting attributes the decision to failures concerning the party’s membership register and nomination requirements. Responses from Omo-Agege and the NDC were unavailable in the initial reports. The ruling and Monday’s violence are separate matters. Their proximity establishes no connection between them. Ovie Omo-Agege Electorally, however, the judgment creates fresh uncertainty around an influential politician and the organisation supporting him. Any subsequent appeal, interim order and INEC action will matter. The wider lesson reaches across party lines: recruitment and defections must be supported by lawful nomination procedures. Political prominence cannot resolve defective paperwork. Tinubu’s Lagos Outreach Meets An Economic Request President Bola Tinubu’s meeting with Igbo stakeholders in Lagos on Monday continued his effort to broaden support through community and business networks. According to the presidency, participants pledged support while Tinubu offered assurances of inclusive governance. Traders’ representative Tony Nwakeze also requested loans at five per cent interest to help businesses expand and move towards manufacturing. That was a request; the account did not announce an operational loan scheme. The economic request gives the gathering significance beyond its endorsements. Business owners want access to finance, reliable services and room to grow. Their electoral decisions may depend on whether political commitments produce practical improvements. The gathering demonstrates outreach and organised support among those present. It cannot establish the preferences of an entire ethnic community. Voters retain their individual judgments, including when community leaders endorse a candidate. The CBN Holds Its Position The Central Bank’s Monetary Policy Committee retained the benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent today. Set beside the traders’ request, the decision illustrates a central political tension: preserving economic stability while improving access to affordable finance. The policy rate and the interest charged on a particular business loan are different measures. Even so, financing costs remain part of the environment in which enterprises decide whether to invest, employ and expand. For the government, the campaign challenge is to show how stabilisation will translate into stronger livelihoods. For the opposition, promising cheaper credit requires an explanation of funding, eligibility, repayment and protection against politically connected beneficiaries. Voters deserve to see how those proposals would work. Opposition Cooperation Still Awaits Its Decision Day The opposition’s second summit remains scheduled for November 30, following its postponement from November 23. Organisers intend participating parties and candidates to endorse a framework for cooperation, democratic renewal and reform. A common presidential candidate has not been announced. The distinction matters. Atiku, Obi, Makinde, Duke, Adebayo Parties can cooperate on election monitoring, campaign freedoms and policy priorities while continuing to compete for votes. Whether they intend to go further needs an explicit answer. Monday’s summit should be assessed through its commitments: who signs, what each participant authorises and what work begins afterward. The ADC, NDC, APM, SDP, PRP and participating PDP faction also have different local interests to reconcile. A national understanding becomes useful when constituency organisations know how to act on it. Saturday Offers A Measurable Test INEC has selected 17,676 polling units, covering two units in each registration area, for its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise on Saturday, November 28. The announced operating hours are 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time. This gives parties, observers and voters an opportunity to assess performance before the general election. The useful evidence will include whether equipment works, eligible participants can be accredited, results upload correctly and failures receive a prompt, documented response. INEC should publish findings and explain the corrective work required. A test earns public value when its results can be examined. The position of the main camps is clearer in some respects, while important uncertainties remain: •APC/Tinubu: outreach continues through party, community and business networks. The challenge is converting endorsements and the government’s record into individual votes. •ADC/Atiku: the leadership appeal remains consequential. INEC’s latest reported position is that it will await the appellate decision before determining its next action; that does not establish that the ADC has won its appeal. •NDC/Obi-Kwankwaso: the Delta violence creates immediate safety concerns, while the Omo-Agege judgment introduces a separate organisational uncertainty. •APM/Makinde and other opposition partners: November 30 will test whether negotiations produce defined, implementable cooperation. State and constituency developments deserve attention because presidential campaigns depend on local organisers, candidates and polling agents. Recent local and off-cycle results can inform that assessment when turnout, competitiveness and local circumstances are considered. Election Watch assessment: campaign safety and legal uncertainty have become more consequential. The material reviewed does not support declaring a fresh national swing. Can Young People Participate Without Paying With Their Safety? The Delta deaths give this edition’s Youth Metre an immediate focus: the conditions under which people enter political life. Campaigns depend on volunteers, organisers and supporters. Those participants need protection, clear responsibilities and leaders who reject intimidation consistently

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
item.description: null On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space . (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control. The first Aerobee sounding rocket launched on Nov. 24, 1947 under a project led by the U.S. Navy. (Image credit: U.S. Navy) Why it mattered Billed as the " most successful sounding rocket of the space age ," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so. "The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview . "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds." An Aerobee suborbital sounding rocket of the type designed to study Earth's atmosphere. (Image credit: NMMSH) While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space , many more made successful launches in the decades that followed. Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight . More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have launched since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: 'Quid pro quo’: Nvidia too big to fail or ‘too close to personal interest of people around Trump’?
item.description: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Bernard Benhamou, Secretary General of the Institute of Digital Sovereignty and Senior Lecturer in Internet Governance at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University. What does Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia mean for Trump, Lutnick, the US, the AI industry and China? Describing Huang as “the global banker of the AI industry”, Benhamou explains: “He is the visionary, he is the banker. He's not only the chip maker.” He also warns of the repercussions of Donald Trump's decision to reinstate the Nvidia CEO, with congressional and judicial scrutiny looming. “It's far from over. It's just the beginning.”

item.title: Nigeria Is Cutting The Budget, But Not The Deficit
item.description: The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement. President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65.176 trillion, a cut of approximately ₦3.15 trillion, or 4.6 per cent. Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law. The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion. Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend. What Is Being Revised Under the proposed framework, projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. The administration says the revision will regularise expenditure incurred by NNPC Limited on behalf of the Federation, address debt-service obligations that were underprovided for, recognise already issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and refund ministries and special accounts. Some new allocations are also proposed for critical roads, agriculture, farm productivity, market access and water security. These may be legitimate obligations. But their late recognition exposes weaknesses in the original budget’s preparation. The Credibility Problem The 2026 budget began as an executive proposal of approximately ₦58.47 trillion. It was subsequently expanded and signed at ₦68.323 trillion in April. Seven months later, the executive is asking Parliament to reduce it. The new figure remains ₦6.7 trillion above the original proposal. This sequence matters because Nigeria’s budget has become less a binding financial plan than a collection of ambitions, negotiated additions and subsequent corrections. Ministries receive large appropriations but often wait months for releases. Projects are announced without complete financing. Unpaid obligations accumulate and eventually return as supplementary provisions. A smaller, executable budget would be preferable to a larger one that exists chiefly on paper. But credibility requires more than reducing the headline figure. Government should publish exactly which programmes are being removed, reduced, de
item.dc:creator: Nosakhale Akhimien
item.content:encoded: The economic signal this week is that the Federal Government has acknowledged that its 2026 budget is larger than it can credibly implement. President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to repeal and re-enact the 2026 Appropriation Act, reducing total expenditure from ₦68.323 trillion to ₦65.176 trillion, a cut of approximately ₦3.15 trillion, or 4.6 per cent. Budget revision is not inherently a sign of failure. Governments should adjust spending plans when revenue, financing conditions or obligations change. An unrealistic budget does not become credible merely because it has been signed into law. The more important signal is what remains unchanged: a ₦31.457 trillion fiscal deficit and planned new borrowing of ₦29.218 trillion. Nigeria is reducing expenditure, but it is not reducing the gap between what government earns and what it intends to spend. What Is Being Revised Under the proposed framework, projected federal revenue, including receipts from government-owned enterprises, stands at ₦33.720 trillion. Capital expenditure is estimated at ₦26.232 trillion, while the deficit remains equivalent to 5.64 per cent of GDP. The borrowing plan comprises ₦18.428 trillion in domestic financing and ₦10.790 trillion from external sources. The government says its proposed $7.7 billion foreign loan will fund an existing external-borrowing provision rather than increase the approved envelope. President Bola Tinubu signed into law the Appropriation (Amendment) (No.4) Bill, 2025, on September 30, 2026. The administration says the revision will regularise expenditure incurred by NNPC Limited on behalf of the Federation, address debt-service obligations that were underprovided for, recognise already issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and refund ministries and special accounts. Some new allocations are also proposed for critical roads, agriculture, farm productivity, market access and water security. These may be legitimate obligations. But their late recognition exposes weaknesses in the original budget’s preparation. The Credibility Problem The 2026 budget began as an executive proposal of approximately ₦58.47 trillion. It was subsequently expanded and signed at ₦68.323 trillion in April. Seven months later, the executive is asking Parliament to reduce it. The new figure remains ₦6.7 trillion above the original proposal. This sequence matters because Nigeria’s budget has become less a binding financial plan than a collection of ambitions, negotiated additions and subsequent corrections. Ministries receive large appropriations but often wait months for releases. Projects are announced without complete financing. Unpaid obligations accumulate and eventually return as supplementary provisions. A smaller, executable budget would be preferable to a larger one that exists chiefly on paper. But credibility requires more than reducing the headline figure. Government should publish exactly which programmes are being removed, reduced, deferred or reclassified. Without that schedule, Nigerians cannot determine who bears the adjustment. Why The Unchanged Deficit Matters A ₦31.457 trillion deficit means that projected revenue will finance only slightly more than half of the revised spending plan. The administration argues that much of the borrowing will support infrastructure and productive investment. That may be economically defensible where financing is affordable and projects generate measurable value. -A street vendor holds a basket of tomatoes at his stall in Jabi neighbourhood in Abuja, on May 20, 2025. (Photo by OLYMPIA DE MAISMONT / AFP) But borrowing also exposes the budget to interest costs, refinancing pressures and exchange-rate risk. Domestic borrowing can crowd out private-sector credit, while external debt becomes more expensive in naira terms when the currency weakens. The cut therefore raises a central question: if expenditure has been reduced to reflect available resources, why have the deficit and borrowing requirements not also fallen? The answer may lie in the incorporation of previously underfunded debt service and other obligations. If so, the government should provide a clear reconciliation. Fiscal arithmetic should not require citizens to infer what has changed. The Political Dimension The revision comes weeks before the expected presentation of the 2027 budget and less than two months before the presidential election. The government will describe the exercise as responsible adjustment evidence that it is prioritising existing commitments and improving capital budget execution. Opposition parties are likely to portray it as proof that the original budget was inflated or poorly planned. Neither political conclusion should substitute for legislative scrutiny. The National Assembly approved the expansion to ₦68.323 trillion. It should now explain the basis on which it evaluates the reduction, rather than treating the new request as an administrative formality. What To Watch Watch the detailed schedule of reductions. Are politically inserted projects being removed, or are essential capital programmes carrying the burden? Watch actual revenue collections and capital releases. Appropriation is not implementation. Finally, watch the 2027 budget. If it repeats optimistic revenue assumptions and large legislative additions, the current revision will have corrected a number without correcting the process. Bottom Line Reducing an unrealistic budget is fiscally sensible. Retaining an unchanged deficit and borrowing plan makes the adjustment less reassuring. Nigeria does not merely need a smaller budget. It needs an honest one built on credible revenue, transparent obligations and projects that can actually be completed. The true test of fiscal discipline is not how much government appropriates. It is how closely promises, resources and delivery finally align. The post Nigeria Is Cutting The Budget, But Not The Deficit appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia comeback sends AI videos into overdrive
item.description: Just 11 days after resigning as Nvidia CEO, Jensen Huang’s return has unleashed a fresh wave of AI-generated videos. But the internet has changed its tune: while last week’s memes mocked Huang, many now celebrate his comeback. One viral video purportedly showing him dancing is actually AI-manipulated footage of a basketball coach from 2016. From humiliation to hero worship, the technology Nvidia helped popularise is rewriting the narrative surrounding its own CEO, as Vedika Bahl explains.

item.title: Did Nvidia knowingly send chips to China 'cutout'? Was there ‘pay-to-play’ involving Trump, Lutnick?
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Andrew Weissmann, Professor of Practice at NYU School of Law and a former federal prosecutor known for leading major Department of Justice (DOJ) and FBI investigations. “Why were they treating Nvidia so favorably? Professor Weissmann joins us to discuss the legal and ethical questions surrounding the Trump administration's dealings with the chipmaker. He examines allegations of personal financial gain, the implications for US national security, the limits of presidential immunity and what he describes as an “unholy alliance of tech bros, of Wall Street, and of politicians."

item.title: NASA+ Content Coming to Big Screen at Greenbelt, Maryland Cinema
item.description: Credit: NASA NASA announced Monday that NASA+ content has found its first theatrical home at The Greenbelt Cinema in Greenbelt, Maryland, expanding the agency’s reach across major viewing platforms and bringing space even closer to home. “The National Aeronautics and Space Act of 1958 calls us to share our story of space exploration with the broadest possible audience, and our partners help us accomplish that,” said Rebecca Sirmons, general manager of NASA+ at the agency’s Headquarters in Washington. “Artemis II captured the imagination of the Artemis generation, but we are just getting started. With Artemis III on the horizon and our sights set on building humanity’s first Moon Base, this is only the beginning of our story being told, and we’ll continue sharing transparent, engaging content every step of the way.” NASA and The Greenbelt Cinema will kick off their partnership with screenings of the NASA+ original documentary “The Europa Concept,” which follows NASA’s journey to investigate the science driving future exploration of Europa, Jupiter’s icy moon. Dates for screenings will be announced soon on NASA.gov. Future programming may include other NASA+ original content, in-person live streaming events of NASA’s Artemis missions, including the first crewed mission to the Moon under the Artemis program, additional Europa content, and more. NASA+ also will remain available for free, with no ads, through the NASA app and on the agency’s website . Earlier this year during its Ignition event, NASA outlined a bold path forward for the agency, including increasing the cadence of Artemis missions to the lunar surface, and building the first Moon Base , among other agency priorities. Partnerships like this one help NASA maximize engagement with communities around the world by making the agency’s missions and educational content available to viewers on their preferred devices and channels. For more information about NASA missions, visit: https://www.nasa.gov Share Details Last Updated Nov 24, 2026 Related Terms NASA+

item.title: 2027: Omo-Agege Not A Threat, Can’t Get 25% Of Votes For Obi – Delta Council Chairman
item.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Council in Delta State, Jaro Egbo, has dismissed former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege as a political threat ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that the former lawmaker lacks the support to secure significant votes for the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. Egbo said Omo-Agege would struggle to deliver even 25 per cent of the votes for the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, arguing that his political influence in Delta State was exaggerated. The council chairman spoke on Tuesday as a guest on Channels Television’s ‘Politics Today’, where he was asked whether Omo-Agege’s claim that the APC could not win elections in Delta State was a source of concern, particularly given Obi’s victory in the state during the 2023 presidential election. Responding, Egbo questioned Omo-Agege’s political strength, recalling that the former deputy senate president was a member of the All Progressives Congress during the 2023 elections but could not secure 25 per cent of the votes for President Bola Tinubu in Delta State. “When Peter Obi contested and won in Delta in 2023, Omo-Agege was in APC. Omo-Agege couldn’t get 25 per cent of the vote for Mr President. If he was that popular, why was he unable to get 25 per cent for Mr President?” he asked. ﻿ Egbo, who said he belonged to the Peoples Democratic Party at the time, added that his party secured more than 25 per cent of the votes for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar. He argued that Omo-Agege’s defection to the NDC would not translate into electoral gains for Obi, insisting that the former deputy senate president lacked the political following to influence the outcome of the election. “Now that he has gone to NDC, I am sure he won’t be able to also get 25 per cent for Peter Obi. So, he’s not a threat to anybody. He knows that he’s not a threat,” he said. Egbo, who is also from Ughelli North, Omo-Agege’s hometown, urged Omo-Agege to face the electorate rather than make claims about his political strength, saying voters would determine his popularity at the polls. Egbo also called on the former deputy senate president to tone down his political rhetoric. Omo-Agege had, during an appearance on Politics Today on Monday, dismissed the APC’s chances of winning elections in Delta State in 2027, citing Obi’s popularity and the support base he claimed to command. “Peter Obi remains very popular here in Delta State. There is no chance that APC will win anything,” he said. Omo-Agege, who left the APC for the NDC in May 2026, also argued that a combination of his political support base and Obi’s popularity would make it difficult for the ruling party to win in the state. However, the Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, on Tuesday invalidated Omo-Agege’s nomination as the NDC candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District in the 2027 elections over alleged violations of the Electoral Act. item.title: Teams Lock in Mission Architecture for NASA’s SR-1 Freedom
item.description: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space. Credit: NASA/Jonathan North NASA completed a major review for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom and locked in key elements of the spacecraft, which is targeted to launch in 2028 and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space for the first time. Experts from across the agency, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and industry met at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland for a major SR-1 mission design review in October. Several key decisions were made, propelling the mission from an early concept toward a defined spacecraft design. “SR-1 marks a pivotal step in how we travel through the solar system,” said Steve Sinacore, SR-1 Freedom program director. “This mission will be the first freight run on the railroad of the solar system, and the decisions we’re making now are laying the tracks for every nuclear-powered spacecraft that follows.” Planned for launch in late 2028, SR-1 will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall , a capsule carrying three next-generation helicopters, to Mars. Once deployed, the helicopters will study Martian geology and climate history, explore new terrain, and search for signs of subsurface ice. As NASA prepares for more ambitious exploration missions, future spacecraft and surface operations will require significantly more power than current systems can provide, particularly in environments where sunlight is limited or unavailable. SR-1 will demonstrate how fission power can enable long-duration missions, pave the way for reliable surface power systems to support NASA’s future Moon Base , and enable exploration deeper into the solar system. Key design decisions The SR-1 Freedom spacecraft design has evolved since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman first introduced the concept in March at the agency’s Ignition event, where leadership shared plans to develop a fission-powered spacecraft in time for the next Mars launch window. One significant change is to use a shorter boom than the one shown in early illustrations. The boom separates the reactor from the spacecraft’s main body, known as the Power and Propulsion Element. The shorter boom will reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design. Planned for launch in late 2028, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall to Mars. This infographic explains the components of the spacecraft. Credit: NASA/David Lam NASA and DOE experts also determined that improvements in shielding and spacecraft design will allow the reactor to operate closer to the rest of the spacecraft. This will simplify integration while maintaining the radiation protection needed for spacecraft electronics and the SkyFall payload.
item.dc:creator: Heather Baeslack
item.content:encoded: 5 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space. Credit: NASA/Jonathan North NASA completed a major review for Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom and locked in key elements of the spacecraft, which is targeted to launch in 2028 and demonstrate nuclear electric propulsion in deep space for the first time. Experts from across the agency, the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), and industry met at NASA’s Glenn Research Center in Cleveland for a major SR-1 mission design review in October. Several key decisions were made, propelling the mission from an early concept toward a defined spacecraft design. “SR-1 marks a pivotal step in how we travel through the solar system,” said Steve Sinacore, SR-1 Freedom program director. “This mission will be the first freight run on the railroad of the solar system, and the decisions we’re making now are laying the tracks for every nuclear-powered spacecraft that follows.” Planned for launch in late 2028, SR-1 will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall , a capsule carrying three next-generation helicopters, to Mars. Once deployed, the helicopters will study Martian geology and climate history, explore new terrain, and search for signs of subsurface ice. As NASA prepares for more ambitious exploration missions, future spacecraft and surface operations will require significantly more power than current systems can provide, particularly in environments where sunlight is limited or unavailable. SR-1 will demonstrate how fission power can enable long-duration missions, pave the way for reliable surface power systems to support NASA’s future Moon Base , and enable exploration deeper into the solar system. Key design decisions The SR-1 Freedom spacecraft design has evolved since NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman first introduced the concept in March at the agency’s Ignition event, where leadership shared plans to develop a fission-powered spacecraft in time for the next Mars launch window. One significant change is to use a shorter boom than the one shown in early illustrations. The boom separates the reactor from the spacecraft’s main body, known as the Power and Propulsion Element. The shorter boom will reduce weight, simplify assembly, and help streamline the spacecraft’s design. Planned for launch in late 2028, Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom will use both nuclear and solar power to deliver SkyFall to Mars. This infographic explains the components of the spacecraft. Credit: NASA/David Lam NASA and DOE experts also determined that improvements in shielding and spacecraft design will allow the reactor to operate closer to the rest of the spacecraft. This will simplify integration while maintaining the radiation protection needed for spacecraft electronics and the SkyFall payload. Teams are continuing to evaluate other key design features, including the number of radiator panels on SR-1, output power levels of its nuclear power module , and how long its reactor will operate. These decisions will help shape the final spacecraft design and ensure it meets mission objectives. In addition, the team is modifying the spacecraft’s Power and Propulsion Element by updating its communications system for the journey to Mars. SR-1 Freedom will use larger X-band antenna dishes to send data across deep space back to Earth. Further maturation of the spacecraft plans will focus on reducing risk, simplifying the design, and staying on schedule. NASA awarded a $39.3 million contract to Johns Hopkins University’s Applied Physics Laboratory to develop the heat rejection system for the spacecraft’s nuclear power module. The system will remove excess heat generated by the spacecraft’s nuclear power system, allowing it to operate safely and efficiently. The lab is working with the company Advanced Cooling Technologies as a key strategic commercial partner for providing the critical heat pipe and composite radiator technologies that will enable the system to meet the demanding mission requirements. Awarded under the Aerospace Research, Development, and Engineering Support II contract, the contract action ensures the Applied Physics Laboratory team will design, build, test, and evaluate the system, along with producing the hardware needed for flight. The heat rejection system is a key part of demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in space and will help lay the groundwork and industrial production foundation for future high-power nuclear systems used in deep space exploration. Updated mission profile Along with the spacecraft design, teams have defined the mission timeline and planned operations. After launch and once the spacecraft has left Earth orbit, SR-1 Freedom will activate and gradually increase reactor power. The reactor system will operate for an initial period of time before shutting down. During this period, the spacecraft will collect and send performance data back to Earth. Solar arrays will then provide power as it cruises to Mars. NASA’s Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) Freedom, the first fission-powered spacecraft to travel beyond Earth orbit, cruises past Mars in this artist’s concept, demonstrating nuclear electric propulsion in deep space. Credit: NASA After delivering SkyFall to Martian orbit, SR-1 Freedom will restart its fission reactor, collecting additional data on the spacecraft’s performance in deep space. “By refining the design and advancing this architecture, we’re not just building a spacecraft, we’re establishing the foundation for a new era of reliable, efficient transport beyond Earth orbit,” Sinacore said. “What we learn from SR-1 Freedom will shape the future of exploration for decades to come.” With key design decisions advancing and teams across NASA, DOE, and industry working together, SR-1 Freedom is moving toward its 2028 launch goal. The mission will demonstrate new capabilities for nuclear-powered transportation and help establish the foundation for future exploration beyond Earth. To learn more about NASA’s efforts in nuclear power in space, visit: https://www.nasa.gov/space-nuclear

item.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' executive producers talk architectural easter eggs and franchise continuity for Prime Video's new sci-fi series (interview)
item.description: null Prime Video's new " Blade Runner 2099 " series arrives Nov. 25, 2026, and it flips the cyberpunk universe on its head. The new show casts replicants as the dominant species on Earth, with humans relegated to second-class citizens after a global uprising. This dreary dystopian cyberpunk realm originates from sci-fi legend Phillip K. Dick's 1968 novel, "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?," and was then so vividly brought to life in Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 adaptation, " Blade Runner ." The 2017 sequel, "Blade Runner 2049," was directed by "Arrival’s" and "Dune’s" Denis Villeneuve. Starring Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Matthew Needham, Dimitri Abold, and Lewis Gribben, " Blade Runner 2099 " hails from creator and showrunner Silka Louisa and Alcon Entertainment founders Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, who executive produce with Ridley Scott's Scott Free Productions. Here, Yeoh's dying replicant blade runner Olwen unites with Schafer’s Cora, a human masquerading as a synthetic, to hunt down a dangerous rogue replicant that holds the key to a dark secret. (Image credit: Alberto Rodriguez/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images) We spoke to Kosove and Johnson about being respectful keepers of "Blade Runner's" creative flame, the pitch that sold them, and dipping back into Dick's original novel. "When the original film came out in 1982, and even when "2049" came out about a decade ago, a lot of things that these movies envisioned seemed far, far away and hard to comprehend," Kosovo tells Space. "The creation of artificial sentient beings. Today, sitting here in November of 2026, the world is catching up quicker to the world of 'Blade Runner,' with artificial technology and concerns of how do humans use this technology for our benefit without it taking over." "Silka came in several years ago and pitched her very simple idea, which was, the next chapter of 'Blade Runner' should be what happens when the replicants overtake their creators." explains Kosovo. "We thought that idea was going to be particularly resonant. It was simple to understand so new fans could enter the world without being steeped in the first two movies. And we thought it had logical continuity to the story canon that came before it. It checked a number of key boxes for us. Even though we talked to a number of showrunners who were much more established in their careers than Silka was at that point, she won the day with the most elegant idea in our opinion." (Image credit: Prime Video) Johnson admits that Louisa's pitch approval was just the opening round of a multitude of responsible decisions to be ruminated over as the production process advanced. "Once you agree that this is the story we’re telling, then it becomes a multi-year partnership in honoring all the artists and visionaries that came before as it relates to visual design and music," he notes. item.dc:creator: Jeff Spry
item.content:encoded: null Prime Video's new " Blade Runner 2099 " series arrives Nov. 25, 2026, and it flips the cyberpunk universe on its head. The new show casts replicants as the dominant species on Earth, with humans relegated to second-class citizens after a global uprising. This dreary dystopian cyberpunk realm originates from sci-fi legend Phillip K. Dick's 1968 novel, "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?," and was then so vividly brought to life in Ridley Scott’s seminal 1982 adaptation, " Blade Runner ." The 2017 sequel, "Blade Runner 2049," was directed by "Arrival’s" and "Dune’s" Denis Villeneuve. Starring Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Matthew Needham, Dimitri Abold, and Lewis Gribben, " Blade Runner 2099 " hails from creator and showrunner Silka Louisa and Alcon Entertainment founders Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, who executive produce with Ridley Scott's Scott Free Productions. Here, Yeoh's dying replicant blade runner Olwen unites with Schafer’s Cora, a human masquerading as a synthetic, to hunt down a dangerous rogue replicant that holds the key to a dark secret. (Image credit: Alberto Rodriguez/The Hollywood Reporter via Getty Images) We spoke to Kosove and Johnson about being respectful keepers of "Blade Runner's" creative flame, the pitch that sold them, and dipping back into Dick's original novel. "When the original film came out in 1982, and even when "2049" came out about a decade ago, a lot of things that these movies envisioned seemed far, far away and hard to comprehend," Kosovo tells Space. "The creation of artificial sentient beings. Today, sitting here in November of 2026, the world is catching up quicker to the world of 'Blade Runner,' with artificial technology and concerns of how do humans use this technology for our benefit without it taking over." "Silka came in several years ago and pitched her very simple idea, which was, the next chapter of 'Blade Runner' should be what happens when the replicants overtake their creators." explains Kosovo. "We thought that idea was going to be particularly resonant. It was simple to understand so new fans could enter the world without being steeped in the first two movies. And we thought it had logical continuity to the story canon that came before it. It checked a number of key boxes for us. Even though we talked to a number of showrunners who were much more established in their careers than Silka was at that point, she won the day with the most elegant idea in our opinion." (Image credit: Prime Video) Johnson admits that Louisa's pitch approval was just the opening round of a multitude of responsible decisions to be ruminated over as the production process advanced. "Once you agree that this is the story we’re telling, then it becomes a multi-year partnership in honoring all the artists and visionaries that came before as it relates to visual design and music," he notes. "Everything needs to be of the highest quality. Even though it's a TV show we feel it has theatrical level visual effects. It’s practical and tactile and analog. There’s a lot of things that come along with how you produce the show. At its core that becomes a partnership when you decide these are the characters I’m going to spend hours with and you go down that journey." With nearly 60 years of "Blade Runner" material to play with, there’s bound to be easter eggs dropped into the tale over the course of " Blade Runner 2099's " 8-episode season. Michelle Yeoh stars as a dying replicant in "Blade Runner 2099" (Image credit: Prime Video) "You’ve got Tyrell as a critical aspect of our story, but Wallace creeps into the story as well," Kosove teases. "One of the keys things was, from an architectural standpoint, things that exist in "2049" had to exist in this. You see the Wallace spires when you see the Tyrell pyramid. You have the sea wall when they're going south with the spinner. "There’s some story easter eggs too. Silka did something really cool which has not been done in either movie. She brought in concepts that go back to Philip K. Dick's novel, "Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?" That was really interesting. We’re really excited for people to see it and see how they respond.” "Blade Runner 2099" arrives on Nov. 25, 2026 exclusively on Prime Video.

item.title: AI godfather Yann LeCun torches Anthropic CEO over AI gatekeeping
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is taking heat from AI luminary Yann LeCun, one of the founding fathers of modern machine learning, because of the Claudefather's fear-mongering around open-weights models, which also happen to compete with his products. In an X post this week, LeCun likened the Amodei's advocacy to a “new form of medieval obscurantism.” “Dario’s spiel since GPT-2 has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal, and he would stay in control,” LeCun wrote in response to a now three-year-old video posted to the platform in which Amodei warned US Congress members about the dangers of open-weights models, the use of which could not be monitored or policed. “He left OpenAI because he wasn’t going to have control. It’s like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would keep in control of the dogma.” LeCun is one of the most influential names in AI and ML. His team is credited with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the late ’80s during his time at Bell Labs. He later oversaw the development of Meta’s Llama herd of models as chief AI scientist before shifting gears away from LLMs to world model architectures like JEPA. He has also been a strong proponent of open source AI development and open models. Of the major model houses, Anthropic has taken the most hostile position against the adoption of open-weights models. Despite advocating against the unregulated diffusion of open models for years, Anthropic’s fearmonger-in-chief has maintained that the company isn’t opposed to them. “Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models,” Amodei wrote in a blog post earlier this year. The executive has instead fomented fears over their potential misuse. “Open-weights models — it does not matter whether they come from China or anywhere else — do potentially present a higher risk than closed models, because it is very difficult to apply guardrails to them or monitor their usage, and, once weights are released, they cannot be withdrawn,” the blog post read. Amodei has repeatedly hammered these talking points over the past several years, including in the Senate hearing that solicited LeCun’s post. Amodei has also called for measures, such as stricter export controls on the export of high-end accelerators to China; a crackdown on industrial-scale distillation operations, for which his company has previously accused Alibaba and other Chinese model devs; and mandating safety testing for sufficiently advanced open-weights models. In other words, Anthropic doesn’t want all freely downloadable models banned, just the ones that Amodei thinks aren’t playing fair or are powerful enough to compete with its own. LeCun isn’t the only one who has pushed back against anti-open-weights rhetoric in recent memory. Earlier this summer, a cadre of tech titans, including Meta, Microsoft, IBM, Dell, and Nvidia, wrote an open letter [ PDF ] in support of open-weights models. Open m
item.dc:creator: Tobias Mann
item.content:encoded: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is taking heat from AI luminary Yann LeCun, one of the founding fathers of modern machine learning, because of the Claudefather's fear-mongering around open-weights models, which also happen to compete with his products. In an X post this week, LeCun likened the Amodei's advocacy to a “new form of medieval obscurantism.” “Dario’s spiel since GPT-2 has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal, and he would stay in control,” LeCun wrote in response to a now three-year-old video posted to the platform in which Amodei warned US Congress members about the dangers of open-weights models, the use of which could not be monitored or policed. “He left OpenAI because he wasn’t going to have control. It’s like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would keep in control of the dogma.” LeCun is one of the most influential names in AI and ML. His team is credited with the development of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in the late ’80s during his time at Bell Labs. He later oversaw the development of Meta’s Llama herd of models as chief AI scientist before shifting gears away from LLMs to world model architectures like JEPA. He has also been a strong proponent of open source AI development and open models. Of the major model houses, Anthropic has taken the most hostile position against the adoption of open-weights models. Despite advocating against the unregulated diffusion of open models for years, Anthropic’s fearmonger-in-chief has maintained that the company isn’t opposed to them. “Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models,” Amodei wrote in a blog post earlier this year. The executive has instead fomented fears over their potential misuse. “Open-weights models — it does not matter whether they come from China or anywhere else — do potentially present a higher risk than closed models, because it is very difficult to apply guardrails to them or monitor their usage, and, once weights are released, they cannot be withdrawn,” the blog post read. Amodei has repeatedly hammered these talking points over the past several years, including in the Senate hearing that solicited LeCun’s post. Amodei has also called for measures, such as stricter export controls on the export of high-end accelerators to China; a crackdown on industrial-scale distillation operations, for which his company has previously accused Alibaba and other Chinese model devs; and mandating safety testing for sufficiently advanced open-weights models. In other words, Anthropic doesn’t want all freely downloadable models banned, just the ones that Amodei thinks aren’t playing fair or are powerful enough to compete with its own. LeCun isn’t the only one who has pushed back against anti-open-weights rhetoric in recent memory. Earlier this summer, a cadre of tech titans, including Meta, Microsoft, IBM, Dell, and Nvidia, wrote an open letter [ PDF ] in support of open-weights models. Open models “strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at the time. “The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.” As we previously reported , Nvidia’s future depends on its ability to sell to a diverse set of customers ranging from the big model houses like Anthropic and OpenAI to public clouds, neoclouds, and enterprises. And while many of these companies are perfectly happy to get their AI through Claude or ChatGPT, others, whether it be for regulatory or cost reasons, are not. Earlier this month, we reported how British neobank Revolut cut their vibe coding tab by 10x by moving its roughly 2,000 employees from Claude to Z.AI’s GLM 5.1 running on a cluster of 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs. The problem for Anthropic, and OpenAI for that matter, is the more enterprises that embrace open-weights models, the less likely they are to spring for Claude or ChatGPT. The Register reached out to Anthropic for comment, but had not heard back at the time of publication. ®

item.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
item.description: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It's too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. Tackling Riemann The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There's not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. This gives it significance for areas ranging from number theory to cryptography. As Wikipedia accurately states, "It is considered by pure mathematicians to be one of the most important problems in the field." Read full article Comments

item.title: 'We are not ShinyHunters,' says criminal hacking crew that looks and acts just like ShinyHunters
item.description: Inception, a new data theft and extortion gang that security researchers have theorized is a rebrand of the ShinyHunters group, “reject[s] this attribution” and claims it has no affiliation with any prior cybercrime enterprise. In a lengthy statement posted Tuesday and shared on X, the extortionists insist that they are a new group, with new operators, and that their alleged social engineering attacks aren’t copying anyone - but rather just abusing the weakest link in an organization’s security: “a human being holding a phone.” The rant follows a Monday report by Okta Threat Intelligence - along with social media speculation since Inception’s inception last week - that the newly emerged group is very likely ShinyHunters with a different name . Okta’s researchers based their analysis on the two groups’ shared infrastructure, plus Inception’s nearly identical tactics: voice phishing , during which the scammers trick targets into entering credentials into phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA) requests. Inception apparently took offense to this. “We would like to address this once, clearly, and only once,” the crims' statement says. “We are not ShinyHunters. We were never ShinyHunters. We are Inception.” The gang argues that its overlapping domain registrars, hosting providers, and DNS services don’t prove anything. These are commodity services, “available to anyone who can pay for them,” Inception wrote. Plus, their similar methodologies don't necessarily make Inception a reboot. “That is not theft of tradecraft,” they wrote. “It is acknowledgment of a good idea – the same way every group after LockBit used a leak site, and nobody called them LockBit.” “Inception is a new group, with new operators, our own objectives, and our own name,” the statement continues. “What we share with the past is plumbing.” To be fair, the new crime crew has every reason to distance itself from ShinyHunters. That gang’s September FBI hack - plus several earlier digital heists during which the criminals stole information belonging to millions of people, including cancer patients , university and K-12 students - put a massive target on its collective backs. And while at least three ShinyHunters suspects were arrested in September and October, there's no confirmation that authorities have dismantled the entire operation. Plus, as a ShinyHunters spokesperson told The Register in an earlier interview, they and others in the crew started off as GnosticPlayers before rebranding as ShinyHunters in 2020 - so a reboot isn’t beyond the realm of possibility. Inception, for its part, says it “will not comment further on the ghost of ShinyHunters,” and it has its own work to do. And by work, it means copying ShinyHunters' playbook, stealing corporate data, and extorting victim companies for massive sums of money.®

item.title: Gul takes pain for buoyant Galatasaray to condemn Aston Villa to Champions League loss
item.description: This was Aston Villa’s third trip to Istanbul in the calendar year but, this time, they departed with different emotions. Unlike on the banks of the Bosphorus at Besiktas Park in May, the scene of their unforgettable Europa League triumph , or at Fenerbahce in January, they came away with a bloody nose. Galatasaray’s match-winner, Deniz Gul, finished with similar, the substitute requiring a bandage after bravely taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson as the hosts rippled the net on 77 minutes. It was the game’s first effort on target, Galatasaray maintaining their commanding form on home soil to extend Villa’s winless run to six matches in all competitions. On the outside, this is a gladiatorial arena, a giant spaceship parked on Ali Sami Yen complex. But inside there is a poor pitch that began cutting up during the warm-up. John McGinn, one of four changes from Villa’s stalemate with Sunderland on Saturday, gestured towards the turf in frustration after a through ball went awry, but nobody of a Villa persuasion could blame defeat on the surface. As Unai Emery had stated, it was the same for both teams. Continue reading...
