item.title: Back-to-back measles deaths is our new reality; US tally now at 14
item.description: Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water. The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23 . Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died. Deaths and transmission On November 23, Pennsylvania's health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death , an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child . New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby . On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a child between the age of 0 and 4 . Read full article Comments

item.title: Senegal regain AFCON title on appeal at Morocco's expense
item.description: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. CAS said in a statement it had "upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF)" by a "unanimous decision". FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: The One Thing to Know About Jason and Lucia Before You Play Too Much GTA 6
item.description: Even after clearing Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s long story, I keep finding myself drawn back to Leonida. That’s thanks in large part to Jason and Lucia, a pair of charismatic protagonists that I genuinely enjoy spending time with. While you can treat them as independent characters and take them out on solo adventures, GTA 6 shines brightest when you travel around Leonida as a pair. In fact, you’re bound to miss a whole lot if you aren’t letting Jason and Lucia enjoy a date from time to time.

item.title: Amateur Astronomer? Be a Kilonova Catcher!
item.description: Explore This Section Science Citizen Science Amateur Astronomer? Be a… Overview Resources Opportunities Citizen Science Highlights About Science Activation Neutron stars are the ultra-dense, city-sized leftovers of dead stars. When they collide, they can release a brief flash of light called a kilonova . These immensely powerful events forge much of the universe’s gold, platinum and other heavy elements. Since a kilonova fades within days, astronomers have to find it fast, and no single observatory can watch the whole sky. But if you have a telescope with a camera, or access to one, you can help find and follow these cosmic fireworks as a part of NASA’s Kilonova Catcher project! Kilonova Catcher connects amateur astronomers around the world into a rapid-response network. When gravitational wave detectors or space telescopes send out an alert, volunteers point their own telescopes at the sky to help find and track the fading light. The network also follows up on gamma-ray bursts, the most powerful explosions in the universe, and catches other short-lived cosmic events whenever the opportunity arises. The Kilonova Catcher network has more than 150 registered members on several continents. Volunteers work side by side with professional astronomers and observatories. They have already contributed to more than 64 official reports shared through NASA’s General Coordinates Network, the system scientists use to share discoveries in real time. Volunteers’ observations have been credited for their contributions by being named authors in peer-reviewed scientific research papers. Kilonova Catcher volunteers also joined NASA’s lunar Impact Flash! project campaign during the Artemis II mission, recording the tiny flashes of light made when meteoroids strike the Moon. The network is getting ready to help follow up thousands of new alerts from NASA’s new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope . “Here at Kilonova Catcher, by chasing the light from gravitational-wave events, we’re seeing how a single collision reaches across the universe,” said Cristina Andrade, Kilonova Catcher head of operations at the Minnesota Institute for Astrophysics. “The observatories that make this possible will produce an unprecedented amount of data. We need more human minds, more people with their eyes on the sky and on the data, both literally and figuratively. And more importantly, we need more people to realize they are capable of great feats of science, regardless of their background.” The Kilonova Catcher project is co-led by Andrade and Principal Investigator Dr. Damien Turpin, a researcher at the French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA). Damien said, “I am inspired by the expertise and drive of our amateur astronomers. They are always digging for more information and pushing the limits of their understanding. This science could not be done without their contributions.” To register and become a Kilonova Catcher, visit https://kilonovacatcher.in2p3.fr/ or send an

The Kilonova Catcher network has more than 150 registered members on several continents. Volunteers work side by side with professional astronomers and observatories. Volunteers’ observations have been credited for their contributions by being named authors in peer-reviewed scientific research papers. The network is getting ready to help follow up thousands of new alerts from NASA’s new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope . “Here at Kilonova Catcher, by chasing the light from gravitational-wave events, we’re seeing how a single collision reaches across the universe,” said Cristina Andrade, Kilonova Catcher head of operations at the Minnesota Institute for Astrophysics. “The observatories that make this possible will produce an unprecedented amount of data. We need more human minds, more people with their eyes on the sky and on the data, both literally and figuratively. And more importantly, we need more people to realize they are capable of great feats of science, regardless of their background.” The Kilonova Catcher project is co-led by Andrade and Principal Investigator Dr. Damien Turpin, a researcher at the French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission (CEA). Damien said, “I am inspired by the expertise and drive of our amateur astronomers. They are always digging for more information and pushing the limits of their understanding. This science could not be done without their contributions.” To register and become a Kilonova Catcher, visit https://kilonovacatcher.in2p3.fr/ or send an email to kilonovacatcher@gmail.com . Anyone who has access to a telescope with a camera can take part! On Aug. 17, 2017, the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO) and the Virgo Interferometer both detected gravitational waves from the collision between two neutron stars. Within 12 hours observatories had identified the source of the event within the lenticular galaxy NGC 4993, shown in this image, which was gathered with NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope. The associated kilonova is clearly visible in the Hubble observations. This is the first time the optical counterpart of a gravitational wave event was observed. Hubble observed the kilonova gradually fading over the course of six days, as illustrated by the three time-stamped inset images made between Aug. 22 and 28. Credit: NASA and ESA. Fox (STScI) Learn More and Get Involved Kilonova Catcher Use your backyard telescope to spot the most cataclysmic collisions in our Universe! item.title: [VIDEO] NDC: Delta LG Chairman Claims Ughelli Attack Was A Reprisal
item.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Jaro Egbo, has described the violence involving former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege and his supporters as a reprisal, alleging that members of the senator’s entourage opened fire. Egbo, who Omo-Agege accused of masterminding an alleged assassination attempt against him, denied the allegation while speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday. ﻿ He alleged that the senator’s supporters fired the first shots during the senator’s campaign visit, triggering anger among residents. The chairman said he was not present at the venue and was at his office at the time of the incident. Egbo dismissed Omo-Agege’s claim that he was targeted for assassination. He, however, expressed condolences to victims on both sides, irrespective of their political affiliations. Meanwhile, the Delta State Police Command has invited the former deputy senate president and the Ughelli North Local Government Chairman and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on the NDC campaign convoy. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] NDC: Delta LG Chairman Claims Ughelli Attack Was A Reprisal appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: NASA’s Northrop Grumman CRS-25 Mission Overview
item.description: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft. The Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following arrival to the station, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 to grapple the spacecraft before ground controllers robotically install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading. NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket to deliver research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Mission 25 will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 spacecraft is named in honor of NASA astronaut James “Jim” A. Lovell Jr. Lovell flew four missions, including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and the Apollo 13 mission around the Moon. Credit: NASA NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will be on duty during the Cygnus spacecraft’s approach and rendezvous. Watkins will be at the controls of the Canadarm2 robotic arm, ready to capture Cygnus as Delaney monitors the spacecraft’s arrival. Credit: NASA Science highlights In addition to food, supplies, and equipment for the crew, Cygnus will deliver several new experiments aimed at improving drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis treatment, predicting cancer spread, advancing treatments for muscle loss, improving radiation sensing, and supporting food production for future long-duration missions. This research includes: Cardinal Muscle 2.0 Preflight image of the Biocell bioreactor system used to maintain engineered muscle tissue samples as part of the Advancing Therapeutic Treatment of Sarcopenia (Cardinal Muscle 2.0) investigation. Aboard the International Space Station, this investigation tests the effects of potential therapeutics on human muscle cell cultures. The research may help accelerate development of treatments for age-related muscle loss on Earth and support astronaut health during long-duration missions. Credit: Palo Alto Veteran’s Institute for Research Cardinal Muscle 2.0 uses the microgravity environment to explore potential treatments for muscle loss. Muscle atrophy and strength loss experienced by astronauts after spaceflight share many features with age-related muscle decline on Earth and occur more rapidly in microgravity without exercise. Researchers will use a muscle tissue model
item.dc:creator: Joseph Zakrzewski
item.content:encoded: NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission, or Northrop Grumman CRS-25, will deliver about 11,000 pounds of science and supplies to the International Space Station. The mission will be the third flight of the company’s Cygnus XL, the larger, more cargo-capable version of the company’s solar-powered spacecraft. The Cygnus XL will launch aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Following arrival to the station, astronauts aboard the space station will use the Canadarm2 to grapple the spacecraft before ground controllers robotically install it to the Unity module’s Earth-facing port for cargo unloading. NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will launch on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket to deliver research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 mission will deliver approximately 11,000 pounds of research and supplies to the International Space Station. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Mission 25 will launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. Credit: NASA NASA’s Northrop Grumman Commercial Resupply Services 25 spacecraft is named in honor of NASA astronaut James “Jim” A. Lovell Jr. Lovell flew four missions, including Gemini VII, Gemini XII, Apollo 8, and the Apollo 13 mission around the Moon. Credit: NASA NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney will be on duty during the Cygnus spacecraft’s approach and rendezvous. Watkins will be at the controls of the Canadarm2 robotic arm, ready to capture Cygnus as Delaney monitors the spacecraft’s arrival. Credit: NASA Science highlights In addition to food, supplies, and equipment for the crew, Cygnus will deliver several new experiments aimed at improving drug delivery for cancer and osteoarthritis treatment, predicting cancer spread, advancing treatments for muscle loss, improving radiation sensing, and supporting food production for future long-duration missions. This research includes: Cardinal Muscle 2.0 Preflight image of the Biocell bioreactor system used to maintain engineered muscle tissue samples as part of the Advancing Therapeutic Treatment of Sarcopenia (Cardinal Muscle 2.0) investigation. Aboard the International Space Station, this investigation tests the effects of potential therapeutics on human muscle cell cultures. The research may help accelerate development of treatments for age-related muscle loss on Earth and support astronaut health during long-duration missions. Credit: Palo Alto Veteran’s Institute for Research Cardinal Muscle 2.0 uses the microgravity environment to explore potential treatments for muscle loss. Muscle atrophy and strength loss experienced by astronauts after spaceflight share many features with age-related muscle decline on Earth and occur more rapidly in microgravity without exercise. Researchers will use a muscle tissue model to test different Food and Drug Administration-approved drugs used to treat other conditions can be repurposed to prevent or reduce muscle loss. DNA NANO B A confocal microscope image shows a human cartilage cell, with its nucleus stained in blue, following delivery of Janus Base Nanoparticles (JBNp) and the subsequent release of bioactive mRNA (pink) that was translated into function protein (green). Biomimetic Fabrication of Multi-Functional DNA-Inspired Nanomaterials via Controlled Self-assembly in Space (DNA Nano Therapeutics-Mission 2) continues prior research on in-space manufacturing of nanomaterials that mimic DNA and have applications for vaccines and regenerative medicine. Credit: University of Connecticut The DNA Nano B investigation uses microgravity to manufacture tiny, DNA-inspired particles designed to deliver medicine into dense tissues, such as cartilage and solid tumors. Microgravity may enable more uniform particle assembly, helping researchers refine production methods. The results could advance targeted treatments for cancer and osteoarthritis on Earth. ARES Preflight image of an Active Radiation Environment Sensor (ARES) unit undergoing ground testing in a thermal vacuum chamber. This investigation monitors radiation in habitable spacecraft environments and has exposure awareness and warning capabilities for Human Landing System crews. Testing aboard the International Space Station helps researchers validate the technology for future exploration missions. Credit: NASA/HHPC The Active Radiation Environment Sensor ( ARES ) will test a small radiation monitoring device to support future Artemis program and lunar missions. The system is designed to integrate with spacecraft systems and provide real-time radiation monitoring inside crew living areas. The results could inform radiation monitoring strategies and crew safety measures for future exploration missions. ENCAPSULATE-1 Preflight image of colorectal microtumors grown within Encapsulate’s biochip. The investigation, Encapsulate nVasive: Unraveling the Enigma of Metastasis – Flight 1, or Encapsulate-1, grows copies of patients’ tumor samples aboard the International Space Station to study how cancer cells move and interact in microgravity. Results may help researchers develop further testing to predict a patient’s risk of metastasis and support more personalized cancer treatments. Credit: Encapsulate Inc. Encapsulate-1 uses miniature replicas of patients’ tumors to study how cancer cells move, invade surrounding tissues, and potentially spread. Researchers aim to develop a space-based diagnostic tool that could predict cancer progression months or even years in advance, improving early detection and treatment decisions for patients on Earth. OHALO III Preflight image of Utah State University’s OHALO III module with a variety of plants growing from the Utah Re-usable Root Modules. This facility aims to validate plant water delivery, volume optimization, and advance knowledge on crop production, which could inform design decisions for future plant systems on deep space missions. Credit: NASA KSC Ohalo III is a new plant growth facility designed to help food crop production on future long-duration missions. The mostly automated system uses innovative water recovery and air exchange technologies to grow a variety of crops. This research could help lead to better food production methods to keep crew healthy and fed on future exploration missions, including those to Mars. Technology demonstration The upcoming JOINS demonstration inside the Bishop Airlock will perform autonomous robotic welding in space. JOINS will test two distinct approaches: laser beam welding and friction stir welding. Laser beam welding uses a high-precision laser to melt and fuse materials together. Friction stir welding uses a rotating tool to stir the metals together, and that friction generates enough heat to soften the materials. JOINS will perform these welding approaches on two different materials: aluminum and stainless-steel. Credit: Lockheed Martin JOining demonstrations IN-Space (JOINS) will mature technologies that allow robotic systems to join materials directly in space. In-space joining could enable large structures to be assembled and integrated after launch rather than being constrained by the size and volume of a launch vehicle. These capabilities may be needed to build and repair large infrastructure, such as structures that will to support future exploration under Moon Base . Testing technologies in space helps validate their performance in unique environmental conditions, matures their readiness for operational use, reduces technical risk, and builds confidence for future mission applications. item.title: Amazon is knocking almost $50 off six months of Apple TV
item.description: Streaming deals aren’t as plentiful as they used to be, but they’re still around if you know where to look. One that caught our eye is an offer for Apple TV for those with an Amazon account in the US. Apple’s streaming service usually costs $14.99 per month, but following this page will let you get it for $6.99 for your first six months (totaling $42 versus $90 without the deal). Amazon hasn’t shared how long this offer will be available for, so I’d strike on it sooner than later. Apple TV subscription Where to Buy: $15 $7 at Amazon (monthly for 6 months) The subscription includes exclusive access to Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches, not to mention a bunch of acclaimed shows like Severance , Silo , The Morning Show , Pachinko , Pluribus , Slow Horses , and many more. ( Yo Gabba GabbaLand is amazing for kids who enjoy music.) The service also somewhat recently added movies made outside of Apple’s studios, including classics like Arrival , Dead Poets Society , and Anchorman , to name a few. While the service is technically free of ads, Apple advertises plenty of its own original programming as skippable preroll ahead of content.

item.title: 1st-ever detection of a dying star's 'final nuclear heartbeat' challenges what we know about our sun's eventual death
item.description: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." ALMA image of IRAS 06530-0213, revealing a giant ring of molecular gas surrounding a young, hourglass-shaped nebula. (Image credit: ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO); Sahai et al. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life. item.dc:creator: Robert Lea
item.content:encoded: null As ubiquitous as the sun is to us today, our star is not eternal; one day, albeit in billions of years, it will die. While massive stars die in supernova explosions, the sun and stars of similar mass die quieter deaths. But that doesn't mean these stars completely go out with a whimper. New observations collected using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), the world's largest radio telescope comprised of 66 antennas in northern Chile, reveal that the sun's death throes may be different from what scientists had initially believed. NASA Jet Propulsion Lab (JPL) researcher Raghvendra Sahai, who led the investigation, explained the shape the ALMA observations took: "It's essentially a physical snapshot of an event that, until now, we've mostly inferred from theoretical models. We've caught, for the first time, a star's final nuclear heartbeat, frozen in gas." Sun-like stars "die" when they run out of hydrogen in their cores. This means that the fusion of hydrogen to helium ceases in the stellar core, and because this nuclear process is a star's main energy source, the star no longer has the outward push to support itself against the inward push of its own gravity. As the star's core collapses to create a stellar remnant called a white dwarf , the outer layers where hydrogen is still fusing to form helium swell out. This expansion leads to a relatively short-lived " red giant " phase. Eventually, these outer layers will cool and disperse, leaving the central white dwarf surrounded by a so-called "planetary nebula" shell of debris. During the red giant phase, as the stellar core is surrounded by shells of hydrogen and helium, these layers are occasionally rocked by flares in nuclear activity called thermal pulses. During these episodes, stellar material is flung into space. To better understand this phase in stellar evolution, the team focused ALMA on a star called IRAS 06530-0213, located around 12,000 light-years away in the constellation Monoceros. This revealed a giant ring of gas that appears to be a frozen fossil of the star's last thermonuclear flare-up. This thermonuclear fossil rings an hourglass-shaped planetary nebula in the act of forming. "Most of us think of stars as unchanging points of light, but this is a real-time snapshot of a star's death throes," Sahai said. "It's the brief, violent transition between a bloated red giant and a glowing planetary nebula, frozen mid-action." ALMA image of IRAS 06530-0213, revealing a giant ring of molecular gas surrounding a young, hourglass-shaped nebula. (Image credit: ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO); Sahai et al. (2026)) The team was able to determine that this gas shell of IRAS 06530-0213 is around half a light-year wide and was ejected into space around 6,500 years ago. It represents the first direct evidence of the last thermal pulse before this kind of star enters the final phase of its life. The team thinks that for around 2,000 years after the pulse, the star lost mass at a lower rate. This mass loss then increased sharply over the following 1,000 years. This led to the creation of a lumpy shell of gas now seen as a tangle of material filaments around the dying star. The fact that these filaments have a spiral shape could indicate that IRAS 06530-0213 has an unseen partner orbiting it, stirring the gas. Meanwhile, the hourglass-shaped nebula immediately around the star began to take shape around 700 years ago, meaning that the red giant phase for IRAS 06530-0213 only ended very recently, in cosmic terms at least. There are also unexpected elements to the ALMA observations of IRAS 06530-0213. Strange chemistry of dying star The team discovered an unexpected abundance of heavy versions, or isotopes, of elements like carbon , oxygen and nitrogen around IRAS 06530-0213. This doesn't conform to models of how stars like IRAS 06530-0213 forge elements and mix them into their surroundings, though similar signatures have been seen around odd stellar objects, with violent bursts of nuclear fusion thought to be the cause. As well as seeing something unexpected, the researchers didn't detect something they expected to observe. Dying stars like IRAS 06530-0213 have previously been known to have companions , typically sitting with them inside compact disks of dust. These disks are indirect evidence of material being dragged from the close companion star to the dying star. This is a process scientists have used to explain jet-sculpted hourglass shapes. The antennas of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), set against the splendour of the Milky Way. (Image credit: ESO/B. Tafreshi/TWAN (twanight.org)) However, ALMA failed to detect such disk around IRAS 06530. The team suggests that this could be because a disk existed, albeit briefly, during which time it powered a short burst of high-speed jets that helped sculpt the hourglass, following this the disk simply faded away. "Dying stars so often have hidden companions that reshape their ejected material into intricate, bipolar or multipolar forms instead of simple spheres," Sahai concluded. "IRAS 06530 shows that the story is more complicated than the tidy explanation we've been using." The team's research was published on Friday (Nov. 20) in The Astrophysical Journal.

item.title: Amazon drone crashes on garage after delivering shampoo, draws FAA probe
item.description: An Amazon delivery drone that clipped a fiber-optic line before crashing onto a garage roof is now the subject of an investigation by the US Federal Aviation Administration. It’s the latest delivery drone mishap caught on video as Amazon and other companies are ramping up such aerial delivery operations across the United States. The November 20 incident began with Jim Brennan and his wife, residents of Huntington Woods, Michigan, placing an order for shampoo and being surprised by a notification about the package arriving by drone within seven minutes, according to WXYZ 7 News Detroit . After the drone dropped the package into Brennan’s backyard, it lost a propeller when it caught on fiber-optic cable and floundered sideways before getting pinned between the neighbor’s garage roof and some power lines. “Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan told WXYZ 7. Read full article Comments

item.title: Amazon discovers Falcon 9 and Ariane 6 can deliver when nobody else can
item.description: A European Ariane 6 launcher propelled 36 satellites into orbit for the Amazon Leo broadband constellation Tuesday, continuing the network's build-out after 40 satellites were lost earlier this month during a failure of United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket . The launch was an important rebound for Amazon, bringing the Amazon Leo fleet to 432 satellites as the company seeks to fill the void left by the grounding of ULA's Vulcan rocket, Amazon's primary launch provider. Now, an Amazon official tells Ars it is accelerating several Falcon 9 launches the company has purchased from SpaceX, which also owns the Starlink satellite network that Amazon seeks to dethrone. The next Falcon 9 launch for Amazon Leo is now planned for December, Amazon said, moved forward from its previous launch date next year. Several more Falcon 9s are scheduled to launch Amazon Leo satellites in rapid succession after the December flight. Read full article Comments

item.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
item.description: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production , but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists. As previously reported , the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018 , OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper— identified the growing popularity of " dry hopping " (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon. Read full article Comments

item.title: Kalshi makes “difficult decision” to halt Utah trading after losing court fights
item.description: Kalshi made the “difficult decision” to pause operations in Utah after losing a court fight to block the state’s ongoing enforcement actions under Utah gambling laws, Kalshi spokesperson Jacki McGavick said Monday. It seems Kalshi’s legal troubles in Utah have become too much for the prediction market platform to gamble on continued operations there. In Utah, several lawsuits are still playing out, and Kalshi also lost a bid to persuade a federal appeals court to block those cases until the appeal is resolved. Kalshi also wasn’t saved by an emergency motion from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission—which argues that the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over prediction market trading. At this time, the federal district court has not granted that motion to block Utah’s enforcement actions, either. Read full article Comments

item.title: Arm strongarms site that hosts ad-free documentation and it may disappear
item.description: Arm is swinging the hammer at an enthusiast’s site hosting a bloat-free version of its instruction reference documentation, demanding it be taken offline after several years of availability. The demand from Arm lawyers to Jon Palmisciano concern Jon’s Arm Reference , a site that provides the same arm Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) info available on Arm’s site, but with what Palmisciano describes as “without a million popups and all of the bloat” that Arm provides on its own. According to Palmisciano, his copy of the Arm ISA was culled from machine-readable XML files and stripped of the bloat. He built his version in 2022 with new CSS on top of it, and the addition of a quick search feature that, according to his comments on Hacker News, isn’t available in the official version. “The aim has always been to make it the most comfortable and bullshit-free browsing experience for people who need these docs daily,” Palmisciano wrote in HN. Based on the responses the site seems to have plenty of fans. That doesn’t matter to Arm, though: As far as the lawyers are concerned, Palmisciano’s site is a copyright violation due to its use of Arm trademarks and inclusion of copyrighted reference material for the Armv9-A and Armv9-A architecture. Arm doesn’t care if Palmisciano’s project is well intentioned or for the benefit of the many software developers that write code for its chipsets, either: They want it offline by December 4 – 10 days from the publication of this story – or else. As for what is going to happen, it seems like Jon’s Arm Reference will likely cease to exist in a little over a week – at least in its current form. “Ideally I'd love to just get permission from Arm to keep the site up, but I'm pretty pessimistic about that,” Palmisciano told us. That said, Palmisciano has “already seen a few archives and mirrors already.” The HN thread discussing the takedown order includes links to several versions, and Palmisciano has another trick up his sleeve that he’s considering playing: Open-sourcing the software he used to build his ISA page. “I'd also consider open-sourcing my tooling so that people can (for their own private use) turn the original XML downloads from Arm into an identical site they can host locally,” Palmisciano told us. He said that he'll likely tweet about opening the tooling if he does do so. He's also considered directing the URL for Jon's Arm reference to point to the open-source tool, but Arm wants the subdomain it's hosted on removed from his site as well, so that may not happen. Arm has been in touch to defend itself as well, saying that Arm appreciates the efforts of people like Palmisciano, but that it still has to protect its brand, and documentation. "We have a responsibility to ensure Arm is the primary source of technical resources and information and to protect the Arm brand," an Arm spokesperson told us. That doesn’t matter to Arm, though: As far as the lawyers are concerned, Palmisciano’s site is a copyright violation due to its use of Arm trademarks and inclusion of copyrighted reference material for the Armv9-A and Armv9-A architecture. Arm doesn’t care if Palmisciano’s project is well intentioned or for the benefit of the many software developers that write code for its chipsets, either: They want it offline by December 4 – 10 days from the publication of this story – or else. As for what is going to happen, it seems like Jon’s Arm Reference will likely cease to exist in a little over a week – at least in its current form. “Ideally I'd love to just get permission from Arm to keep the site up, but I'm pretty pessimistic about that,” Palmisciano told us. That said, Palmisciano has “already seen a few archives and mirrors already.” The HN thread discussing the takedown order includes links to several versions, and Palmisciano has another trick up his sleeve that he’s considering playing: Open-sourcing the software he used to build his ISA page. “I'd also consider open-sourcing my tooling so that people can (for their own private use) turn the original XML downloads from Arm into an identical site they can host locally,” Palmisciano told us. He said that he'll likely tweet about opening the tooling if he does do so. He's also considered directing the URL for Jon's Arm reference to point to the open-source tool, but Arm wants the subdomain it's hosted on removed from his site as well, so that may not happen. Arm has been in touch to defend itself as well, saying that Arm appreciates the efforts of people like Palmisciano, but that it still has to protect its brand, and documentation. "We have a responsibility to ensure Arm is the primary source of technical resources and information and to protect the Arm brand," an Arm spokesperson told us. "Striking the right balance between third parties sharing helpful peer-to-peer resources while ensuring copyrighted Arm-related technical content is accurate has been critical to building the thriving ecosystem we have today." In other words, if you’re an Arm dev worried about losing a valuable resource and having to turn to a website that bombards you with junk just to look up a few simple opcodes and operands you’d better find a backup host before next month. That said, Arm is willing to work something out with Palmisciano, the company told us. "We have recently flagged our concerns with regard to the use of Arm copyright content and the Arm brand on this website and shared the Arm trademark guidelines," Arm explained. "Our hope is to open a constructive dialogue, and we've asked that the website owner reach out as we seek to resolve this." As Palmisciano posted on HN, Arm is asking for removal of its trademark and copyrighted documentation. That, Palmisciano said, "seems hard to work around while still keeping the site useful." He also followed up around 8.30 pm GMT on Tuesday to let us know that he has not yet heard directly from Arm. ®

item.title: Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli
item.description: The Delta State Police Command has invited a former deputy senate president, Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Chairman Jaro Egbo and five others for questioning over the deadly attack on a campaign convoy of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state. The police said the invitations were part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during an NDC campaign in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area, on Monday. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Police Public Relations Officer, Bright Edafe, said the invited individuals had been asked to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) at the police headquarters in Asaba on specified dates. Omo-Agege, the NDC senatorial candidate for Delta Central, is expected to appear on Thursday at 11 a.m., while Egbo has been invited for 2 p.m. on the same day. The five other invitees are Gowon Egoide, a former chairman of Uduere Quarters; Onoriode Oneya, the incumbent youth chairman of Uduere Community; Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Egoide; Erukaye Egoide, Egoide’s nephew; and Tony Gabon Mevowovo, another associate of Egoide. Photo of a Nigerian Police They are expected to appear before the police on Friday, November 27, at noon. The police said the invitations were intended to establish the individuals’ level of involvement in the incident. The development comes as Governor Sheriff Oborevwori, accompanied by the Commissioner of Police, Samuel Erale, and other heads of security agencies, visited Uduere community for an on-the-spot assessment of the attack. During the visit, the governor expressed confidence in the police command to ensure that everyone found culpable was brought to justice, irrespective of political affiliation or status. ﻿ The Commissioner of Police urged the invited individuals to honour the invitations and cooperate with investigators. He also warned that the command would not accept the presence of supporters or other persons who had not been formally invited. The police assured residents that the investigation would be thorough and impartial, adding that anyone found culpable would be brought to justice. The command also appealed to residents to remain calm and law-abiding as investigations continue. ﻿ Meanwhile, Omo-Agege and Egbo have traded conflicting accusations over who orchestrated the attack. The attack left six people dead, according to preliminary police reports, while several others sustained injuries. Omo-Agege reportedly escaped unhurt. The post Police Invite Omo-Agege, Delta Council Chairman, Five Others Over Attack In Ughelli appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
item.description: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn't enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated. As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal's total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it's only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements. Read full article Comments

item.title: CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06%
item.description: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026. The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026. In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR. It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent. The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control. ﻿ It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures. However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate. According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026. Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period. The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season. It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors. The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. Inflation Risks View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. Despite the improvement in key economic indicators, the MPC identified potential risks that could put renewed pressure on prices. These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities. The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process. item.dc:creator: Nosakhale Akhimien
item.content:encoded: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has retained its Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) at 23 per cent, despite a further decline in the country’s inflation rate to 14.06 per cent in October 2026. The decision was taken at the 308th meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), held on Monday and Tuesday, November 23 and 24, 2026. In a communiqué issued on Tuesday and signed by the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, the committee also retained the Standing Facilities Corridor at +50/-300 basis points around the MPR. It further maintained the Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR) for Deposit Money Banks at 45 per cent, Merchant Banks at 16 per cent and non-Treasury Single Account (TSA) public sector deposits at 75 per cent. The committee said the decision was informed by the need to sustain the progress made in reducing inflation and keep inflation expectations under control. ﻿ It noted that headline inflation had moderated for five consecutive months, supported by exchange rate stability and improved transmission of monetary policy measures. However, members expressed concern over prevailing economic headwinds that could slow the pace of the decline in price pressures, maintaining that the current monetary policy stance remained appropriate. According to the CBN, headline inflation declined to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September 2026. Core inflation also dropped to 10.78 per cent from 12.95 per cent, while food inflation eased to 19.13 per cent from 19.59 per cent over the same period. The committee attributed the moderation in food inflation to lower prices of processed food and farm produce following the commencement of the harvest season. It also noted that the composite Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 53.2 points in October from 53.0 points in September, indicating sustained expansion in economic activities across the industrial, agricultural and services sectors. The CBN said Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $54.02bn as of November 17, 2026, providing cover for 10.26 months of imports of goods and services. Inflation Risks View of a market area in Osun State, Nigeria. Despite the improvement in key economic indicators, the MPC identified potential risks that could put renewed pressure on prices. These include the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which could sustain elevated global energy prices, as well as increased spending associated with the end-of-year festive season and election-related activities. The committee also expressed confidence that continued exchange rate stability and improved food supply would support the disinflation process. It welcomed a Memorandum of Understanding between the CBN and the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, aimed at boosting foreign exchange inflows, supporting energy project financing and improving macroeconomic stability. According to the committee, effective implementation of the agreement would strengthen foreign exchange market liquidity, boost external reserves and improve investor confidence. The MPC also noted the resilience of the banking sector, citing adequate capital buffers and improved risk management practices. Looking ahead, the committee expressed optimism about Nigeria’s economic outlook for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027, citing improved crude oil production and sustained growth in the agricultural, industrial and services sectors. It, however, warned that disruptions to global energy supplies and adverse weather conditions remained key risks to the inflation outlook. The CBN said it would continue to monitor domestic and global economic developments to ensure that future monetary policy decisions remain data-driven and focused on maintaining price stability. The next MPC meeting is scheduled for February 22 and 23, 2027. The post CBN Retains Interest Rate At 23% As Inflation Drops To 14.06% appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Russia's war on Ukraine: 'Both sides are prepared to operate outside of the conflict zone'
item.description: Charli James is pleased to welcome Gavin Hall, Teaching Fellow in Political Science, and International Security at the University of Strathclyde. Hall examines recent Russian and Ukrainian operations beyond the main conflict zone, the conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement and the implications of diminishing direct US military support for Ukraine. “Both sides are prepared to operate beyond the main battleground and outside of the conflict zone,” he explains. Hall discusses why both sides want to negotiate from a position of strength and the conditions under which a “mutually hurting stalemate” could lead to a negotiated settlement.

item.title: Best New Nigerian Songs This Week: Rema, Wizkid, Falz, Simi & More
item.description: Falz and Simi reunite on their new single “Jaiye”, ten years after their 2016 joint EP Chemistry. Photo Credit: Falz/Instagram Your playlist called, it wants a proper refresh before the week runs away from you. Between surprise link-ups from two of Afrobeats’ biggest names, cheeky big-money banter, and easy-going tunes built for the dance floor, Nigerian artists have given us plenty to queue up right now. If you are hunting for something smooth to soundtrack your Lagos traffic commute, gearing up for a night out, or simply tired of hitting replay on the same ten tracks, here are five new Nigerian songs to listen to this week that deserve a spot in your rotation. Rema featuring Wizkid – “Feel Alright” When Rema and Wizkid finally lock into the studio together, you press play immediately. Serving as the opening track on Rema’s freshly released seven-track EP, E-Mortal Boy ( EMB )—which follows his 2024 album HEIS and 2023’s Ravage EP—”Feel Alright” brings two generations of global Afrobeats stars onto one mid-tempo groove. Rema glides across the beat in a mix of English, Pidgin, and Yoruba while pursuing a love interest, before Wizkid slides in with his laid-back cadence. The official lyric video is already out too, so you can catch every bar from start to finish. ﻿ Adekunle Gold featuring Blaqbonez – “Money in a Wheelbarrow” Did you ever picture Adekunle Gold and Blaqbonez on the same track? Adekunle Gold revealed that this single actually reunites him with an artist who dropped a diss track about him years ago—and marks their second attempt at making a song together. Arriving after Adekunle Gold’s Fuji album era and Blaqbonez’s fifth studio album, NOMADINHO: 4TH PRIME, “Money in a Wheelbarrow” turns big-money talk into a two-and-a-half-minute celebration of hard-earned wins. Adekunle Gold brings warm, melodic ease to the hook while Blaqbonez trades witty verses about stacking cash and enjoying the fruits of your grind right now. ﻿ Falz featuring Simi – “Jaiye” Ten years after their beloved 2016 joint EP, Chemistry—and following favourites like “Soldier” and their 2024 duet “Borrow Me Your Baby” from Simi’s Lost and Found album—Falz and Simi are back together on “ Jaiye “. Following Falz’s 2024 EP Before The Feast and his 2026 project Break Time, this new single leans into bright, feel-good rhythms and relatable Nigerian humour about choosing enjoyment despite the daily hustle. Falz brings his witty, conversational flow while Simi answers with silky vocals that remind you why fans never get tired of hearing them side by side. ﻿ Olamide featuring FOLA – “Jaiye” Fresh off the release of his 10-track studio album, Time and Space —which arrived on 16 November following the lead single “Burukutu”, his 2025 self-titled album Olamidé, and his 2024 EP Ikigai Vol. 1—Olamide teams up with rising star FOLA for the project’s sole guest appearance on “Jaiye”. item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: Everybody Should Be Allowed To Campaign Freely, Says Obi
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has called on the Federal Government and security agencies to ensure that all political parties and candidates are allowed to campaign freely ahead of the 2027 general elections, condemning the growing incidents of political violence across the country. Speaking to Channels Television after interacting with residents during a town hall meeting in Taraba State, the former Anambra State governor described the situation as unhealthy for Nigeria’s democracy. Obi was responding to questions about the reported attack on the campaign convoy of his party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Ovie Omo-Agege, and concerns over the safety of opposition politicians. ﻿ He said there was no justification for subjecting Nigerians to violence during political campaigns, stressing that the country should uphold peaceful democratic practices. Obi also urged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to allow a free, fair and credible electoral process, noting that the party already controls the government. Beyond politics, Obi said his town hall engagements were aimed at listening to Nigerians and understanding their challenges, including unemployment, overtaxation of small businesses, lack of access to funding, strikes in schools and inadequate primary healthcare. He described listening to citizens as an essential part of responsible and demand-driven leadership. The post [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: Everybody Should Be Allowed To Campaign Freely, Says Obi appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: An AI coding agent, a browser, and a Mac tool found a financial firm's access key in under 6 minutes
item.description: A Romanian hacker, armed with only an open source coding agent, a Chrome browser, and a Mac, tried multiple ways to break into a financial services firm, ultimately found an access key - luckily, it was a decoy - and carried out an entire (almost) attack in under six minutes. It’s a stark reminder that miscreants don’t need sophisticated malware - as in the Binance heist - or AI pen-testing tools like ARTEX to carry out intrusions into critical networks. Open source coding agents, and specifically OpenCode in this case, also work just fine. “What surprised me most was how little it took and the toolkit: a free coding agent, the curl that comes with every Mac and an ordinary Chrome, all from one laptop,” Jesta co-founder and CTO Lior Finkelshtein told The Register . “Until now I thought that we had more time until tools like OpenCode are used in offensive operations. This incident shows us that it's already in use in the field, and we will probably see more of that in the future.” Jesta is a Tel Aviv-based security startup that builds defensive tools to detect and stop autonomous AI attacks. In a report shared exclusively with The Register , Finkelshtein documented an attempted intrusion targeting a major financial services company that’s also a Jesta customer - the security shop declined to say which one. Jesta’s investigation into the incident determined that someone in Bucharest downloaded a free AI coding agent called OpenCode and pointed it at the financial services customer on November 16 at 4:24:57 a.m. ET. 'Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking' OpenCode is an open source coding agent that lets users connect to more than 200 model providers or local models, including Anthropic’s Claude models, OpenAI’s GPTs, Google’s Gemini, DeepSeek, and Z.ai’s GLM. Jesta doesn’t know which model the attacker used, as there was nothing in the traffic that named the model. OpenCode's web fetch tool, however, did name itself, so Jesta knows the attacker used this coding agent - not a scanner - to do the dirty work. “Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking,” Finkelshtein said in a Tuesday report about the agent-led attack. But, he added, nothing in the coding agent “stops you from pointing it at someone else's website either. When you do, the agent goes through the site the same way it goes through code. It reads, tries something, reads the result and tries the next thing, for as long as you let it run.” That’s what it did in this operation, which took less than six minutes and cost the human operator nothing. The first call came from a Chrome browser on a Mac, requesting the front page of one of the financial firm’s systems. The site refused it, and six seconds later, the same IPv6 address in Bucharest, on an ordinary DIGI Romania business line, tried again. It used the same Chrome version, but said it was an Android Pixel 10 phone (it wasn’t) to see if the site would let a phone in (it didn’t). After failing to gain access through the front page, the
item.dc:creator: Jessica Lyons
item.content:encoded: A Romanian hacker, armed with only an open source coding agent, a Chrome browser, and a Mac, tried multiple ways to break into a financial services firm, ultimately found an access key - luckily, it was a decoy - and carried out an entire (almost) attack in under six minutes. It’s a stark reminder that miscreants don’t need sophisticated malware - as in the Binance heist - or AI pen-testing tools like ARTEX to carry out intrusions into critical networks. Open source coding agents, and specifically OpenCode in this case, also work just fine. “What surprised me most was how little it took and the toolkit: a free coding agent, the curl that comes with every Mac and an ordinary Chrome, all from one laptop,” Jesta co-founder and CTO Lior Finkelshtein told The Register . “Until now I thought that we had more time until tools like OpenCode are used in offensive operations. This incident shows us that it's already in use in the field, and we will probably see more of that in the future.” Jesta is a Tel Aviv-based security startup that builds defensive tools to detect and stop autonomous AI attacks. In a report shared exclusively with The Register , Finkelshtein documented an attempted intrusion targeting a major financial services company that’s also a Jesta customer - the security shop declined to say which one. Jesta’s investigation into the incident determined that someone in Bucharest downloaded a free AI coding agent called OpenCode and pointed it at the financial services customer on November 16 at 4:24:57 a.m. ET. 'Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking' OpenCode is an open source coding agent that lets users connect to more than 200 model providers or local models, including Anthropic’s Claude models, OpenAI’s GPTs, Google’s Gemini, DeepSeek, and Z.ai’s GLM. Jesta doesn’t know which model the attacker used, as there was nothing in the traffic that named the model. OpenCode's web fetch tool, however, did name itself, so Jesta knows the attacker used this coding agent - not a scanner - to do the dirty work. “Nothing in OpenCode was built for hacking,” Finkelshtein said in a Tuesday report about the agent-led attack. But, he added, nothing in the coding agent “stops you from pointing it at someone else's website either. When you do, the agent goes through the site the same way it goes through code. It reads, tries something, reads the result and tries the next thing, for as long as you let it run.” That’s what it did in this operation, which took less than six minutes and cost the human operator nothing. The first call came from a Chrome browser on a Mac, requesting the front page of one of the financial firm’s systems. The site refused it, and six seconds later, the same IPv6 address in Bucharest, on an ordinary DIGI Romania business line, tried again. It used the same Chrome version, but said it was an Android Pixel 10 phone (it wasn’t) to see if the site would let a phone in (it didn’t). After failing to gain access through the front page, the agent asked the system for its API definition, which was also refused. Five seconds later, it tried a different address - this one was a decoy set up by Jesta - and it answered the agent, providing the readable file defining how the API works. The agent read the document, and 13 seconds later followed a link it contained. At 4:26:01 a.m. ET, Jesta’s defenses marked the website visitor as an AI agent, opened a case, and from here on out, everything the agent accessed was contained inside a fake environment designed to trick intruders. This included a phony key, which the attacker then used to attempt to break into the company’s systems. “It worked like a developer,” Finkelshtein said about the coding agent. “It read the API docs and did what they said. It found a key and used it. It checked whether the lock was real, then made up a key of its own and tried that. None of the threat feeds the customer has knew the address, so a blocklist would never have stopped it. The bar for doing this is now installing an app. Think about how many people can do that.” 'No blocklist would have helped' In addition to OpenCode, the attacker used only Chrome 157, both in desktop and mobile modes, and curl/8.7.1, a command-line tool that has shipped with every Mac since macOS 15. The agent passed information between the three tools. It included the planted key in a command-line request and then tested three scenarios – using the decoy key, no key, and a fabricated key – to determine whether what it found in the API documentation was legit. It also tried multiple URLs using the browser. While it ultimately identified a valid endpoint, it attempted to read from one that accepts only data submissions, so its request was blocked again. Five minutes and 44 seconds after the first request, it gave up, and the logs haven’t detected any activity from this same intruder since then. The security shop and its customer disclosed the activity to law enforcement and told us it’s “being handled.” While the attacker wasn’t able to steal anything in this attempt, security teams still need to take note, according to Finkelshtein. “No blocklist would have helped” detect the malicious traffic, he explained. “Most security tools still decide by asking whether an address is known to be bad, and for this one the answer was no. If that key had been real, it would have been in.” Instead of blocklists, Finkelshtein suggests paying attention to what the visitor does. In this case, several of its actions gave it away - including following a link that only existed inside an API doc, using a desktop browser and a fake phone, then curl, all from the same address within minutes, and trying multiple keys - including one with a made up name and then no key - within seconds. “Open source lets anyone build software without a big team,” Finkelshtein wrote in the Tuesday blog. “AI is doing the same for hacking. The skill is in the model, the model is a setting, and the person giving the instructions doesn't need to know how any of it works.” ®

item.title: Microsoft refreshes Copilot app search for users without an AI subscription
item.description: Microsoft is updating search in its Microsoft 365 Copilot app for users without a Copilot license, with a toggle to restore the classic interface. Google, meanwhile, is giving AI searches more prominence on its homepage, where the familiar Search button is absent from a newly demonstrated layout. Microsoft's change is rolling out now and will hit Deferred Release by mid-January 2027. It will impact users with a Microsoft 365 license who do not have a Copilot license and "provides modern search controls to help users find, refine, and navigate search results more easily." It's enabled by default, which is a shame since administrators would likely prefer an opt-in rather than opt-out approach, and users can switch back to the "classic search experience" via a toggle on the search results page. Microsoft has not specified how long this toggle will remain available. Its separate Copilot Search experience had a fallback toggle scheduled for removal 60 days after general availability. "With the updated search experience, users can continue to find files using keywords, use modern search controls to refine and navigate results, and search supported connected third-party content when their organization has configured connected sources," Microsoft said. The results will still only display content to which users have permission. Microsoft advises administrators to brief users and help desks on the changed interface and the option to switch back. Microsoft's search tweaks arrive as the future of the Google Search button on Google's desktop homepage looks uncertain. In a post , Google VP of Product Robby Stein described a collapsible sidebar that lists users' recent AI conversations, pushing AI deeper into the search experience. Stein called it "a much simpler way to pick up where you left off," and said it would help customers "easily find & jump back into your recent AI searches." However, something else was obvious in Stein's post: the Google Search button was not present. Stein explained in August that Google had performed a "small test on desktop to help people find new things they can do with Search." Part of that test was the removal of the Google Search button. Users can still submit queries by pressing Enter. Stein said the test would have "no impact to how the core search works." The sidebar rollout doesn't itself confirm the Search button's permanent retirement. For now, its absence from Stein's demonstration is another sign of which features Google wants users to notice. ®

item.title: Porsche 718 Boxster prototype drive: This electric roadster is real
item.description: Porsche provided flights from Albany, New York, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the 718 EV prototype. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. It wasn't until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche's upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle. That's not particularly low for a sports car, but it's practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. In these SUV-heady days, that's usually not a problem, possibly even an advantage. But, in a car like this, the closer you can get your keister to the road, the greater the sensation of speed. So, for the company's first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver. That powers a single motor spinning the rear wheels and creates a driving experience that both honors the simple joy of motoring in a mid-engined Boxster while pushing the 718 to new heights of power and performance. Read full article Comments

item.title: Webb Reveals New Details in Supernova Remnant
item.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals the hot dust that makes up Cassiopeia A. The composition of its dust provides clues to the structure of Cassiopeia A’s original star. NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Tea Temim (Columbia University), Rick Arendt (UMBC), Dan Milisavljevic (Purdue University); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI) NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope reveals the hot dust that makes up Cassiopeia A (Cas A) in this high-resolution, mid-infrared image released on Nov. 23, 2026. Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets. The Webb data supports a scenario in which the interior of the star underwent a dramatic change, possibly just hours before its demise. See what scientists have learned about Cas A from Webb’s observation. Image credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Tea Temim (Columbia University), Rick Arendt (UMBC), Dan Milisavljevic (Purdue University); Image Processing: Joseph DePasquale (STScI)

OK, I’ll admit it: I wanted to hate You Can See Everything, the A24 documentary about Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes, which finally arrived in UK cinemas last week. item.title: No more heated seat subscriptions for cars in New York from 2027
item.description: Car buyers in New York may find the cost of ownership reduces a little next year. Maybe. Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill yesterday that bans car companies and dealerships from locking up car features behind a subscription, a law that goes into effect on February 27 next year. “People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets,” the governor said. In the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact. That started to change with services like General Motors’ OnStar, which introduced telematics to the vehicle—for a monthly fee. Read full article Comments

item.title: NASA may get $2 billion boost as White House seeks to accelerate Artemis
item.description: As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress that it seeks in the near term for the federal government ( PDF ). The list of so-called "funding anomalies" is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA's Artemis program for a "higher rate of operations." The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA's Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. It comes at a time when it is increasingly clear that China's lunar ambitions are as expansive as NASA's, and there is a good chance the country reaches the Moon with astronauts before NASA can get back there. Read full article Comments

item.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
item.description: Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China's Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that's vital to the story of how our genus, Homo , took over the world. The chemical makeup of the teeth's enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we'd previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans. A handful of teeth with a lot to say Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and her colleagues analyzed proteins and chemical isotopes from the enamel of five of these teeth. Read full article Comments
